The chairperson may also temporarily revoke the right to use licences or professional certificates, temporarily suspend activities, confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations, and apply the remedial measures provided for under the cited regulation.

The Chairperson of the Provincial People’s Committee is the official who leads a provincial-level People’s Committee. Under the decree, the officeholder is authorized to apply the remedial measures specified in Clause 3 of Article 3 and to confiscate objects and vehicles used in administrative violations.

The COMPANY-LEVEL MOBILE POLICE UNIT is an unnamed company-level unit of the Mobile Police. Under Article 43, clause 2 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, its head has specified authority to impose administrative penalties, including fines of up to 15,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, and to confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations valued at no more than 30,000,000 đồng.

“Article 43” refers to provisions in two Vietnamese legal instruments. Article 43 of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerns the sanctioning authority of the People’s Public Security, specifying which officials may impose penalties. Separately, Article 43 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 sets out responsibilities of vehicle inspection facilities, vehicle owners, and vehicle operators. These are distinct provisions with the same article number, addressing different subjects.

A **POLICE POST** is a police unit whose chief or head is authorized under the decree, within the scope of assigned duties, to impose administrative penalties for specified road-traffic violations. The chief is named in Article 41 as having authority to sanction those violations and is also listed in Article 43, including Clause 3, among officials empowered to impose administrative penalties. Under Article 43, Clause 3, the chief may impose fines of up to 2,500,000 Vietnamese dong and apply specified remedial measures.
The **TEAM LEADER** is an unnamed leader of a police team referenced in Article 43. The role is listed among officials authorized to impose sanctions and apply specified remedial measures.

The BORDER-GATE POLICE STATION CHIEF is the official who heads a police station at a border gate. Under Article 43 of the decree, the chief is authorized to impose penalties and apply specified remedial measures.

The **COMMUNE-LEVEL POLICE CHIEF** is the official who heads a commune-level police force or unit. Within the functions, duties, and scope assigned to the office, the chief may impose administrative sanctions for specified violations involving road-traffic order and safety, including those covered by Article 41 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The listed sanctions include warnings and fines, and the chief may also apply authorized remedial measures.

The descriptions give different fine limits: one cites a maximum of **37,500,000 đồng**, while Article 43, Clause 3 is cited as setting a maximum of **2,500,000 đồng**. These figures should be understood as applying under different stated legal authorities or contexts; the limit applicable to a particular violation depends on the governing provision.

The chief’s stated enforcement powers also include seizing objects or vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed **5,000,000 đồng** under Article 43, Clause 3, and confiscating exhibits or vehicles where authorized under Clause 4. The office may further be empowered to revoke temporarily the right to use specified permits or professional certificates, suspend certain activities, and apply the remedial measures specified in Article 3, Clause 3.

DISTRICT-LEVEL POLICE refers to police units organized at the district level. The chief of a district-level police unit is listed among the officials authorized to impose sanctions or administrative penalties.

The EXPORT-PROCESSING-ZONE POLICE STATION CHIEF is the official who heads a police station in an export processing zone. Under Article 43 of the decree, the chief is authorized to impose penalties and apply specified remedial measures.

The PROFESSIONAL DIVISION OF THE TRAFFIC POLICE DEPARTMENT is a professional division within the Traffic Police Department. Its chief is among the officials authorized under Article 43 to impose penalties and sanctions.

The Mobile Police Battalion’s commander is listed among the officials authorized under Article 43, Clause 3, to impose specified administrative penalties, including fines, and to apply specified remedial measures.

The MOBILE POLICE BATTALION COMMANDER is an authority identified in Article 43, Clause 3, with power to impose administrative fines of up to 2,500,000 Vietnamese đồng. The commander may also seize objects and vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 5,000,000 đồng, and apply the remedial measures specified in the decree.

The Head of a Professional Division of the Traffic Police Department is an official who leads a professional division within the department. Under Article 43, the officeholder is authorized to impose administrative penalties.

Vietnam’s People’s Public Security (Công an nhân dân) is the country’s public security and law-enforcement force. It is responsible for, among other functions, driver-training and testing databases and related licensing and certification activities, including records concerning people who operate specialized vehicles within its system.

Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out the administrative-penalty authority of designated People’s Public Security personnel and units. Depending on their position and the limits specified in the decree, they may issue warnings and fines, confiscate exhibits or vehicles involved in administrative violations, suspend or revoke certain permissions, and apply remedial measures. The provisions identify authorities including officers performing official duties, commune-level police chiefs, police-station chiefs, provincial-level directors, department directors, the Mobile Police commander, and other designated officials. They include a fine limit of 500,000 đồng for specified on-duty officers and allow certain officers to confiscate exhibits or vehicles valued at no more than 15,000,000 đồng.

The force also carries out road-traffic enforcement. Traffic Police may coordinate patrol and control operations with other People’s Public Security units, which can be mobilized and equipped according to their assigned tasks. The governing law for the People’s Public Security provides a basis for additional Traffic Police duties.

The People’s Public Security of Vietnam is a law-enforcement force whose designated officials and units have enforcement and sanctioning powers under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. These powers include imposing fines and other penalties for administrative violations. The force is also referenced in connection with databases relating to vehicle inspection and driver training.

The **Head of a Provincial-Level Police Division** is an official who leads a division within a provincial-level police force. The role includes heads of the provincial divisions responsible for administrative management of social order, traffic policing, and mobile policing. The officeholder is authorized to impose penalties under Article 43.

The Traffic Police Division is a unit within provincial-level police. It may receive examination applications directly, and commune-level police forward valid applications to it. The division organizes tests on legal knowledge of road traffic order and safety. In specified cases, its head is authorized to restore driving-licence points.

The Department for Administrative Management of Social Order (Cục Cảnh sát quản lý hành chính về trật tự xã hội) is identified in Article 43 as an authority with powers to impose administrative sanctions. Those powers include officials such as the department’s director and chiefs of its professional or specialist divisions. Under Article 43, Clause 6, the director is also authorized to confiscate objects and vehicles used in administrative violations.

The PROVINCIAL TRAFFIC POLICE DIVISION is a provincial-level police division responsible for traffic policing. Its head is among the officials granted powers under Article 43 and is included among the listed sanctioning authorities.

The DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE POLICE FOR SOCIAL ORDER is part of the People’s Public Security and is responsible for administrative policing and maintaining social order. Its director, as well as the heads of its professional divisions, is authorized to impose administrative penalties under Article 43.

Article 43 of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP sets out the authority of the People’s Public Security to impose administrative penalties and identifies the officials whose positions confer that authority.

The Director of Provincial-Level Police is the official who leads a provincial-level police authority or unit. Under the cited provisions of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, the director is authorized to impose administrative sanctions, including fines of up to 75,000,000 Vietnamese dong, and to apply specified remedial measures.

The **HEAD OF THE TRAFFIC POLICE DIVISION** is the official who leads the provincial-level Traffic Police Division and oversees the organization of road-traffic legal-knowledge tests. The official is authorized under Article 43 to impose penalties and, in cases covered by Clause 3 of Article 51, to restore driving-licence points.

Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, titled “Authority to impose penalties of the People’s Public Security,” sets out the administrative-penalty powers of specified People’s Public Security officials. Clause 4 identifies officials authorized to confiscate evidence and vehicles used in administrative violations, subject to a value limit of 30,000,000 đồng. Clause 5 addresses the powers of certain division heads within the Traffic Police Department.

**PROVINCIAL-LEVEL POLICE** are units of Vietnam’s People’s Public Security operating at the provincial level. Under the cited provisions, their directors are authorized to impose administrative sanctions and specified remedial measures, and may confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations. The heads of certain provincial police divisions—including administrative-management, traffic, and mobile police divisions—are also identified as having penalty-imposing authority.

The descriptions cite fine ceilings of both 37,500,000 and 75,000,000 Vietnamese dong. As they may refer to different provisions or versions of the rules, the applicable ceiling depends on the cited legal authority.

**CONFISCATION OF EVIDENCE AND VEHICLES** is an administrative enforcement action involving the confiscation of evidence or vehicles used in, or otherwise involved in, an administrative violation. The descriptions give conflicting value limits—30,000,000 đồng and 45,000,000 VND—so the applicable ceiling cannot be determined from the information provided.
The Chief of District-Level Police is the official who heads a district-level police unit. Article 43(4) lists the chief as having authority to impose administrative sanctions.

CÔNG AN NHÂN DÂN, or Vietnam’s People’s Public Security, is the country’s national public security force. Its officials’ authority to impose administrative sanctions is addressed in Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Under clause 3, certain officials may impose fines of up to 22,500,000 đồng.

The Department of Administrative Management of Social Order is a department of the People’s Public Security responsible for administrative management of social order. Under Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, its director is authorized to impose specified administrative sanctions, confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations, and apply specified remedial measures. Under Article 43, clause 6, the director may also temporarily revoke permits or professional certificates and temporarily suspend operations. The department’s professional-division heads are also among the officials authorized to impose administrative sanctions.

The **Head of the Provincial Traffic Police Division** is the official who leads the province-level traffic police division and is listed as having sanctioning authority. When the provincial-level People’s Committee chairperson issues an administrative penalty decision, the Head is responsible for entering the related driving-licence point-deduction data into the relevant database.

CÔNG AN CẤP TỈNH (provincial-level police) operates within the People’s Public Security system. Its director is authorized to confiscate exhibits and vehicles used in administrative violations and to apply specified remedial measures.

The **Police Department for Administrative Management of Social Order** is a department of the People’s Public Security. Under the applicable decree, its director is authorized to apply specified remedial measures and, under Article 43, Clause 6, to impose fines of up to 75,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.

The DIRECTOR OF THE DEPARTMENT FOR ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER is the official who leads the Department and is authorized under Article 43 to impose sanctions for administrative violations. Under Article 43, Clause 6, the Director may also confiscate objects and vehicles used in such violations.

The **SPECIALIZED INSPECTORATE** is the inspection authority whose administrative sanctioning powers are addressed in Article 44 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The article authorizes specialized inspectors and other assigned personnel, while performing their official duties, to impose administrative penalties and apply specified remedial measures. Clause 2 specifically grants the Chief Inspector of the Department of Transport the power to confiscate items or means in connection with those powers.

The Traffic Police Department (Cục Cảnh sát giao thông) is a department of Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security and a channel through which implementation issues are reported to the Ministry. It receives applications and supporting dossiers for specified vehicle-entry and traffic activities, including applications to allow right-hand-drive cars to operate in Vietnam for non-tourism purposes and applications from Vietnamese international travel service businesses seeking approval to organize foreign vehicles’ entry into Vietnam. For valid, complete applications under the relevant procedure, the Department reviews the dossier and issues written approval or refusal within five working days. It sends decisions to applicants directly, online, or by post, and distributes approvals to relevant authorities for coordination.

The Department also receives examination applications directly, checks their validity, and can provide an expected examination time and place. It organizes training and issues examiner cards for legal-knowledge tests on road traffic order and safety. Its director is responsible for research and the development, administration, maintenance, and upgrading of examination software; for managing the related administrative-violation database; and for directing, monitoring, guiding, inspecting, and urging implementation of specified Ministry circulars. Test computers connect over the Ministry’s WAN to a server hosted by the Department, which supports the testing system and stores connection and data-editing logs.

The Department issues, reissues, and revokes permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles registered with it for eligible central-level ministries, sectors, and agencies, except military vehicles on urgent missions. It also issues operating permits for intelligent transport vehicles, except those serving national defense purposes.

Under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, the Department’s director and heads of its professional divisions have specified administrative-sanctioning authority. The director’s powers include imposing fines of up to 75 million Vietnamese đồng, applying designated temporary sanctions and remedial measures, confiscating objects and vehicles involved in violations, temporarily revoking permits or professional certificates, suspending operations, and restoring driving-licence points in specified cases. The Department’s website is used to publish or update information about vehicles involved in violations and driving licences whose points have been deducted or restored.

The Director of the Department of Administrative Management of Social Order is the official heading that department. Under Article 43, Clauses 6 and 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the Director is authorized to apply specified remedial measures and to confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations. The Director may also revoke licenses or professional certificates for a fixed period or temporarily suspend activities.

**Persons Assigned to Specialized Inspection Duties** are individuals assigned to conduct specialized inspections. While performing their official duties, they are authorized to impose sanctions and apply the specified remedial measures.

The Commander of the Mobile Police is an official authorized under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP to impose administrative penalties and apply specified remedial measures. The Commander may confiscate exhibits and vehicles used in administrative violations and may revoke licenses or professional certificates for a fixed period or temporarily suspend activities, as provided by the Decree.

The **Provincial-Level Police Director** is the office-holder who leads a provincial-level police force and exercises administrative sanctioning powers under Article 43. These powers include issuing warnings, imposing fines, revoking permits or professional practice certificates for a specified period, suspending specified activities for a specified period, confiscating exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations, and applying remedial measures.

The descriptions give fine ceilings of 37,500,000 đồng and 75,000,000 đồng. These can be reconciled as the individual and doubled organizational limits, respectively, where the applicable rules provide for higher fines against organizations. The precise sanctions depend on the violation and the relevant provision.

CONFISCATION OF OBJECTS AND VEHICLES is an administrative sanction authorized by Article 44. It involves seizing objects and vehicles used in or connected with an administrative violation, provided their value does not exceed 1,000,000 đồng.
A **centrally governed city** is governed directly by the central government. Its Chief Inspector is also covered by the authority described in the text.

The Chief Inspector of the Department of Transport is the official who heads the Department of Transport Inspectorate and is authorized to impose administrative penalties. The officeholder may revoke the right to use permits or professional certificates, or suspend operations, for a fixed period; confiscate exhibits and vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 75,000,000 Vietnamese đồng; and apply the remedial measures specified in Clause 3, Article 3 of the relevant decree.

The **Director of the Traffic Police Department** is the office-holder heading the department; the role is identified by title, not by personal name. The Director is responsible for directing, monitoring, inspecting, and urging implementation of the relevant circular, and for ensuring consistent guidance at locations where legal-knowledge examinations are held. The position also covers organizing research and the application of science and technology, and managing examinations on legal knowledge concerning road traffic order and safety.

Under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the Director is authorized to impose administrative sanctions and to apply specified remedial measures. The listed powers include confiscating exhibits, objects, and vehicles used in administrative violations, and revoking licences or professional certificates for a fixed period or temporarily suspending activities. The descriptions cite different clauses of Article 43 for some of these powers; taken together, they identify the Director as holding the stated enforcement authorities.

The Director also manages and operates the database on administrative violations involving road traffic order and safety, and is authorized to restore driving-licence points in cases covered by Clause 3 of Article 51, including through automatic restoration where applicable.

THANH TRA SỞ GIAO THÔNG VẬN TẢI (the Inspectorate of the Department of Transport) is the department-level body responsible for inspection and oversight within its area of management. In some cases, the Inspectorate may not have been established. Where it exists, officials performing their duties are authorized to prepare records of violations falling within its management remit.

The **DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT INSPECTORATE** is the inspectorate associated with or operating within a Department of Transport. The cited provisions address situations in which the inspectorate has not been established, including this as a condition relevant to the Chief Inspector’s authority. That authority includes imposing specialized inspection sanctions: the Chief Inspector may revoke, for a fixed period, the right to use permits or professional certificates, or suspend operations for a fixed period.
Sở Giao thông vận tải (the Department of Transport) is the parent department of the Inspectorate mentioned in the text. The provision refers to the establishment of that Inspectorate as a condition.

The Department of Transport is a provincial or municipal government department whose inspectorate may be established depending on the circumstances described in the applicable provision. Where the inspectorate exists, it is referred to as the Department of Transport Inspectorate. The department’s Chief Inspector is authorized under the cited provisions to enforce administrative-violation rules, including imposing fines of up to 37,500,000 đồng and confiscating exhibits and vehicles used in violations, subject to the applicable value limit.
A province is a provincial-level administrative area and a jurisdiction whose Chief Inspector is mentioned in the text. The reference may be to the Chief Inspector of a province in general.

**CONFISCATION OF EXHIBITS AND VEHICLES** is an administrative penalty involving the confiscation of exhibits and vehicles used in an administrative violation. It is authorized for specified transport-sector officials under Article 44, Clause 4 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. The descriptions give two value limits—75,000,000 and 105,000,000 Vietnamese đồng—but do not explain how they differ. The applicable limit therefore depends on the relevant provision or official’s authority.

The Director General of the Vietnam Road Administration is the official who heads the Administration. Under Article 44, the Director General has authority to impose specified administrative penalties and may establish an inspection team or delegation. The head of that team or delegation is also authorized to impose penalties.

The Chief Inspector of the Ministry of Transport is the official who heads the Ministry’s inspectorate. Under Article 44, Clause 4, the Chief Inspector is authorized to impose penalties and apply the remedial measures specified in Article 3, Clause 3.

Article 44 is identified primarily as a provision of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP on administrative sanctioning authority. It concerns the authority of specialized inspectors, provincial or centrally governed city Chief Inspectors, other designated officials, and heads of inspection delegations to impose administrative penalties.

One description instead associates Article 44 with Law 36/2024/QH15 and road traffic order and safety for road transport vehicles in urban areas. This conflicts with the repeated descriptions linking Article 44 to Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, so that reference may reflect a source or numbering discrepancy.

The Director of the Vietnam Register is the official who heads the Vietnam Register. Under Article 44, Clause 4, the Director is authorized to exercise the specified sanctioning powers and apply the remedial measures set out in Article 3, Clause 3.

VIETNAM REGISTER is a Vietnamese government agency responsible for vehicle registration and inspection. Under Article 44, including Clause 4, its Director General is authorized to impose administrative penalties, including fines of up to 75,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, and to confiscate exhibits and vehicles used in administrative violations.

**APPLICATION OF REMEDIAL MEASURES** is the process of applying measures to remedy the consequences of administrative violations involving road traffic order and safety. The measures are those specified in Article 3, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. Article 44, Clause 4 authorizes their application, while Article 45 addresses the relevant authority and process. The named police department directors and the Mobile Police commander are empowered to undertake the measures.

The **Law on Handling of Administrative Violations** is a Vietnamese law governing the handling of administrative violations. It provides legal grounds for using database information to determine violations and for temporarily seizing items or documents before an administrative penalty decision, as cited under Article 125. Its principles are also referenced by Article 45 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, with Article 52 identified as the relevant provision.

SPECIALIZED INSPECTORS conduct specialized inspection duties while performing their official functions. Under Article 44, clause 1, they are authorized to impose sanctions, including fines of up to 500,000 Vietnamese đồng.

The Vietnam Road Administration (Cục Đường bộ Việt Nam) is Vietnam’s national government body responsible for road administration. Under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, its Director General has authority to impose specified administrative penalties, including fines of up to 75,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, and to confiscate exhibits or vehicles used in violations and apply specified remedial measures. The Director General may also establish inspection teams or delegations, whose heads may have sanctioning authority.

The decree also grants penalty-imposing authority to directors of subordinate Road Management Areas, including regional road management areas. Separately, the Vietnam Road Administration is identified as a competent authority for deciding on the placement of speed signs on specified roads within the Ministry of Transport’s management scope, and as an agency with which journey-monitoring data is connected and shared.

VIOLATORS are people who commit violations covered by Article 47, including people who obstruct or resist inspections or fail to comply with inspection and control requests made by persons performing official duties. When one violator’s conduct is covered by different articles in Chapter II, penalties are applied according to the rules stated there.

“Article 45” refers to provisions in two different Vietnamese legal instruments:

- **Article 45 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15** concerns road traffic order and safety requirements for automobiles transporting passengers. It requires passenger transport to follow the registered schedule and route, except in cases of force majeure. It also prohibits carrying hazardous or prohibited goods, smuggled goods, wild animals, foul-smelling goods, or other goods or animals that could affect passengers’ health or the environment. Drivers and onboard service personnel are responsible for guiding, requiring, and checking that people in the vehicle comply with Clause 2 of Article 10.

- **Article 45 of Decree No. 168/2024/ND-CP** sets out principles for determining the authority to impose administrative sanctions and apply remedial measures.

Article 46 is referenced in connection with two Vietnamese legal instruments. In Law No. 36/2024/QH15, it concerns road traffic order and safety requirements for cars transporting preschool children and students. Separately, Article 46 of Decree No. 168/2024/ND-CP is described as addressing who is authorized to prepare records of administrative violations related to road traffic order and safety. These references concern different provisions in different instruments.
Chapter II of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP contains provisions on road-traffic violations cited in Article 47(3). Those provisions are compared under that clause and may apply when violations overlap.

The **ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATION RECORD** is the official document prepared by a competent person to record a vehicle owner’s administrative violation. It may state the deadline by which the violator must resolve the case. If the vehicle owner is absent, the driver signs the record as a witness.

The Director of the Vietnam Road Administration is the official who heads the agency and is granted administrative sanctioning authority under Article 44. The Director may impose penalties and apply the remedial measures specified by the relevant provisions. The Director is also authorized to establish an inspection team or delegation. The head of such a team may have separate sanctioning powers under Article 44, including authority to impose fines of up to 60,000,000 đồng and, where specified, apply remedial measures.

Article 47 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP establishes procedures and principles for penalizing vehicle owners and drivers who violate road-traffic order and safety regulations. It addresses how authorities should handle cases in which the same person’s conduct falls under multiple provisions, including overlapping violations. It also covers violations detected using professional technical equipment when authorities cannot stop the vehicle immediately.

TRANSPORT BUSINESS UNITS are organizations engaged in transport businesses. Their details and vehicle badge information are recorded in the road traffic order and safety database. They are subject to the relevant legal provisions when violations occur and are responsible for implementing the requirements set out in Article 64 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

**DRIVER-IMAGE RECORDING DEVICE VIOLATIONS** are breaches of the rules governing the installation and use of devices that record images of vehicle drivers, as addressed in Article 29 and corresponding provisions of Article 32. They include operating a commercial transport vehicle, tractor unit, or internal transport vehicle without a required device; participating in traffic with a device that is not functioning; and falsifying the device’s recorded data.
**EXCEEDING VEHICLE OR ROAD LOAD LIMITS** refers to a violation of applicable regulations or limits on a vehicle’s load capacity or the load permitted on a road.

“Article 47” refers to provisions in two different Vietnamese legal instruments, so its meaning depends on the instrument cited.

Article 47 of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out procedures and principles for sanctioning vehicle owners and drivers or operators for road-traffic violations. It addresses how to handle a violation covered by multiple provisions, including when the same person committed it or the vehicle owner was also the direct operator. Its provisions also cover specified violations involving road use, environmental requirements, passenger capacity, vehicle loads and dimensions, and securing cargo.

Article 47 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 concerns road-traffic order and safety when motorcycles, mopeds, motorbikes, and rudimentary vehicles are used to transport passengers or goods. Among its requirements, cargo extending beyond a vehicle must be marked in red at the front and rear during daylight; in darkness, lights or other signals must be used.

Chapter II of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP contains provisions on traffic violations, including Articles 20 and 26. Its provisions are among those compared in Article 47, including the provisions cited in Clause 3 of that article.
PENALTY PRINCIPLES are the rules governing the imposition of penalties on vehicle owners, drivers, and operators for specified road traffic violations.
UNAUTHORIZED ROADWAY OR SIDEWALK USE is a violation involving use of a roadway or sidewalk for a purpose not permitted by applicable regulations.

Functional authorities are the relevant public authorities or enforcement personnel responsible for addressing road and traffic matters. Traffic police notify them of deficiencies in road and traffic organization and may recommend corrective measures. When a violation is discovered, functional authorities may also instruct how vehicles, machinery, equipment, signs, or advertisements must be removed.

The **Administrative Penalty Procedure** sets out the principles and process for imposing administrative penalties on vehicle owners and operators who commit specified violations of road traffic rules.
**EXCEEDING PERMITTED PASSENGER CAPACITY** is a violation that occurs when a vehicle carries or transports more people than it is permitted or authorized to carry.

The **Ministry of Transport of Vietnam (Bộ Giao thông vận tải, abbreviated BGTVT)** is the government body responsible for transport and for a broad range of road-traffic functions. Under Law No. 36/2024/QH15 and related regulations, it manages driver training, testing, and licensing; vehicle technical safety and environmental protection; and the national highway system and other roads within its remit.

The Ministry and its Minister are authorized or assigned to issue detailed rules and national technical regulations on road use and vehicle operation. These include vehicle size, weight, and load limits; oversized and overweight cargo and the permits required to transport it; road use by tracked vehicles; vehicle speed and safe distances; operational speed-limit signs; and the safe arrangement and fastening of goods transported by car. The Minister also prescribes rules for road signals, excluding commands from traffic controllers, and requirements concerning clean-energy and environmentally friendly vehicles.

The Ministry’s regulatory responsibilities cover vehicle inspection and emissions-testing facilities, inspection procedures and exemptions, emissions testing for motorcycles and mopeds, and certification of modified vehicles and intelligent transport vehicles. It sets requirements for vehicle technical safety and environmental protection, including national technical regulations for vehicles in road traffic. It also establishes driver-education programs, forms and content for training and tests, safe-driving training periods, motorcycle training-establishment standards, licensing procedures and forms, and requirements for international driving licenses. Its remit includes theoretical examination questions, examiner qualifications and training, examiner-card procedures, motorcycle test-ground standards, and technical regulations for road-vehicle testing centers. The Ministry’s regulations also govern the certification and standards referenced for vehicle inspection, emissions testing, and vehicles participating in road traffic.

The Ministry builds and manages specialized databases, including those for vehicle inspections, driver training and licensing, and vehicle operators, subject to specified exclusions. Its databases connect with the road traffic order and safety database to support information sharing on compulsory motor-vehicle insurance, accidents, administrative penalties, vehicle registration, and inspection.

In matters involving foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam, the Ministry serves as a coordinating agency for organizing and managing relevant activities. Together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, it coordinates with other agencies and foreign representative bodies; its relevant units receive copies of approval documents. It is also notified of approvals so it can coordinate management. The Ministry of Public Security must notify it of specified legal violations, traffic accidents, or incidents involving foreign drivers or vehicles.

The Ministry’s Chief Inspector is authorized under cited provisions to impose administrative fines of up to **75,000,000 Vietnamese đồng** and to confiscate exhibits and vehicles used in administrative violations. The abbreviation **BGTVT** appears in citations to Ministry-issued regulations, including Circular No. 38/2024/TT-BGTVT, which addresses operational speed-limit signs and safe distances, as well as Circulars No. 31/2019/TT-BGTVT and No. 06/2023/TT-BGTVT.
An **ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION VIOLATION** is a violation of regulations concerning environmental protection, including violations covered by the cited road-traffic penalty provisions.

**PENALTY PROCEDURE** refers to the procedure for imposing penalties on vehicle owners, drivers, and operators for violations of road traffic order and safety regulations. The procedure for relevant traffic violations is addressed in Article 47 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.

The MOBILE TRAFFIC APPLICATION is a mobile application for citizens, developed, managed, and operated by the Ministry of Public Security. Subject to the required infrastructure, technical, and information conditions, it enables citizens to receive electronic notices, including notifications about points deducted from their driver’s licenses.

VEHICLE OWNERSHIP CHANGE refers to a change in ownership of a motor vehicle or specialized motorcycle. Registration procedures may be required, and issuing a new registration certificate is subject to specified requirements.
CARGO-SECURING VIOLATIONS are breaches of regulations governing the securement of transported goods, as referenced in Article 12.
VEHICLE OR ROAD LOAD-LIMIT VIOLATIONS are violations of regulations governing vehicle load limits and vehicle or road dimensional limits.

The Ministry of Transport of Vietnam, abbreviated BGTVT, is the Vietnamese government ministry identified by the issuing-authority code in Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT. The circular is associated with transport and road-safety regulations, including maximum and operating speeds for vehicles, speed rules on expressways, the placement of operating-speed signs, minimum safe distances between vehicles in specified conditions, and Article 5 on road design speed. The ministry’s chief inspector is also named among officials with authority under a related decree.

A **VIOLATOR** is a person alleged or identified as having committed an administrative violation. This may include a road user who refuses an inspection or control request, or obstructs or resists someone performing official duties. The violator may be required to resolve the case, comply with a penalty or sanction decision, and provide required documents or information within the appointed period. If the violator is identified, the driving-license issuing agency may be notified.

A PENALTY DECISION is a decision imposing an administrative penalty for a violation. The violator must comply with the decision by the specified deadline. It may be issued after a vehicle and related documents have been temporarily seized.

**CLAUSE 8** is described in two different article contexts. In Article 47, it addresses traffic violations detected by technical equipment when authorities cannot stop the vehicle immediately. The vehicle owner must cooperate in identifying the driver and may face penalties for failing to do so. In Article 57, it sets requirements for holders of international driving permits who drive in Vietnam: they must carry a valid national driving licence for the appropriate vehicle class and comply with Vietnamese road traffic laws.
A TRAFFIC VIOLATOR is a person who commits a road-traffic violation and is required to resolve the resulting case or comply with the applicable penalty decision.

The VEHICLE INSPECTION AUTHORITY is responsible for conducting vehicle inspections. Before carrying out an inspection, it must check the relevant vehicle-violation and violator data. After a violation case is resolved, the competent sanctioning official notifies the authority.

DATA CONNECTION AND SHARING refers to the electronic connection and exchange of information between relevant authorities and agencies. This enables an official to notify the appropriate agencies, but depends on the necessary infrastructure, technical capabilities, and information conditions being in place. The connection and sharing arrangements may not yet be established.

The Government of Vietnam is the national authority responsible for unified state management of road traffic order and safety. The Ministry of Public Security assists the Government as the focal agency, reports to it, and submits proposals. The Government’s subordinate agencies implement the relevant laws and decrees, and it may negotiate and sign international treaties and agreements concerning road traffic order and safety.

The Government is tasked with issuing detailed regulations across a wide range of related matters. These include the management, collection, use, connection, and sharing of information and data from vehicles, technical equipment, and road-traffic databases; the use of technical equipment to detect administrative violations; and product and goods recalls. It also regulates road-safety measures and the operation of inspection facilities.

In the licensing and operation of vehicles and drivers, the Government sets rules for vehicle license-plate auctions; the management and use of signaling devices on priority vehicles and the issuance, renewal, and revocation of permits for them; driver training and licensing; driver testing-center conditions and driving-test permits; motorcycle driving-test practice grounds; and the deduction and restoration of driving-licence points, including the implementation roadmap. It also specifies requirements for rudimentary vehicles and their operating conditions, and regulations on motor-vehicle service life.

The Government further provides detailed rules for road-traffic procedures and authorities, including those concerning the transport of goods within the scope of a smart border gate. These responsibilities are established or referenced under relevant provisions of Law 36/2024/QH15 and other applicable regulations.

ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATION CASE RESOLUTION is the process of resolving an administrative violation case concerning road traffic order and safety in accordance with applicable rules and the requirements of a competent state agency. Resolution must occur by the deadline specified in the violation record or in a notice issued by an authorized person.

Vehicle registration is the process by which a vehicle is recorded with the relevant regulatory authority and its license plate is associated with it in the vehicle registration and management system. It includes the registration of motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles recorded in a specialized database managed by the Ministry of Public Security; military vehicles are excluded.

Registration may also involve a license plate won at auction. The winning bidder generally must complete the procedure to attach the plate to a vehicle within 12 months of receiving confirmation. A vehicle fitted with an auction-winning plate may also be registered following a transfer, exchange, gift, or inheritance, with the plate recorded in the registration and management system as required by law.

A vehicle identified through a relevant data lookup as involved in a road traffic violation may not be registered until the associated administrative violation matter has been completed and the relevant authority notified. Once the violation is resolved, registration may proceed under the applicable rules. Vehicle registration also serves as a means of verifying vehicle information and detecting violations. In this context, vehicle control software or engines must not be altered to manipulate inspection results.

**Temporary Seizure of Vehicles and Related Documents** is a preventive administrative measure provided for in Article 48 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Under specified legal conditions, an authorized person may temporarily seize a vehicle and documents related to the driver or vehicle before issuing a penalty decision. The measure is intended to immediately prevent an administrative violation and applies to specified violations.

The **MINISTRY OF PUBLIC SECURITY PUBLIC SERVICE PORTAL** is an online channel for submitting notices, applications, examination applications, and examination registration dossiers. It may be used by Vietnamese international travel service enterprises to submit application dossiers to the Traffic Police Department. The portal also provides an electronic channel for accessing shared information from the road traffic order and safety database, and for sending administrative-violation decisions and related documents to users’ registered accounts.

**VEHICLE INSPECTION** is the process of examining a motor vehicle for technical safety and environmental protection. Depending on the applicable rules, the driver or vehicle operator may be required to present specified documents, including a driving licence, vehicle registration, and technical inspection documents. These may be provided on paper or through an electronic identification account.

A vehicle inspection may be subject to administrative procedures when the vehicle is connected to a road-traffic violation. If a violation is identified in the relevant data lookup, inspection processing may be withheld until the required administrative matter is completed; inspection may then proceed under the applicable rules after the violation is resolved and the relevant authority is notified. The law may also specify circumstances in which a vehicle holding the required certificate is exempt from inspection during a transfer.

Inspection of motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles within the People’s Public Security is also identified as a subject covered by a specialized database managed by the Ministry of Public Security.

The TRAFFIC APPLICATION is a mobile-device application that can provide citizens with electronic notifications about the restoration of driving-licence points. Where the required technical infrastructure is available, it may also be used to deliver administrative-violation documents to a person.

The **National Public Service Portal (Cổng Dịch vụ công quốc gia)** is Vietnam’s national online government service platform. It serves as a channel for individuals, vehicle owners and their authorized representatives, agencies, and organizations to submit application dossiers, electronic forms, follow-up documents, and written requests to competent authorities.

The portal supports a range of procedures, including applications for authorization or approval to operate a smart traffic vehicle; applications to change or reissue a vehicle operating permit; permit and other administrative applications; and registration for examinations, including the legal-knowledge examination. Applicants can also use it to track application processing and receive notices. Licensing authorities may send notices to applicants’ accounts about applications or documents that are incomplete, refused, or ineligible. The portal is also identified as a channel for delivering administrative-violation decisions and related documents to users’ registered accounts. In addition, it provides public access to information from the road traffic order and safety database.

An **AUTHORIZED OFFICIAL** is a person empowered under the cited rules to temporarily seize a vehicle and its related documents to prevent an administrative violation. The official is also authorized to decide whether to impose an administrative penalty for a paperwork violation.

“Article 48” refers to provisions in two Vietnamese legal instruments. Article 48 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerns the temporary impoundment or custody of vehicles and documents related to the driver and violating vehicle. It sets out circumstances in which an authorized person may impound a vehicle before issuing a penalty decision, including cases where a driver cannot present required documents during an inspection, and identifies relevant violations. It also addresses costs associated with arranging replacement transport and moving detained vehicles.

Separately, Article 48 of Law 36/2024/QH15 establishes road traffic order and safety requirements for motorized four-wheeled vehicles used to transport passengers or goods. These include displaying the transport operator’s name and telephone number and, for passenger transport, the fares.

The **Ministry of Public Security (Bộ Công an; BCA)** is Vietnam’s focal agency assisting the Government in unified state management of road traffic order and safety. It coordinates with other ministries and government bodies on implementing relevant laws and decrees, leads international cooperation in this field, and assists the Government with negotiating and signing international treaties and agreements. The Traffic Police Department operates under the Ministry and carries out functions assigned to it, including receiving reports and handling traffic-related tasks.

The Ministry builds, centrally manages, and operates the road traffic order and safety database and related specialized databases. These cover matters including vehicles and their registration, driver training and testing, driving licences, traffic violations, and road accidents. Its electronic administrative-violations database records driving-licence points, deductions, and restorations. The Ministry’s systems are connected with other agencies’ databases to share information such as insurance, registration, inspection, accidents, and penalties. It is responsible for the development, operation, maintenance, and upgrading of these systems and receives allocated funding for that work.

The Ministry also regulates and administers driver testing and licensing, including procedures for issuing, exchanging, reissuing, and revoking licences and international driving permits. Its Minister is assigned authority to set related rules and standards, including provisions for police personnel performing security or national-defence duties. The Ministry oversees driver testing and licensing responsibilities and is tasked with developing a regular, elite, modern Traffic Police force. It also issues or directs rules in areas such as traffic patrol and enforcement, accident investigation, vehicle registration, technical and environmental inspection, traffic-command systems, and monitoring equipment. It directs the management and use of signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles and issues or revokes relevant permits, subject to exceptions for vehicles managed by the Ministry of National Defence.

For foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam, the Ministry coordinates with the Ministries of Foreign Affairs, Transport, Finance, Construction, and other relevant bodies. It helps organize and manage these activities, coordinates temporary-import and re-export procedures, maintains a database on foreign vehicles, and inspects and addresses violations. It is notified of relevant violations, accidents, and incidents and, where required, informs other agencies and representatives. The Ministry also manages a mobile traffic application, including its use for real-time reporting of foreign-vehicle convoy activities, and provides online public-service channels.

The Ministry coordinates road-traffic legal education with education and labour authorities, including instruction in educational and vocational institutions and safe motorbike-riding materials for students. It approves software for legal-knowledge tests and receives test-result reports. Regulations cited as Ministry instruments use the designation **BCA**; reports on implementation difficulties may be submitted through the Traffic Police Department.

The **National Identification Application (Ứng dụng định danh quốc gia)** is Vietnam’s national digital-identity service and an online channel for administrative procedures. Applicants may use it to submit application dossiers, examination registrations, written requests, and follow-up documents, including applications for permits, approvals, and authorization to operate smart traffic vehicles. It may also provide an electronic form for requesting changes to or reissuance of a smart traffic vehicle operating permit.

The application can be used to receive notices about application processing, including notices that an application or supporting documents are incomplete or do not meet the relevant requirements, or that an application has been refused. Such notices may be sent to the electronic account of the relevant individual, business, or organization.

The application is also associated with electronic identity accounts and identity verification. Where the relevant system and technical infrastructure are available, it may support delivery of administrative-violation documents to a person’s electronic identification account, access to identity information for verification, and updates to a driver’s deducted- or restored-points status when a driving licence is represented as a data message.

Article 48 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, titled “Temporary seizure of vehicles and documents related to the driver and violating vehicle,” governs the temporary seizure of vehicles and relevant documents in connection with violations. It sets out circumstances in which an authorized person may temporarily seize a vehicle before issuing a penalty decision. Clause 3 addresses cases where a driver cannot present required documents during an inspection: if the driver then fails to provide the documents, or the relevant information integrated into an electronic identification account, by the deadline recorded in the administrative violation record, the provision governs the resulting handling of the case. It also addresses violations involving required paperwork that is presented later.

**ISSUANCE OF A PENALTY DECISION** is the formal administrative act of deciding to impose a penalty for an administrative violation. A vehicle may be temporarily seized or detained before the decision is issued.

TEMPORARY DETENTION OF VEHICLES AND RELATED DOCUMENTS is a preventive measure and procedure set out in Article 48 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. It allows authorized persons to temporarily hold a vehicle and its related documents in specified circumstances, including in connection with a violation.

An **ADMINISTRATIVE PENALTY DECISION** imposes a penalty for an administrative violation. A vehicle may be temporarily seized before the decision is issued, and temporary custody of the vehicle or related documents may also be used to help ensure the decision is enforced. Once the decision takes legal effect, any related driving-licence point deductions are automatically recorded in the relevant database.

The **Issuance of an Administrative Penalty Decision** is the act of deciding to impose an administrative penalty. The decision may follow the temporary seizure or custody of a vehicle under the cited legal provisions, where the vehicle is held to immediately prevent a violation.

Article 125 of the Law on Handling Administrative Violations is cited as the legal basis for temporarily detaining or seizing a vehicle before an administrative penalty decision is issued. The cited provisions include point b of clause 1 and clauses 2 and 8, as referenced by Article 48 of the decree.

The **ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONING PROCEDURE** covers the process for imposing administrative penalties on vehicle owners and drivers who violate road-traffic safety and order regulations, as described in Article 47 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It includes preparing a record of the violation and applying the governing principles for penalties. If the vehicle owner is absent when the violation is handled, the vehicle’s driver may sign the violation record as a witness.

**FAILURE TO PRESENT REQUIRED DOCUMENTS** refers to a vehicle operator’s inability or failure to produce one or more required documents during an inspection, including a driver’s license or vehicle registration certificate. The required documents may be presented in paper form or through information integrated into an electronic identification account. The violation also applies when the operator does not provide the documents or their electronic information by the deadline for resolving the violation.

**TEMPORARY CUSTODY OF VEHICLES AND RELATED DOCUMENTS** is an administrative measure under Article 48 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. In specified violation cases, an authorized person may temporarily hold a vehicle and relevant documents before a penalty decision, to verify facts needed to decide the penalty or to ensure enforcement of that decision. The procedure may apply when a driver cannot present required paperwork during an inspection. If the driver continues driving after the deadline for resolving the violation has passed, they may be penalized as though they did not have the required documents.
CREDIT INSTITUTION BRANCH is referenced in connection with the provision of a valid receipt accompanied by a certified copy of the vehicle registration certificate or documents.

TEMPORARY VEHICLE DETENTION refers to the temporary holding of a vehicle under applicable rules or a decree when specified document-related violations are identified. This detention may result in costs for replacement transportation and relocating the vehicle.

The **Administrative Violation Proceeding** is the process documented in an administrative violation report. It includes a specified period for resolving the case, during which the driver may present required documents or qualifying information from an electronic identification account.

**TEMPORARY SUSPENSION OF ACTIVITIES** is an administrative penalty or sanction that temporarily halts an activity or operation for a specified period. It may be imposed by the chairperson of a commune-level People’s Committee.

Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out the authority, order, and procedures for restoring driving-licence points. Its first clause identifies the officials authorized to restore points in the cases specified in Clause 3.

“Article 51” refers to two separate legal provisions. Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP addresses the authority, sequence and procedures for restoring driving-licence points. Article 51 of Law 36/2024/QH15 concerns ensuring road traffic order and safety for road vehicles transporting dangerous goods. These provisions cover different subjects and are distinguished by their respective legal instruments.

“Article 50” refers to two distinct provisions in Vietnamese legislation:

- **Article 50 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP** sets out the principles, authority, sequence, and procedures for deducting points from driving licences. When multiple point-deductible violations are handled in a single case, points are deducted only for the violation carrying the highest deduction.
- **Article 50 of Law 36/2024/QH15** establishes road-traffic order and safety requirements for vehicles transporting live animals or fresh food. Such transport must comply with applicable traffic-safety, food-safety, disease-control, and environmental-hygiene requirements.

The PUBLIC SERVICE PORTAL is an online government platform through which applicants can submit applications and required documents, including applications for operating permits. Citizens may also use a registered account to receive electronic notifications about points deducted from or restored to their driving licences. These notifications depend on the necessary infrastructure, technical capabilities, and information conditions being in place. The portal’s specific name is not provided in the source.

RESTORATION OF DRIVING-LICENSE POINTS is the process of returning points to a driving license. Restoration may occur automatically in cases specified in Clause 2 of Article 51. When a driver’s points have been exhausted, restoration is available after the driver passes the required theory test on legal knowledge.

**DRIVING-LICENCE POINT RESTORATION** is the procedure for restoring points on a driving licence in cases covered by the relevant decree. It includes the applicable authority, the sequence of steps, and the procedures to be followed, and is carried out by the traffic-police officials authorized under the decree.

The **Restoration of Driver’s License Points** procedure is addressed in Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It applies when a driver’s points have not been fully deducted and no further points have been deducted for 12 months following the most recent deduction. Article 51 sets out the responsible authority and the applicable sequence and formalities for restoring points.

**Driver’s License Point Restoration** is governed by Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. If a driver’s license has not had all its points deducted and no points have been deducted for 12 months since the most recent deduction, its point balance is automatically restored to 12. This rule also applies while the license is subject to suspension of usage rights.

When all points have been deducted, restoration is handled under Article 51(3). Once the license’s point data has been restored to 12, the person authorized under Article 51(1)(b) informs the license holder.

ỨNG DỤNG ĐỊNH DANH QUỐC GIA (Vietnam’s National Identification Application) is an online channel through which applicants can submit a dossier. It also displays updated driving-licence points-restoration status in a citizen’s electronic identification account when the driving licence is represented as a data message.

The **ROAD TRAFFIC LEGAL-KNOWLEDGE TEST** assesses knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety and is organized by a Traffic Police Division. It forms part of the process for restoring points on a driver’s license, using the forms specified in the relevant circular.

For eligible ethnic-minority test takers who cannot read or write Vietnamese and whose A1 motorcycle-license points have been exhausted, the test is administered separately through oral questions and answers, using a paper-based multiple-choice method similar to the A1 licensing examination. The authority may provide an interpreter, or the test taker may hire one.

For tests registered under Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA but held after Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA takes effect, the provisions of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA apply.

DRIVING LICENSE POINT RESTORATION is the procedure for restoring points on a driving license under Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Restoration occurs after the license holder passes the required test.

PHỤC HỒI ĐIỂM GIẤY PHÉP LÁI XE là thủ tục khôi phục điểm trên giấy phép lái xe. Theo quy trình được mô tả, người lái xe phải chưa bị trừ hết điểm và không bị trừ điểm trong 12 tháng kể từ lần bị trừ điểm gần nhất; đồng thời phải vượt qua kỳ kiểm tra kiến thức pháp luật về trật tự, an toàn giao thông. Sau khi đạt yêu cầu, điểm giấy phép lái xe được khôi phục lên 12 điểm và cập nhật tự động.
The heads of government agencies, including agencies attached to the Government, are responsible for implementing Decree 168/2024/ND-CP.

“KIỂM TRA KIẾN THỨC PHÁP LUẬT VỀ TRẬT TỰ, AN TOÀN GIAO THÔNG ĐƯỜNG BỘ” là kỳ kiểm tra kiến thức pháp luật về trật tự, an toàn giao thông đường bộ dành cho người lái xe có toàn bộ điểm trên giấy phép lái xe bị trừ. Người lái xe phải tham gia và đạt yêu cầu để đủ điều kiện được phục hồi điểm giấy phép lái xe.

CỤC CẢNH SÁT GIAO THÔNG (the Traffic Police Department) is a department under Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security. It receives dossiers required under the relevant provisions, including Article 33, and issues, reissues, or revokes permits for eligible priority vehicles registered with it by central-level ministries, sectors, and agencies.

The department develops and issues the theoretical question set used to test knowledge of road traffic laws for motor vehicle driver licensing. Its director is responsible for providing consistent guidance at locations where road traffic order and safety knowledge tests are held and, under the cited provision, is authorized to impose fines of up to 75,000,000 đồng. The department also comprises the professional divisions and their heads specified in the relevant regulations.

For implementation of the relevant circular, police units and local authorities report difficulties to the Ministry of Public Security through the department. Its electronic information page is also used to publish updated information about driving licences whose points have been restored.

The DRIVER’S LICENSE HOLDER is a person who holds a driver’s license and is eligible, subject to the stated conditions, to exchange it or obtain a reissued license. The holder’s license points have been restored to 12, and the holder is to be informed of that restoration.

An **ADMINISTRATIVE ROAD-TRAFFIC VIOLATION** is a breach of administrative rules governing road-traffic order and safety. The database records the violation conduct, time, and location as required by applicable regulations. The descriptions concern violations that occurred and ended before Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP or Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP took effect; a violation may nevertheless be discovered or remain under review after the relevant decree takes effect.

The ministers are identified as responsible for implementing Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Decree 151/2024/ND-CP, Decree No. 236/2026/ND-CP, and Decree 238/2026/ND-CP. Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is cited twice in the descriptions.

The **Environmental Protection Law** is the body of legislation governing environmental protection. Its provisions determine when the motorcycle and moped emissions-inspection rule takes effect, including the provision in point b, clause 1 of Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.

ROAD-TRAFFIC VIOLATION SANCTIONING is the procedure described in Article 47 for imposing penalties on vehicle owners or drivers who violate road-traffic rules and safety regulations. It also addresses how to handle a single person’s conduct when that conduct falls under multiple provisions.
The chairpersons of provincial and municipal People’s Committees—including those in provinces and centrally governed cities—are responsible for implementing Decree 168/2024/ND-CP.

Government agencies are subordinate to the Government and are responsible, within their assigned duties and authority, for implementing Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. Their heads are identified in the decree’s implementation provisions. These agencies must coordinate with the Ministry of Public Security to build and manage the database on road traffic order and safety. They may also own intelligent transport vehicles and prepare and submit the required application dossiers for operating permits.

“CARRYING PASSENGERS NOT ON THE CONTRACT LIST” is a violation in which a passenger-transport vehicle picks up or carries a person whose name does not appear on the passenger list for the signed contract.

Ministerial-Level Agencies are government agencies at the level of ministries. Within their respective duties and authority, they organize communication and dissemination of laws on road traffic order and safety and coordinate with the Ministry of Public Security to build and manage the road-traffic-order-and-safety database. Their heads are identified in the relevant decree provisions as responsible for implementation, including Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and Decree 238/2026/ND-CP.

Centrally governed cities are cities directly administered by the central government. Under the decree, the chairpersons of their People’s Committees are responsible for implementing it, and their police traffic divisions are included among the authorities covered by Article 23.

The heads of ministerial-level agencies, including agencies equivalent to ministries, are the officials responsible for implementing Decree 238/2026/ND-CP, Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, and Decree 151/2024/ND-CP.

Government ministries are responsible for implementing relevant government decrees, including Decree 184/2025/ND-CP and Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, within their assigned duties and authority. They coordinate with the Ministry of Public Security to build and manage the database on road traffic order and safety, and organize communication and dissemination of laws in this area. The Traffic Command Center is also permitted to connect with and share data with ministries.

The **Department of Construction** (Vietnamese: **Sở Xây dựng**) is a government department whose director is identified in Articles 41 and 44 as an official with authority to impose specified administrative penalties for violations. Under Article 44, including paragraph 2, the director may apply remedial measures and, where authorized, temporarily revoke permits or suspend activities. This authority applies during inspections and is limited to the sanctions specified in the decree. No particular department, locality, or individual director is identified.

The Provincial and Municipal People’s Committees are local government bodies of provinces and centrally governed cities. Their chairpersons are responsible for implementing Decrees 238/2026/ND-CP and 168/2024/ND-CP. These committees also direct local authorities in managing and inspecting foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam, and receive copies of relevant approval documents to support coordination and management.

The Head of the Inspection Team established by the Minister of Construction is an unnamed official with authority to impose administrative penalties under Article 41. Article 44 lists this position among the officials with sanctioning authority.

The **Inspection Team Established by the Minister of Construction** is a ministerial inspection team whose head is among the officials authorized to impose administrative penalties. Article 44, clause 3, specifies that the team’s head may impose fines of up to 75 million Vietnamese dong. The team is also referenced in connection with penalty authority under Article 41.

A **Road Management Area** (Khu Quản lý đường bộ) is an organizational unit under the Vietnam Road Administration. Under Article 44, its Director is authorized to impose specified administrative penalties, including fines of up to **37,500,000 đồng**, and to apply specified remedial measures. The Director may also temporarily withdraw permits or temporarily suspend activities where authorized by the article. The descriptions primarily identify Article 44 as the source of this authority.

The head of the inspection team established by the Director General of the Vietnam Road Administration is authorized to impose administrative penalties under Article 41. Article 44 also identifies this position as having sanctioning authority.

**TEMPORARY REVOCATION OF LICENSE OR PROFESSIONAL CERTIFICATE USE** is an administrative sanction in which the right to use a license or professional certificate is withdrawn for a specified period. It may be imposed by the chairperson of a commune-level People’s Committee.

The Director of the Road Management Area is the official who heads a Road Management Area under the Vietnam Road Administration. The position is recognized in Articles 41 and 44 as having authority to impose administrative penalties. This authority includes imposing fines of up to 37,500,000 đồng, temporarily withdrawing the right to use permits, temporarily suspending activities, and applying the remedial measures specified in Article 3, Clause 3.

A **Regional Road Management Area** (*Khu Quản lý đường bộ*) is an organizational unit under the Vietnam Road Administration. Its director is authorized to impose administrative penalties for specified violations, including in connection with inspections. The director is listed among the officials with sanctioning authority under Article 44. No particular Regional Road Management Area is identified.

The **Director of the Department of Construction** is an unnamed official who heads a Department of Construction; no particular person or department is identified. Under the decree, Article 44 lists the director among officials authorized to impose administrative penalties. This authority includes imposing fines of up to 60,000,000 đồng and applying specified administrative and remedial measures, including those set out in Article 3(3). The director may also temporarily revoke the right to use a permit or temporarily suspend activities. The descriptions additionally refer to Article 41 as a source of the director’s penalty authority.

“CLAUSE 1” refers to several different provisions, depending on the article. Clause 1 of Article 52 defines oversized vehicles as motor vehicles or specialized motor vehicles whose overall dimensions exceed the limits permitted by national technical regulations for motor vehicles. Clause 1 of Article 43 authorizes on-duty People’s Public Security officers to impose fines of up to 7,500,000 Vietnamese dong. Clause 1 of Article 45 requires automobile passenger transport to follow its registered schedule and route, except in cases of force majeure. Clause 1 of Article 57 describes driving-licence categories and the vehicles permitted under Category C.
The NATIONAL POPULATION DATA CENTER is a national center for population data. Under Article 43, its director is among the officials authorized to impose administrative penalties.

The REGIMENT-LEVEL MOBILE POLICE UNIT is a Mobile Police unit organized at the regiment level. Its commander is among the officials authorized under Article 43 to impose specified administrative penalties.

The **PROVINCIAL-LEVEL PEOPLE’S COMMITTEE** is a local government body at the provincial level. Under Article 42, Clause 2 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, its chairperson has authority to impose administrative sanctions, including issuing warnings, imposing fines of up to 75,000,000 đồng, suspending permits or activities for a limited period, confiscating items or vehicles involved in violations, and applying the remedial measures specified by law.

The **Minister of Construction** is the unnamed official who heads the Ministry of Construction and is responsible for prescribing or issuing a range of regulations and requirements concerning road traffic. Under Law 36/2024/QH15, these include national technical regulations and related procedures and requirements under Article 41; road signals under Article 11; the classification of road-traffic vehicles under Article 34; and matters specified in Article 52, including road limits, vehicle operation, and permits.

The Minister is also authorized to prescribe detailed rules on vehicle speed and safe following distances, requirements for safely arranging and securing goods transported by automobile, and the classification and safety and environmental quality certification of intelligent transport vehicles. The Minister’s responsibilities further include setting driver-training requirements under Article 60 and prescribing training programs and formats, testing procedures, certificate issuance and reissuance procedures, and standards for training establishments under Article 63.

For enforcement, the Minister may establish an inspection team or delegation. Its head is among the officials authorized to impose administrative penalties under Article 44; the descriptions also associate the Minister’s inspection authority with Article 41.

The **Head of a Company-Level Mobile Police Unit** is a role, not a specifically named individual. Under the cited provision, the role holder is authorized to apply specified remedial measures and to confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 30,000,000 đồng.

The **BATTALION-LEVEL MOBILE POLICE UNIT COMMANDER** is an unnamed commander or head of a battalion-level Mobile Police unit. Under Article 43, the commander is authorized to impose administrative penalties and apply specified remedial measures.
The head of an inspection team established by the Director of the Vietnam Road Administration is identified in Article 44 as an official authorized to impose administrative penalties.

Article 3, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP lists the remedial measures applicable to administrative violations concerning road traffic order and safety in road transport. It specifies the measures authorized for application under Article 43, Clause 7, and contains the measures referenced in Article 44.
The **Head of the Inspection Team Established by the Minister of Construction** is authorized under Article 44, clause 3, to impose administrative penalties.
The PROVINCIAL MOBILE POLICE DIVISION is a provincial-level police division responsible for mobile policing. Its head is among the officials granted powers under Article 43.

The Division of Guidance, Vehicle Registration, and Inspection is a professional division within the Traffic Police Department. It is responsible for providing guidance on vehicle registration and inspection, and it is identified by the title of its head. The division’s head is among the officials authorized under clause 5.
The Head of the Inspection Delegation established by the Minister of Construction is listed in Article 44 among officials authorized to impose administrative penalties.

The head of an inspection team established by the Director of the Vietnam Road Administration is an unnamed official with sanctioning authority under Article 44. The role is authorized to impose fines of up to 60,000,000 đồng and to apply the remedial measures specified in Article 44(2).

The inspection team established by the Director of the Vietnam Road Administration is listed in Article 44 among the bodies whose officials have administrative sanctioning authority. Under Article 44(2), the team’s head or leader is authorized to impose fines of up to 60,000,000 đồng, apply remedial measures, and temporarily revoke permits or suspend activities.
The Head of the Inspection Delegation established by the Director of the Vietnam Road Administration is listed in Article 44 among officials authorized to impose administrative penalties.

The **Inspection Delegation Established by the Minister of Construction** is an inspection body whose head is among the officials authorized under Article 44 to impose administrative penalties. The head may issue warnings, impose fines of up to 75,000,000 đồng, suspend or revoke permits, and apply remedial measures.

The Director of the Regional Road Management Area under the Vietnam Road Administration is an official with authority to impose administrative penalties. The role is listed in Article 44 among officials with sanctioning authority.

The Inspection Delegation Established by the Director of the Vietnam Road Administration is an inspection body created by the Director. Under Article 44, its head is authorized to impose administrative penalties, including issuing warnings, imposing fines of up to 60,000,000 đồng, suspending or revoking permits, and applying remedial measures.

The **Road Management Area under the Vietnam Road Administration** is a subordinate road-management body. Its director is listed in Article 44 among officials with authority to impose administrative sanctions. The director may issue warnings, impose fines of up to 37,500,000 đồng, suspend or revoke permits, and apply remedial measures.

Article 44 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out the sanctioning authority of specified officials, including heads of inspection teams. It also identifies the remedial measures those officials are authorized to apply.
