The **Ministry of Construction (Bộ Xây dựng, BXD)** is a Vietnamese government ministry with responsibilities in road transport, vehicle safety, driver training, and related information systems. Under the cited laws and decrees, it manages driver training and the technical safety and environmental-protection quality of motor vehicles, specialized motor vehicles, and their parts.

The Ministry builds or manages databases covering vehicle and specialized-vehicle inspections; driver training and certificates concerning road-traffic-law knowledge; road-transport businesses and vehicle badges; and electronic road-traffic payments. Its information systems connect with the road traffic order and safety database and support the sharing of information—including journey-monitoring data and vehicle insurance, accident, violation, registration, and inspection records—for road safety, law enforcement, and state management.

The Minister of Construction is assigned to issue or prescribe detailed rules in areas including vehicle classification, speeds and safe distances, vehicle safety and environmental standards, energy consumption, warranty and maintenance facilities, vehicle inspectors, road signals, and intelligent-transport-vehicle certification. The Minister also sets requirements for driver-training programs and testing, certificate procedures and training establishments, safe-driving times, motorcycle driver-training facilities, and the arrangement and securing of goods transported by automobile. Other assigned matters include road load and clearance limits, vehicle operations, oversized or overweight cargo and its transport, and permits for oversized, overloaded, or tracked vehicles. The Ministry also issues national technical regulations for child safety equipment.

In coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry helps organize and manage activities involving foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam. It receives relevant approval documents and copies for coordination and management, and is to be notified of specified legal violations or traffic accidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign vehicles in Vietnam.

The Minister may establish inspection teams or delegations under the cited provisions; their heads are among the officials authorized to impose specified administrative penalties. The Ministry is also identified by the BXD designation in national technical regulation **QCVN 07-4:2023/BXD**.

CỤC ĐƯỜNG BỘ VIỆT NAM (the Vietnam Road Administration), under the Ministry of Transport, is a Vietnamese government agency responsible for managing assigned road infrastructure. It has authority to decide where speed-limit signs are placed on expressways under its management and receives information and data collected by vehicle journey-monitoring devices. Its director has sanctioning authority under Article 44 and may establish an inspection team. The Regional Road Management Zones are part of the agency.

The **Head of the Inspection Delegation Established by the Minister of Construction** is granted sanctioning authority under Article 44. This authority includes imposing fines of up to 75,000,000 đồng and applying the specified remedial measures and other administrative measures, including those provided for in Clause 3.

The Head of the Inspection Delegation established by the Director of the Vietnam Road Administration is listed in Article 44 as an official with administrative sanctioning authority. The office may impose fines of up to 60,000,000 đồng and apply other administrative measures specified in that Article.

Civil servants are government employees or public officials who perform official duties or tasks and are authorized under the relevant decree or provision to prepare and make records of administrative violations.
Public employees are authorized under the decree to prepare records of administrative violations when performing their assigned official duties or tasks.
The Ministry of Transport of Vietnam is identified by the abbreviation BGTVT, which appears in the designation of the relevant circular.

ROAD TRAFFIC PARTICIPATION is the activity of taking part in traffic on roads. Its requirements vary by participant group: lower secondary students are instructed to wear a compliant helmet and fasten its strap correctly, while drivers and specialized motor vehicle operators must observe speed limits and maintain safe distances. Article 30 addresses participation by pedestrians and other listed groups, setting rules applicable to those groups.

BỘ GIAO THÔNG VẬN TẢI (Vietnam’s Ministry of Transport), abbreviated BGTVT in official circular designations and numbers, assigns expressways to designated agencies for management. The Ministry also built and manages the database of inspections for motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles, and receives information and data collected by vehicle journey-monitoring devices.

THÔNG TƯ 38/2024/TT-BGTVT is a Vietnamese circular governing road-speed regulations and safe distances. Article 1 defines its scope, covering road design speeds and the operating speeds and safe distances of motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles using roads. These provisions do not apply to priority vehicles performing duties under law. Article 4 sets out principles for complying with operating-speed and safe-distance requirements while driving. Under Article 7, specialized motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles may travel at no more than 40 km/h on roads other than expressways. Article 12 addresses implementation: if a normative document cited in the circular is amended, supplemented, or replaced, the corresponding amended, supplemented, or replacement document applies.

Article 6 of Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT establishes default maximum permitted speeds for motor vehicles on roads outside expressways when the specified road signs are absent. The maximum is 60 km/h on divided roads or one-way roads with at least two motor-vehicle lanes, and 50 km/h on two-way roads or one-way roads with a single motor-vehicle lane. Drivers must comply with these limits.

PROVINCES are administrative areas whose People’s Committee chairpersons are responsible for implementing the decree. Their police traffic divisions are also included among the authorities described in Article 23.

**Road traffic** is the activity of people and vehicles traveling or participating on roads, including public roads. It involves drivers and other vehicle operators, including operators of specialized motorcycles, as well as passengers and other road users.

The cited provisions regulate conduct and safety in road traffic. They address participation by children, pregnant women, elderly or frail people, people with disabilities, and people lacking civil act capacity; requirements for vehicle drivers and specialized-motorcycle operators; safe conduct and speed; and maintaining a safe following distance between vehicles. They also require drivers and passengers to wear seat belts where seats are equipped for them and set out a prohibition concerning passengers on motorcycles and mopeds.

Article 7 of Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT sets out provisions relevant to drivers when the specified road signs are absent. It is also referenced by Article 6 as identifying motor vehicles excluded from the general speed limits in Article 6’s table; the available descriptions do not provide those vehicle categories or the detailed rules.

SPECIALIZED MOTOR VEHICLE OPERATORS are people who operate specialized motor vehicles on roads. They are required to comply with regulations governing operating speed and safe following distances. They are also the intended participants in road-traffic-law knowledge training and examinations, and may seek training and certification in that knowledge.

Article 8 of Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT sets the maximum permitted operating speeds for motorized four-wheel passenger and freight vehicles on roads other than expressways. Drivers must follow these limits when the specified road signs are absent. Article 6 also refers to Article 8 for the motor vehicles excluded from the general speed limits in its table; the descriptions provided do not specify which vehicles are excluded.

The **COMPETENT ROAD MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY** is the authorized body responsible for issuing circulation permits for vehicles transporting oversized or overweight cargo, including oversized vehicles, overweight vehicles, and tracked vehicles operating on roads. As specified in Clause 3 of Article 10, it also leads and coordinates with the relevant traffic police and district-level People’s Committee to determine the permitted operating speed and arrange for the installation of speed signs.

The ROAD MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY is the competent authority designated under Clause 3 to manage roads and address risks or problems affecting road infrastructure and traffic safety. It should be notified promptly when a qualifying unexpected situation is discovered and must respond, within its functions and duties, when it detects or receives information about an unexpected situation that causes disorder or threatens road traffic safety. The authority leads coordination to determine permitted operating speeds and arrange the installation of speed-limit signs. It is also connected to the data-management system described in Article 71 of Law 36/2024/QH15 and shares information through that system.

Populated areas are densely inhabited geographic zones that serve as reference points for distinguishing road segments located outside them. In these areas, horn use is restricted between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m., except by priority vehicles.

**Placement of Operational Speed Signs** is a regulatory activity in which a competent authority determines where to place signs indicating the operational speed limit on specified roads. It applies to the cases specified in Clause 4 of Article 10.

The **Traffic Police Force** is the organization identified in Article 65, clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15 as carrying out patrol and control activities to maintain road traffic order and safety. It manages, operates, and uses the traffic command center and its infrastructure, equipment systems, and database, including the road traffic order and safety database.

Under Article 71 of the law, the Traffic Police Force also manages, operates, and uses systems for managing data from journey-monitoring devices and devices that record images of drivers and passenger compartments. Its applications are designated as electronic channels for accessing shared information from the road traffic order and safety database.

For roads under its responsibility, the Traffic Police Force coordinates with the relevant road management authority when considering permitted operating speeds and deciding how speed-limit signs should be installed or arranged. It also leads or coordinates the organization of safe motorbike-riding skills instruction for students, working with high school authorities and vocational education establishment management agencies.

Children are among the groups whose participation in road traffic is addressed by Article 30 of Law 36/2024/QH15, including under clause 2. The law provides for their road use to be accommodated and regulated. Children enrolled in preschool educational institutions are intended recipients of education on road traffic law and safety, including how to wear a helmet correctly, to strengthen their self-protection and awareness of complying with traffic rules. Children are also the people the described safety device is designed to protect while they are sitting or lying in a car.

A ROAD TRAFFIC CONTROLLER is a person responsible for directing road traffic. The role may be performed by a traffic police officer or by a person assigned to guide traffic on roads. The relevant provisions describe signals made with the controller’s right hand and specify the directions in which nearby road users may travel.

ROAD TRAFFIC LAW VIOLATIONS are conduct that breaches laws and regulations governing road traffic order and safety. They may be detected and assessed by equipment and handled by the competent authorities. Such violations should be promptly detected and prevented, and those identified should be dealt with strictly in accordance with the law.

ROAD TRAFFIC DIRECTION AND CONTROL comprises the activities of planning, directing, and managing road traffic. When congestion occurs, these activities are assigned to the traffic police agency. They are regulated by Law No. 36/2024/QH15.

TRAFFIC COMMAND CENTERS are subject to regulation under Article 75, which governs their construction, management, and operation and provides for the issuance of national technical regulations. State policy also calls for their modernization.

NHÀ NƯỚC (the State) establishes policies on road traffic order and safety. The cited law addresses these policies and provides for rewards and compensation for people who assist state agencies in carrying out related duties.

Road traffic congestion is a disruption in which people and vehicles become backed up and travel very slowly or are unable to move. It may prompt traffic-control measures and efforts to ease the congestion or prevent it from worsening.

ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY ASSURANCE is the activity of maintaining order and safety on public roads. It covers road vehicles transporting dangerous goods and oversized or overweight cargo vehicles traveling along their routes. The activity is to be conducted openly and transparently, and in a manner convenient for the public.

CIRCULAR 38/2024/TT-BGTVT is a Vietnamese Ministry of Transport regulation on vehicle operating speeds and safe distances on roads. Article 3 defines terms including “operating speed” (a vehicle’s speed while participating in road traffic), “one-way road,” “payload” (the permitted cargo mass recorded in specified technical-safety and environmental-protection certificates), “road in a densely populated area,” and the safe distance between vehicles.

Article 4 sets out the principles drivers must follow for operating speeds and safe distances. Where relevant signs are absent, drivers are directed to apply Articles 6, 7, 8 and 11. Article 5 addresses road design speeds, including the basis for determining rural-road design speeds and the design speeds used to calculate expressway technical criteria.

Article 6 establishes maximum permitted speeds for motor vehicles on roads other than expressways, with limits differentiated by road configuration and provisions addressing roads outside populated areas. Article 8 sets maximum speeds for four-wheel motorized passenger and cargo vehicles on non-expressway roads; passenger vehicles are limited to 30 km/h when operated within the permitted area and time. Article 9 sets maximum and minimum speeds for motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles on expressways: the maximum is 120 km/h, and the minimum is generally 60 km/h. Where an expressway’s design speed is 60 km/h, the minimum is determined by the approved traffic organization plan. The article also requires speed-limit signs.

Article 10 governs how permitted operating speeds are determined and how speed signs are installed, including requirements for sign placement. Article 11 sets safe-distance rules. On clear, dry, level roads, required distances depend on vehicle speed; below 60 km/h, drivers must maintain a distance appropriate to traffic conditions.

Under Article 12, the circular takes effect on January 1, 2025. It replaces Circular 31/2019/TT-BGTVT and Article 15 of Circular 06/2023/TT-BGTVT.

The **Minister of Transport** is the unnamed officeholder responsible for Vietnam’s Ministry of Transport. The cited laws and regulations assign the Minister authority to issue national technical regulations and detailed rules governing road transport and vehicles.

The Minister’s responsibilities include defining oversized and overweight cargo and regulating its road transportation and circulation permits; issuing road-signal regulations; and prescribing vehicle standards, technical requirements, size and load limits, and specified certification and inspection procedures. These responsibilities also cover vehicles and specialized motorcycles under research and development, intelligent-transport-vehicle classification and safety and environmental certification, motorcycle and moped emissions-inspection establishments, inspection exemptions and procedures, and vehicle standards and inspection certificates.

The Minister is further authorized to set conditions and procedures for issuing, exchanging, reissuing, and revoking driving licenses, subject to the stated exception, and to issue detailed regulations under Article 34, including defining identification signs for certain motor vehicles. The officeholder is also identified as the issuer of Circulars 31/2019/TT-BGTVT and 06/2023/TT-BGTVT. The source material does not name the individual holding the office.

Pregnant women are identified in Article 30 of Law 36/2024/QH15 as a group participating in road traffic. Their participation is addressed under Article 30, including clause 2, and the text says they should be accommodated and helped when crossing a road.

People with disabilities are among the groups whose participation in road traffic is addressed by Article 30 of Law 36/2024/QH15, including clause 2. Their needs are to be accommodated while they use the road, and they should be assisted when crossing. The text specifically refers to wheelchair users crossing the road and provides that they are given the right of way when required.

**Road traffic accidents** are incidents occurring on roads that are subject to detection, reporting, investigation, resolution, statistical recording, and prevention under Law No. 36/2024/QH15 and related regulations. Their management forms part of state management of road traffic order and safety. The Traffic Police investigate and resolve accidents under applicable law and procedures prescribed by the Minister of Public Security; investigative agencies may also handle cases. The Traffic Command Center supports authorities, and relevant equipment can assist work at accident scenes.

Under Article 81, reports of road traffic accidents are detected, received, and handled. Article 83 requires accidents to be investigated and resolved promptly, accurately, objectively, and lawfully. Where there are signs of a crime, the case is handled under criminal law and criminal procedure law. Other cases may involve expert assessment, reconstruction of the scene, and tracing the responsible vehicles and drivers.

Article 84 requires accident statistics to be accurate, complete, and timely, so they can support research and the development of prevention measures. Article 11, Clause 12 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP addresses database information on accident consequences, including the number of accidents, deaths and injuries, property damage, accident classifications, and the road traffic safety coefficient, as well as information on investigation and resolution, including cases handled administratively or criminally. The Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of National Defense are each assigned responsibility for building and managing specialized databases that include road traffic accidents.

The Road Traffic Accident Damage Mitigation Fund described in Article 85 is intended to mitigate damage resulting from accidents. Assistance may include rescue, treatment, and transport of injured people to emergency care. Road traffic accidents are also addressed through education about their risks and consequences, international cooperation, and measures to prevent their occurrence.

Relevant Agencies and Organizations are those concerned with road traffic order and safety and with the decree. They coordinate with the state management agency to communicate and disseminate relevant laws and are responsible for implementing the decree.

ROAD TRAFFIC LEGAL EDUCATION is the teaching and dissemination of legal knowledge concerning road traffic, traffic order, and safety. It is intended especially for children and students and helps people understand how to prevent traffic-accident risks, the consequences of traffic incidents, and how to respond when they occur.

AGENCIES are government or other organizations with various responsibilities related to legal and road-traffic administration. They may organize legal education and disseminate legal information to people under their management; their covered personnel or other eligible subjects may receive permits to use signaling equipment on priority vehicles. Their lawful rights and interests must be respected and protected by forces performing patrol and control duties. Government agencies may also be involved in checking knowledge of road-traffic rules and safety, and amendments or supplements issued by government or other agencies may be used to update the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database.

**RELEVANT INDIVIDUALS** are the people concerned by the circular and decree who are assigned responsibility for implementing them and may report any difficulties or obstacles. They also work with state management agencies to communicate and disseminate laws on road traffic order and safety, and coordinate with road management agencies to identify the causes of traffic congestion.

Educational institutions are the settings in which legal knowledge and education about road traffic order and safety are provided. They include preschool institutions, schools, upper-secondary schools, vocational education institutions, and other educational establishments. The education may address children and students, with content suited to the relevant group. These institutions are also responsible for organizing legal awareness and information activities for people under their management. In schools and vocational institutions, instruction may additionally cover safe motorcycle riding and include assessment.

Preschool Educational Institutions are establishments serving preschool-age children. Their teaching programs and activities are to provide age-appropriate education on road traffic laws, traffic order, and road safety. This education includes safety while walking and while travelling in road vehicles, as well as awareness of the dangers and consequences of failing to follow traffic safety rules. These institutions are also settings in which instruction on traffic-law compliance is organized and compliance with relevant road traffic laws is managed.
Vocational education students are learners enrolled in vocational education institutions who receive legal education on laws concerning road traffic order and safety.

**ROAD USERS** are people participating in or using road traffic. They are required to follow applicable traffic rules and signals, in the stated order of priority; keep to the right and use the designated lane or part of the road; and comply with lawful inspection and control requests. Traffic police guide road users and encourage compliance, while road-safety policies should treat them fairly and equally and protect their safety.

Road users must stop when instructed by a signal or traffic controller. The specific directions depend on the signal: for example, users in front of or behind a controller may be required to stop while those to the controller’s right or left may proceed; under another specified signal, users behind and to the right must stop, those in front may turn right, and those to the left may proceed in any direction. At a crossing, they must stop on their side before the stop line when a crossing guard signals, a red light flashes, a bell rings, or a barrier is moving or closed.

Road users must also be able to notice warning signals for goods extending beyond the front or rear of an automobile and must be promptly informed when an unexpected situation may threaten their safety.

The **ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE** is a nationwide shared information system established to support state management of road traffic order and safety. Under Decree 151/2024/ND-CP, its construction, management, operation, use, maintenance, and upgrading are addressed by Articles 9 and 16. It is built and managed by the Ministry of Public Security and operated and exploited by the Traffic Police Force. Relevant provincial and centrally governed city People’s Committees also have state-management responsibilities within their remit.

As described in Article 11, the database holds information on motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles, including registration, owners, and vehicle specifications; inspection and modification records; vehicle journeys and drivers’ operating times; and invoices related to vehicle purchases and sales. It also includes information on drivers and specialized-motorcycle operators, such as training, testing, licences, related certificates, health, and licence-point history. Other records cover transport businesses and vehicle badges; compulsory civil-liability insurance and insurance compensation; traffic accidents and recommendations for traffic organization at accident locations; and administrative violation handling, including vehicles involved, penalties, fines, supplementary sanctions, remedial measures, compliance deadlines, and licence-point management.

Article 12 addresses the collection of information for the database, including information obtained from national, ministerial, specialized, and other designated databases, as well as the driver and specialized-motorcycle operator health database. Records are updated by adding or adjusting information from specified sources and must be stored in accordance with archival law.

The database is intended to connect and share information with the National Population Database, the Road Database, and other relevant databases. Under applicable rules, competent state agencies may connect to, access, extract, share, and use its information. The system is to be maintained as complete, accurate, timely, continuous, stable, and accessible for lawful use by competent agencies, organizations, and individuals. Access excludes information related to national defense and security.

General Education Institutions are educational establishments—including preschool, primary, lower-secondary, and upper-secondary institutions—covered by the decree’s requirements concerning road-traffic legal education and compliance. They are settings where instruction on road traffic order and safety is organized, and where compliance with relevant laws is managed. Their teaching programs are to incorporate appropriate legal knowledge about road traffic order and safety, tailored to students’ educational levels. Their students are among the intended recipients of this education.

Vocational education institutions are educational establishments that provide vocational education and are covered by the road-traffic safety requirements described in Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. Their students—including those beginning their studies—are intended recipients of legal education on road traffic order and safety and guidance in safe motorbike, moped, or motorcycle riding skills.

The Ministry of Education and Training is responsible for developing instruction on relevant road-traffic laws. Vocational education institutions must incorporate this knowledge into their teaching programs in ways appropriate to their fields of study, carry out the teaching and compliance-management activities described in Article 8, and include compliance with road-traffic laws and safety requirements among the criteria for assessing and classifying students’ conduct.

Under Article 6, these institutions also help guide students in safe motorbike-riding skills, coordinating with the Traffic Police Force where required. They are responsible for organizing students and their families to sign commitments to obey traffic laws and safety requirements, reminding students to honor those commitments, and communicating with families about compliance.

The relevant ministries and ministerial-level agencies are other Vietnamese government bodies not individually named. They coordinate with the Ministry of Education and Training in carrying out the responsibilities described in Article 7, including developing and incorporating knowledge of road traffic order, safety, and related laws into education curricula.

ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY FORCES are responsible for maintaining order and safety on roads and for detecting, preventing, and handling legal violations. Their training and capacity-building are also addressed through international cooperation.

**International Cooperation on Road Traffic Order and Safety** is an area of state management under Article 86 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 and is described in Article 8, Clause 2. It covers international cooperation on road traffic order and safety, including cooperation to strengthen the material conditions needed to maintain that order and safety.

The Ministry of Public Security leads and carries out this cooperation in coordination with relevant ministries and sectors. It must be conducted in accordance with Vietnamese law and relevant international treaties, while respecting international law and protecting Vietnam’s independence, sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity, and lawful interests.

The Ministry of Education and Training is a Vietnamese government ministry responsible for incorporating road traffic order and safety into education. Under Article 7 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, it leads and coordinates the development and integration of relevant legal knowledge into curricula, organizes instruction and related educational activities, and manages compliance with traffic laws in preschools and general education institutions. It organizes road-safety education for preschool children and students from primary through upper-secondary school, and includes compliance with road traffic laws among the criteria for assessing students’ conduct.

The Ministry also develops relevant instruction for upper-secondary and vocational education, coordinating with the Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs on road traffic law education at vocational institutions. For practical safe motorbike-riding instruction, it works with the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs to develop curricula and guidance materials, and leads and directs preparations of the necessary facilities and motorcycles. Separately, it is responsible for regulating procedures concerning specialized motorcycle-operation certificates for tractor operators who hold specified driving licences.
The 15th National Assembly of Vietnam is the legislature identified by “QH15” in the citation and identifier of Law 36/2024/QH15. In that identifier, “QH15” denotes Vietnam’s 15th National Assembly.

“CƠ QUAN NHÀ NƯỚC CÓ THẨM QUYỀN” (competent state authority) is an authority empowered to issue vehicle license plates; plates not issued by such an authority may not be used. It may also require the resolution of administrative violations involving road-traffic order and safety. Any such requirement must be fulfilled before the vehicle can undergo inspection.

The relevant ministries and sectors coordinate with the Ministry of Public Security to guide and organize implementation of the decree. They also cooperate with the Ministry in international efforts concerning road traffic order and safety.

The National Assembly of Vietnam is the legislature of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam. The designation “QH15” in legislation identifies the 15th National Assembly. During its 15th term and 7th session, it passed Law 36/2024/QH15 and is also the body behind Resolution 73/2022/QH15.

**Law No. 36/2024/QH15**, passed by Vietnam’s National Assembly on June 27, 2024, is the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. It establishes a broad legal framework for safe and orderly road traffic, including the responsibilities of road users, vehicle operators, public authorities, and transport businesses.

The law sets out state policies, governing principles, public education and international cooperation, and a database for road-traffic order and safety (Articles 3–8). Article 9 identifies prohibited conduct, including unsafe or unlawful vehicle operation and transport, unauthorized vehicle alterations, and misuse of traffic or monitoring data. Articles 10–33 regulate road-user conduct: obeying signals and speed and distance rules; lane use, overtaking, turning, stopping, parking, reversing, and opening vehicle doors; and travel on expressways, in tunnels, or across ferries. They also address priority vehicles, pedestrians and people needing assistance, animal-drawn and rudimentary vehicles, and motorcycle and moped drivers, passengers, and cargo.

Articles 34–43 cover vehicle classifications and roadworthiness, vehicle registration and identification plates, service-life limits, technical-safety and environmental requirements, inspections, and the responsibilities of vehicle owners, operators, and inspection establishments. Articles 44–55 regulate transport activities and specialized circumstances, including urban transport, passenger and school transport, goods and dangerous goods, live animals and fresh food, oversized or overweight loads and tracked vehicles, and foreign-registered vehicles operating in Vietnam.

The law also governs operator eligibility and licensing. Articles 56–63 address age and health conditions, driving-licence categories and validity, licence points, training and tests, licence issuance and exchange, and qualifications for specialized-motorcycle operators. Article 64 limits working and continuous driving time for drivers in commercial and internal transport. Articles 65–73 provide for patrol, control, vehicle stops, violation detection, monitoring systems, data management, and measures against obstruction or resistance to officials. Articles 74–79 cover traffic command and control, unexpected disruptions, and temporary use of roadways or sidewalks.

Articles 82–87 address accident rescue and recovery, investigation and resolution, statistics, the Road Traffic Accident Damage Mitigation Fund, and state-management responsibilities. Article 88 concerns implementation and effectiveness; Article 89 sets transitional rules, including continued validity or conversion of certain pre-existing licences, registration documents, and other arrangements.

**LAW NO. 36/2024/QH15** is a Vietnamese law governing road traffic order and safety. It covers traffic rules; vehicles and road users; traffic direction, control, patrol, and inspection; responses to road traffic accidents; and the responsibilities of state authorities. Its provisions include:

- **State policy, education, and cooperation:** Articles 4–8 address state policy and resources, public education and dissemination of traffic laws, family members’ responsibility to encourage compliance and protect young children on motorcycles, road-safety databases, and international cooperation.
- **Road-user conduct and vehicle use:** Articles 9–30 cover prohibited acts, child restraints and seating in cars, expressway use, horn signals, overtaking and yielding, towing, pedestrians and other specified road users, and when people may ride in the cargo bed of a goods vehicle. They also address passengers and goods carried on motorcycles, mopeds, and rudimentary vehicles.
- **Vehicles and transport operations:** Articles 34–57 classify vehicles and set participation and registration requirements; regulate license plates, auctions, inspection, and vehicle safety and environmental standards; and establish rules for passenger and goods transport. These include duties of passenger-vehicle drivers and service staff, safety requirements for school and preschool transport, and conditions for oversized, overweight, tracked, foreign-registered, and right-hand-drive vehicles. The law also addresses driving eligibility for people with disabilities.
- **Licensing and enforcement:** Articles 60–73 cover driver training and licence eligibility, exchange, reissuance, and revocation; patrol and control powers and procedures; equipment used during patrols; monitoring systems and data management, including personal-data protection; and measures against refusing or obstructing official inspections. Article 65 includes duties of traffic police, while Article 72 addresses road users’ rights and responsibilities.
- **Road infrastructure and public administration:** Articles 77–87 cover temporary use of roads and sidewalks, congestion remedies, safety recommendations for road works and infrastructure hazards, the Road Traffic Accident Damage Mitigation Fund, and the content and allocation of state-management responsibilities, including those of the Ministry of Health.

Article 89 provides transitional rules for certain licences issued before the law takes effect, including conversion or reissuance according to prior licence classes and certificates for operating specialized tractors. Article 88 establishes commencement and generally renders Road Traffic Law No. 23/2008/QH12 ineffective, subject to Article 89’s exceptions; it also provides that Clause 3 of Article 10 takes effect on July 1, 2026.

A PEDESTRIAN CROSSING AREA is a section of roadway marked or otherwise signposted for pedestrians to cross, or a place where pedestrians and wheelchair users are crossing. Overtaking is prohibited in this area.

Operators of specialized motorcycles are required to comply with applicable road traffic rules when using expressways under Article 25 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. Under Article 12, they must also observe speed limits and maintain a minimum safe distance from the vehicle ahead. Their health information may be held in the driver health database.

STOPPING is the act of bringing a vehicle to a stop. Under Law 36/2024/QH15, it is addressed alongside parking in Article 18, and drivers are required to stop as a safety action in the circumstances listed in Article 12, clause 3.

Article 11, “Compliance with Road Signals,” of Law 36/2024/QH15 sets out requirements for complying with road signals and defines the components of road signaling. It also assigns the Minister of Public Security responsibility for specifying the details of Clause 3.

A **ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT SCENE** is the location where a road traffic accident occurred. Road users and other people present are expected to help protect the scene and follow applicable safety instructions, including slowing down or stopping when necessary. Those responsible for the accident scene are instructed to preserve it, and an insurance enterprise’s dispatched person or representative must coordinate there with the accident-resolution unit.

“YIELDING TO A VEHICLE REQUESTING TO OVERTAKE” refers to the road-use conduct of giving way to a vehicle that has requested to pass. It is addressed alongside overtaking in Article 14 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

ROAD VEHICLE OPERATORS are people who operate vehicles participating in road traffic. They may operate vehicles in accordance with the law, subject to applicable requirements concerning age and health. They must obey orders to stop and requests for inspection or control; in specified circumstances, they must not disregard such orders and flee. They are also required to observe, reduce speed, or stop when necessary to ensure safety, comply with restrictions on stopping or parking in designated locations, and support and cooperate with the forces responsible for road traffic order and safety. During road-traffic patrol and control activities, they have the right to report legal violations.

Densely populated areas are places with a high concentration of people. Road users must remain alert and slow down or stop when needed to ensure safety. Between 22:00 and 05:00, a vehicle may request to overtake in these areas only by using lights.

**ROAD CROSSING** is the act of pedestrians or wheelchair users crossing a road. Where a designated crossing is available, pedestrians are required to use it; otherwise, they should observe traffic carefully and use hand signals as appropriate. Vehicle operators must take precautions when people are crossing. Children under seven, pregnant women, elderly or frail people, people with disabilities, and people who lack civil act capacity should be assisted when crossing.

**ROAD TRAFFIC CONTROL** is the activity defined in Article 74 of Law 36/2024/QH15, involving the direct guidance of road traffic to maintain order, safety, and smooth flow. It includes directing traffic, temporarily diverting traffic, and managing or operating traffic signals and related devices. When road traffic control is being conducted in an area, vehicle operators must follow instructions and, as necessary, slow down or stop to ensure safety.

**OVERTAKING A VEHICLE** is the act of passing another vehicle, as addressed in Article 14 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The article prohibits overtaking when the conditions set out in Clause 3 are not met and in locations specified under the article, including those covered by Clause 6.

A **TWO-WAY ROAD** is a road where traffic travels in both directions. The descriptions identify it as a location where overtaking is prohibited when visibility is restricted near a hill crest. They also list a two-way road with a total traveled-way width of less than 3.0 meters as one possible configuration of an operating road in a densely populated area with unfavorable conditions.

**YIELDING TO AN OVERTAKING VEHICLE** is the action taken by a driver whose vehicle is ahead when a vehicle behind requests to pass. When it is safe, the driver slows down, signals a right turn, and moves to the right to allow the overtaking vehicle to pass. If passing is unsafe or the road is obstructed, the driver signals left to indicate that passing is not permitted.

“DỪNG XE, ĐỖ XE” refers to stopping or parking a vehicle on a road, as regulated by Article 18 of Law 36/2024/QH15. Drivers must follow the applicable road-use rules. They may stop or park on a sufficiently wide roadside shoulder or on land outside the traveled portion of the road. If the shoulder is narrow or absent, they must stop or park close to the right edge of the road in their direction of travel.

**AVOIDING ONCOMING VEHICLES** is the road-traffic situation addressed by Article 17, in which vehicles traveling in opposite directions must pass one another. When the road has no separate lanes for each direction, drivers must reduce speed and keep to the right in their direction of travel.

**OVERTAKING** is the traffic maneuver in which a vehicle passes a vehicle traveling ahead. On a road with one motor-vehicle lane in each direction, it is defined as the vehicle behind moving left to pass; on roads with multiple lanes in the same direction, moving ahead is governed by lane-use rules.

Under Article 14 of Law 36/2024/QH15, overtaking is permitted only when the road ahead is safe. The overtaking driver must signal and maintain a safe distance from vehicles ahead and behind, while the vehicle being passed must not obstruct the maneuver. Overtaking is prohibited in specified circumstances, including when weather or road conditions make it unsafe, where visibility is restricted at a hill crest on a two-way road or on a curve, and in specified road-crossing situations.

Road vehicle drivers are people who operate vehicles participating in road traffic. They are subject to the applicable stopping and parking restrictions and, when stopping, parking, or moving into or out of a stopping or parking position, must signal as required by the cited provision. The term also includes drivers who fall within the management scope of the Ministry of National Defense.

**VEHICLE PARKING** refers to the act or event of a vehicle being parked. It is named alongside vehicle stopping in Article 18 of Law 36/2024/QH15, although the cited excerpt does not define it. Under the cited provision, parking is prohibited at road intersections and within five meters of their edges. Article 19 permits a vehicle door to be opened in connection with a parked vehicle.

Vietnamese Law No. 36/2024/QH15, the **Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety**, establishes rules and responsibilities for safe and orderly road traffic. It addresses road users’ conduct at level crossings and shared railway bridges (Article 24), the classification of specialized road vehicles—including certain national-defense or security vehicles using roads (Article 34(3))—and responsibilities relating to vehicle inspection and administrative violations (Article 43).

The law sets safety and order requirements for oversized, overweight, and tracked vehicles operating on roads, including when they may receive road-use permits (Article 52). It also prescribes conditions for drivers (Article 56), age and health requirements for vehicle operators (Article 59)—including an age of at least 24 for licences in classes D1, D2, C1E, and CE—and training, testing, and certification in road-traffic law for drivers of specialized motor vehicles (Article 63). Article 9 prohibits, among other conduct, the illegal production, use, purchase, or sale of vehicle licence plates and their improper attachment or alteration.

Other provisions cover the duties of the Traffic Command Center (Article 75), urgent mobilization of civilians, vehicles, and equipment and the duties of those mobilized (Article 68), and responses to noncompliance with inspection or control requirements and obstruction or resistance against officials (Article 73). When necessary, Article 73 permits proportionate use of force, support tools, or weapons as allowed by law to stop violations or for legitimate self-defense. Under Article 89, technical safety and environmental-protection quality certificates issued before the law takes effect remain valid until their stated expiration dates.

The **Minister of Public Security** is the unnamed government minister heading the Ministry of Public Security. Under the cited legislation, including Law 36/2024/QH15, the minister is assigned a broad range of regulatory responsibilities concerning road traffic and the Ministry’s personnel and operations.

These responsibilities include prescribing details for specified provisions, including Clause 3 of Article 58, Clause 2 of Article 81, Clause 3 of Article 11, Article 74, and Article 84. The minister also prescribes other types of vehicle registration plates and procedures for issuing and revoking designated vehicle registration certificates and plates, except where Article 39 provides otherwise.

The minister regulates driver-licence examinations and the issuance and use of driving licences and international driving permits, including their formats and issuance procedures. The minister also sets examination procedures, requirements for examiners and testing facilities, and rules for licences, driver training, examinations, and age requirements for police forces performing security or national-security duties.

Additional duties include prescribing the form, content, and curriculum for road-traffic-law training and standards for relevant training institutions; setting inspection procedures and technical-safety and environmental-quality certification requirements for vehicles managed by the Ministry of Public Security; and regulating procedures for investigating and resolving road-traffic accidents. Under Article 65, the minister specifies certain provisions and establishes procedures for traffic patrol, control, and violation handling.

The minister also sets rules for police escorts accompanying domestic delegations and foreign guests visiting Vietnam. In relation to traffic technology, the minister issues national technical regulations and prescribes rules for the construction, management, operation, and use of traffic command centers and specified road-traffic monitoring and technical systems. No individual minister’s name is provided.

**STOPPING AND PARKING** refers to the stopping or parking of road vehicles as regulated by Article 18 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. Drivers must signal to other road users when entering or leaving a stopping or parking position, and must not stop or park in ways or locations that obscure road signs or traffic signals, obstruct road users, or endanger people or traffic.

If a technical incident or another force majeure circumstance requires a vehicle to stop or park partly on the roadway or in a place where parking is prohibited, the driver must use the hazard lights or place a warning sign behind the vehicle.
A FORCE MAJEURE CIRCUMSTANCE is an unavoidable circumstance other than a technical incident or failure that may compel a driver to stop or park a vehicle in a road tunnel.

The use of vehicle horn signals refers to the use of horns by vehicles participating in road traffic, as addressed in Article 21 of Law 36/2024/QH15. Under that provision, horn signals may be used only in specified cases, including to warn other road users when a situation may compromise traffic safety.
“PARKING A VEHICLE” refers to the act of leaving a vehicle stationary. Article 18, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15 addresses this conduct and prohibits parking on the left side of a one-way road.

Agencies and organizations are subject to restrictions covering their vehicle access roads, entrance and exit gates, and nearby areas. They may also submit an application dossier to obtain a new permit or license to use signal devices on priority vehicles.

The **RIGHT EDGE OF THE ROAD** is the right-hand boundary of the roadway in the direction a person is traveling. Drivers should stop or park close to it when the shoulder is narrow or absent. Pedestrians should walk close to it when no sidewalk, road shoulder, or pedestrian-only road is available.

“STOPPING A VEHICLE” means bringing a vehicle to a stop on a road, as addressed by Article 18, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The cited provision prohibits stopping a vehicle on the left side of a one-way road.

A **ROAD VEHICLE DRIVER** is a person operating a vehicle that participates in road traffic. The driver is subject to restrictions on stopping or parking in specified locations. If the vehicle is parked in a hazardous or prohibited location under the stated circumstances, the driver must warn other road users. If the driver violates the applicable restrictions, they are required to pay the cost of moving or arranging the movement of the vehicle.

FERRY AND PONTOON BRIDGE CROSSING is the regulated road-traffic activity addressed by Article 23 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The article sets a descending order of priority for vehicles crossing by ferry or pontoon bridge, including vehicles carrying fresh food as a priority category. Under Clause 3, when vehicles descend onto, travel on, or leave a ferry, people may not remain inside them, except for the driver and specified groups of people.
“CROSSING A PONTOON BRIDGE” refers to a road-traffic activity addressed by Article 23 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The article references it alongside crossing by ferry.

PONTOON BRIDGE CROSSING is covered by Article 23. Road users must follow the traffic controller’s instructions. Under Clause 4, motor vehicles and motorcycles intended for specialized use must cross in a single line in their direction of travel and must not obstruct people or vehicles moving in the opposite direction.
FERRY CROSSING refers to the act of crossing by ferry. It is identified in Article 23 as a subject of traffic rules, whose heading covers ferry and pontoon-bridge crossings.
RESCUE AND RELIEF DUTY involves carrying out rescue or relief operations. Vehicles assigned to this duty are designated priority vehicles and are eligible to use priority-vehicle signal equipment.

URGENT DUTY refers to an urgent or emergency assignment performed by military, police, or procuratorial forces. It may also describe a task that members of the People’s Armed Forces are traveling to carry out under a stated exception. Vehicles used by military, police, and procuratorial forces on urgent-duty assignments are covered by the regulation governing priority signal lights.

EMERGENCY MEDICAL RESPONSE is an emergency medical assignment or mission carried out by an ambulance. During the response, the ambulance uses red flashing priority lights and is granted priority at intersections under Article 27, Clause 2 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

The State, specifically the Vietnamese State, is the public authority responsible for managing road traffic order and safety. Its responsibilities include developing, issuing, and implementing related policies, strategies, programs, plans, schemes, and projects. The policies described in Article 4 address matters such as vehicle development, transport safety, environmental protection, and clean energy.

The State is also responsible for supporting the capacity of forces tasked with maintaining road traffic order and safety by ensuring funding, facilities, modern equipment, and other necessary conditions. Its policy includes modernizing traffic command centers and enabling relevant government agencies to connect and share road traffic order and safety data.

The State’s interests must not be infringed through the abuse of road traffic order and safety duties or through the misuse of accident investigations and resolutions. It may also provide or guarantee funding for organizations and individuals conducting public-awareness activities, though such funding is not guaranteed in every case.

A **FUNERAL PROCESSION** is a category of priority-vehicle convoy. However, under the cited provision, funeral processions are expressly excluded from the vehicle groups eligible to have priority-vehicle signal devices installed.

FIREFIGHTING DUTY is an assignment or operation to respond to and extinguish fires. It may be carried out by the Fire Prevention, Fighting and Rescue Police or by other mobilized forces. During the duty, their designated fire engines or fire trucks may operate as priority vehicles and use flashing red priority lights.

**Opening a Vehicle Door** is permitted under Article 19 only when the vehicle has stopped or is parked. Before opening the door, the person must check the front, rear, and door-side areas and determine that it is safe. The door must not be opened or left open when doing so would be unsafe.

**Police Forces** are Vietnamese forces performing national security, national defence, and security duties. Their members’ driving licences—including licence formats, issuance, and use—are governed by regulations prescribed by the Minister of Public Security and, where applicable, the relevant ministers. The Minister of Public Security also prescribes applicable driver-age requirements.

Police members performing these duties are covered by provisions on driver training, driving tests, and certification, including specialized training, testing, and certification for motorcycle operators. A driver examination centre may organize examinations under the stated exception.

Police vehicles are designated priority vehicles when used for urgent duties and may use priority signal devices when responding to emergencies. Police-force vehicle-inspection data, and data relating to driver training, licensing, road-traffic-law certificates, and vehicle operators, are excluded from the specified databases and responsibilities assigned to the Ministries of Transport and Construction.

OTHER MOBILIZED FORCES are forces other than the Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Rescue Police whose fire engines may be mobilized to carry out firefighting duties. Under the decree, their fire trucks use a red flashing light and a priority siren.

EPIDEMIC RESPONSE refers to duties and operations carried out to address epidemics, disease outbreaks, and related incidents. Vehicles assigned to this work may be designated as priority vehicles and are eligible to use priority-vehicle signalling equipment, including flashing blue lights, as provided for under the applicable decree.

NATURAL DISASTER RESPONSE is the work and duty of responding to and addressing incidents caused by natural disasters. Vehicles assigned to or performing this work may be designated as priority vehicles and are eligible to use priority-vehicle signal equipment.

**Military Forces** refers to the Vietnamese armed forces and personnel performing national-defense duties. Their driver training, examinations, certification, and driving licences are subject to special provisions: the relevant procedures and licence formats are prescribed by the Minister of National Defense, including applicable driver age requirements. Driver examination centers may conduct examinations under the stated exception, and military personnel may also be covered by training, testing, and certification rules for specialized motorcycle operators.

Military forces may operate or own priority vehicles used for emergency or urgent duties. Those vehicles may be equipped with or use priority signal devices, including red flashing lights, as provided by the applicable rules. However, military vehicles undertaking such missions are excluded from the permit-granting, reissuance, or revocation authority specified in Article 23. Transitional provisions address existing signal-device permits that do not comply with the relevant decree.

Military vehicle-inspection information, along with specified data concerning military driver training, licensing, vehicle operators, and road-traffic-law certificates, is excluded from the database responsibilities assigned to the Ministry of Transport or the Ministry of Construction.
DIKE PROTECTION DUTY is an official duty performed by designated vehicles to protect dikes. Vehicles assigned to this duty are eligible to use priority-vehicle signal equipment.

The police are an organization whose vehicles may receive priority when performing emergency missions or other urgent duties, and may be equipped with priority signal lights as provided by the cited regulation. Under Clause 3 of Article 40 of Law 36/2024/QH15, police motor vehicles used for security purposes are exempt from the service-life limit.
PROCURACY vehicles are entitled to priority when performing emergency or other urgent duties. During these duties, they must use the legally prescribed priority signals: flashing blue and red lights.

**Rescue and Relief Operations** are emergency duties involving rescue, relief, and the remediation of incidents. The listed missions qualify as uses of priority-vehicle signal devices, including flashing blue lights under the decree. They may be performed by vehicles generally, including military vehicles.
A natural disaster is an event that can create unsafe conditions for road traffic and require vehicles to carry out emergency response and remediation duties.
Elderly and frail people participating in road traffic are identified as a subject covered by Article 30 of Law 36/2024/QH15.
Elderly people, including frail people, are identified in the heading of Article 30 as a group participating in road traffic.

**EMERGENCY DUTY** is a legally defined urgent official mission carried out by vehicles of the military, police, or procuracy forces. Such missions may include arrests, searches, investigative activities, and other urgent assigned tasks. Vehicles performing emergency duty are treated as priority vehicles and are covered by rules on priority-signal devices, including the use of flashing blue and red lights where specified.
Elderly or frail people are recognized as a group participating in road traffic. Their participation is addressed under Article 30, including clause 2, and they should be helped when crossing a road.
People Lacking Civil Act Capacity are individuals who lack or have lost civil act capacity and participate in road traffic. Their participation is addressed in Article 30, including clause 2.
RESCUE OPERATIONS are rescue and relief duties carried out by designated vehicles, with traffic police participating in these operations.

Article 53 of Law 36/2024/QH15 concerns road traffic order and safety for vehicles transporting oversized or overweight cargo. It permits certain vehicles and specialized trailers to be coupled into combinations for that purpose. Clause 3 of Article 53 is cited as an exception to the towing rule in Article 29.
MOTORCYCLE AND MOPED PASSENGERS are people carried on motorcycles or mopeds. They are mentioned in the title and subject of Article 33, which also addresses drivers and cargo.
Clause 1 of Article 35 sets the conditions that intelligent transport vehicles must satisfy.

Persons lacking civil act capacity are identified in the heading of Article 30 as a group participating in road traffic. When travelling on a road, they must be accompanied by someone who can guide them.

A **MOTORCYCLE DRIVER** is a person operating a two-wheeled or three-wheeled motorcycle, motorbike, or moped. The driver is subject to the restrictions in Article 33 and must not engage in specified unsafe towing, carrying, or loading practices. An exception referenced in Article 56(1) applies to the driver where relevant, subject to the requirements set out in Article 56(4).

International organizations and their representative agencies in Vietnam are covered by the stated vehicle-plate provisions. Their administrative and technical staff may hold official identity cards, and their vehicles may use “CV” license plates. The provisions also apply to the organizations’ representative agencies and foreign employees.

Diplomatic representative agencies in Vietnam may have vehicles registered with “NG” license plates, which feature a white background, red lettering, and black numbers. They may also issue a diplomatic note requesting permission for a foreign vehicle to participate in traffic and explaining the reason for the request. The agencies’ administrative-technical staff may hold official identity cards and use vehicles bearing “CV” license plates.

**Disaster Response** includes operations to address natural-disaster incidents and remediate their consequences. It is a qualifying mission for use of a priority-vehicle signal device, and vehicles performing these duties are listed as priorities.

Article 55 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 governs road traffic order and safety requirements for certain foreign vehicles operating in Vietnam. It covers foreign-registered right-hand-drive cars and other foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam by foreign visitors for tourism. Article 35 also cites Article 55 as governing foreign-plated vehicles operating in the country.

FOREIGN ORGANIZATIONS may be issued license plates for their vehicles featuring a white background, black characters and numbers, and the “NN” symbol, except for the subjects specified in point g. They may also arrange for right-hand-drive cars to participate in road traffic in Vietnam for purposes other than tourism, subject to the applicable approval procedure.

A transfer, exchange, gift, or inheritance of a vehicle with an auction-winning plate is a vehicle transaction described in Article 37 that occurs after the vehicle has been assigned the plate. This transaction is an exception to the general rule that the plate is recalled after the five-year retention period: when the vehicle is transferred, exchanged, gifted, or inherited together with its auction-winning plate, the plate is not recalled under that rule.

Foreign individuals may be issued license plates for their vehicles with a white background, black characters and numbers, and the symbol “NN,” except for those specified in point g. For foreign individuals’ temporarily imported vehicles, the registration certificate and license plates are subject to revocation if the vehicle is re-exported, transferred to a new owner, or destroyed.

Consular agencies in Vietnam may be involved in road-traffic matters concerning their personnel and vehicles. They may request permission for a foreign vehicle to participate in traffic by issuing a diplomatic note that states the reason for the request. Their vehicles may receive license plates marked “NG,” with a white background, red lettering, and black numbers. Administrative-technical staff of consular agencies may hold official identity cards and use vehicles bearing “CV” plates. Consular agencies are also among the bodies to be notified about legal violations or traffic accidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles, and their personnel or vehicles may themselves be involved in road accidents.

Representative Agencies of International Organizations are agencies representing international organizations in Vietnam. Their personnel and vehicles may be involved in road traffic accidents, and vehicles belonging to these agencies are issued vehicle plates bearing the “QT” symbol.

The Vehicle Registration and Management System is the system in which vehicle registration data is recorded and managed. It provides data for intelligent transport vehicle operating permit applications and is consulted by the competent authority when processing those applications. Vehicle license plates not selected for auction are also transferred to the system for registration in accordance with the law.

A **VEHICLE LICENSE PLATE AUCTION WINNER** is a person who wins an auction for a vehicle license plate. Under Article 38, the winner has rights and obligations, including the right to transfer, exchange, give away, or bequeath the vehicle associated with the plate, and is subject to the obligations set out in Clause 2 of that article.

The **WINNING BIDDER** is the person determined to have won a vehicle license plate auction. This may be the sole person who registers for or participates in the auction, or the only person who bids at least the starting price. The winning bidder must pay the winning bid and may register a vehicle to use the auctioned plate within the applicable deadline. If they fail to register a vehicle in time, the plate may be auctioned again or transferred to the vehicle registration and management system, and the bid payment is not refunded.

“Other organizations” refers to entities distinct from the former vehicle owner that may receive a license plate from the plate pool after it has been recalled. It also includes organizations that may bring right-hand-drive vehicles into traffic in Vietnam for purposes other than tourism, although approval may be refused following a violation.

An **HEIR** is a person entitled under inheritance law to receive the full amount paid by the winning bidder at an auction if the bidder dies within the specified period and before registering a vehicle to which the auctioned plate is to be attached.

The **WINNER OF A VEHICLE LICENSE PLATE AUCTION** is the person who wins the auction and is subject to the rights and obligations addressed in Article 38. The winner must pay the full winning bid within 30 days after being notified. If the winner fails to pay in full, they forfeit the deposit and any amount already paid and are barred from participating in vehicle license plate auctions for 12 months from the notification date.

Article 38 of Law 36/2024/QH15 sets out the rights and obligations of people who win vehicle license plate auctions. Point d of Clause 1 is also referenced as an additional rule for certain auction cases in which confirmation of the winning bid has not been issued.

The POLICE FORCE operates priority vehicles on urgent or emergency missions. When performing these duties, its vehicles are subject to rules governing the installation and use of legally prescribed priority-vehicle signals, including flashing blue and red lights and a priority siren.

“REVOCATION OF VEHICLE REGISTRATION CERTIFICATES AND LICENSE PLATES” is the administrative action addressed in Article 39 of Law 36/2024/QH15, including Clause 6. It concerns revoking registration certificates and license plates for motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles participating in road traffic, particularly vehicles that have reached the end of their service life or are damaged beyond use.

The issuance of vehicle registration certificates and license plates is the administrative process of issuing new registration certificates and license plates for motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles used in road traffic. As referenced in Article 39 of Law 36/2024/QH15, the issuance must comply with the specified conditions.

The administrative process titled **“Issuance and Revocation of Vehicle Registration Certificates and License Plates”** is addressed in Article 39 of Law 36/2024/QH15. It covers the issuance and revocation of registration certificates and license plates for motor vehicles and specialized or special-use motorcycles participating in road traffic, including vehicles managed by the Ministry of National Defense.

The **cancellation of the auction result** applies when the winning bidder dies within the prescribed period before completing the required vehicle-registration steps. The descriptions identify two relevant deadlines: death within 12 months without registering the vehicle to attach the plate, and death within 30 days before receiving the confirmation decision. The applicable deadline depends on the stage or rule governing the case.

**VEHICLE REGISTRATION AND LICENSE PLATE REVOCATION** is the procedure under Clause 6 of Article 39 of Law 36/2024/QH15 for revoking the registration certificate and license plate of a motor vehicle or specialized vehicle used in road traffic. It applies in specified circumstances, including when a vehicle has been discarded or lost and cannot be found, provided the owner requests revocation. A revocation certificate is also required in the stated circumstances involving a change of ownership.

A **vehicle license plate auction** is the process by which vehicle plates are offered for bidding, including plates for cars, motorcycles, and mopeds. In Vietnam, the auction is addressed in Article 37 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, with its rules and procedures to be specified by the Government. The stated starting prices are at least 40 million đồng for a car plate and 5 million đồng for a motorcycle or moped plate, and the advance deposit must be no lower than the starting price for the plate type. If only one person registers, participates, or bids at least the starting price, that person is deemed the winner.

The winning individual or organization must pay the full winning bid within 30 days after being notified of the result; that payment excludes vehicle-registration and plate-issuance fees. The winner may receive confirmation of the plate after paying in full and must complete vehicle registration to use it. The winner’s rights and obligations are addressed in Article 38. Restrictions also apply to transferring, exchanging, gifting, or bequeathing an auctioned plate, subject to a specified exception. Plates not selected for auction registration are transferred to the vehicle registration and management system for registration under the law.

After auction-organization, advertising, and system-administration costs are deducted, the proceeds are paid into the central budget under state-budget law. The proceeds paid into the state budget are identified as a funding source for the database and for the road-traffic-law knowledge test.

QUALITY INSPECTION is the inspection of measures and standards that ensure the technical safety and environmental protection quality of specified motor-vehicle parts, products, and goods handled by establishments that import, manufacture, or assemble them.
A port is a location that may serve as either the origin or destination for transporting certain vehicles to their place of use under the conditions of the applicable permit and law.

The **Ministry of National Defense** is a Vietnamese government ministry responsible for managing road vehicles and their drivers within its assigned scope, including military and specialized vehicles. Its minister prescribes or jointly regulates relevant procedures and standards, including vehicle registration and license plates, technical requirements for certain plate categories, vehicle certification and technical-safety and environmental inspections, and driving tests, training, and licenses for military personnel performing national-defense or security duties. The ministry also issues driving licenses that may be exchanged or reissued when requested or when a holder no longer performs national-defense duties.

Within its remit, the ministry manages specialized databases, including information on vehicle registration and inspection, driver training and licensing, vehicle operators, road accidents, and administrative violations. Its database is connected to the road traffic order and safety database. The ministry’s functional units manage signal-emitting equipment on priority vehicles and issue or revoke permits for that equipment. The Department of Military Vehicles and Transport, which is part of the ministry, issues permits for intelligent transport vehicles used for defense purposes.

The ministry also participates in interagency coordination. It coordinates with the Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Construction on activities involving foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam, and with the Ministry of Public Security on procedures for temporarily importing and re-exporting foreign motor vehicles. Relevant ministry units receive approval documents or copies of them to support coordination and management. The ministry is also to be notified of specified legal violations, traffic accidents, and incidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam.

VEHICLE OWNERSHIP TRANSFER is a circumstance that may result in the revocation of a vehicle’s registration certificate and license plate. This applies to vehicles generally, including imported and temporarily imported vehicles.

Article 42 of Law 36/2024/QH15 addresses technical safety and environmental protection requirements for motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles participating in road traffic. Paragraph 5 assigns the Minister of Transport authority to prescribe procedures for inspecting emissions from motorcycles and mopeds.

TECHNICAL SAFETY AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION CERTIFICATION is a process for assessing and certifying the technical safety and environmental protection quality of motor vehicles, specialized motor vehicles or motorcycles, and motor vehicle parts that are imported, manufactured, or assembled. It also covers the energy consumption of motor vehicles.

**Người điều khiển xe máy chuyên dùng** là người vận hành xe máy chuyên dùng. Trách nhiệm của nhóm này được đề cập tại Điều 43; họ có thể được đào tạo về pháp luật giao thông đường bộ và được cấp chứng chỉ nếu đạt yêu cầu kiểm tra.

The **Minister of National Defense** is the ministerial office responsible for regulating aspects of military driving and vehicles managed by the Ministry of National Defense. The Minister may prescribe driving tests, driver training, and driver-age requirements for military forces performing national defense duties. The Minister also prescribes the form, content, and program of road-traffic-law training, as well as standards for the relevant training institutions.

For vehicles within the Ministry’s management scope, the Minister prescribes inspection procedures and requirements for technical-safety and environmental-quality certification, along with the procedures for issuing and revoking vehicle registration certificates and license plates. The Minister also regulates the format, issuance procedures, and use of driving licenses for military forces performing national defense duties jointly with the Minister of Public Security. The individual officeholder is not named.

PASSENGER AND GOODS TRANSPORT BY MOTORCYCLES, MOPEDS, AND RUDIMENTARY VEHICLES refers to the road-transport activity covered by Article 47 of Law 36/2024/QH15. It involves using motorcycles, mopeds, or rudimentary vehicles to carry passengers or goods and is subject to the article’s specified road-safety requirements.

A **MOTOR VEHICLE OWNER** is a person who owns a motor vehicle, including a specialized motor vehicle. The owner is subject to the responsibilities set out in Article 43 and the relevant legal passage, including responsibilities that may arise when a road traffic accident occurs. The law also identifies the owner in connection with administrative-violation requirements and possible falsification of vehicle documents.

“TEMPORARY SUSPENSION OF OPERATIONS” refers to the procedure for temporarily suspending the operations of a motor vehicle inspection establishment or a motorcycle and moped emissions-inspection establishment.

The Traffic Police Agency of Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security receives prompt notice about permitted dangerous-goods transport and about vehicles carrying oversized or overweight cargo. For oversized or overweight loads, it helps direct and control traffic, inspect and enforce compliance, and maintain road order and safety.

PASSENGER TRANSPORT BY AUTOMOBILE is the activity addressed by Article 45(1). It must comply with applicable legal requirements and limits, including rules for road-traffic order and safety. Transport must follow the registered schedule and route, except in cases of force majeure.

The **COMPETENT STATE AGENCY** is a state agency authorized to require the resolution of administrative violation cases involving road traffic order and safety. It also has authority to investigate and resolve road traffic accidents and to consent to the burial of a deceased person.

TRANSPORT OF FRESH FOOD refers to the road transport of fresh food. It is subject to Article 50’s provisions on traffic order and road-vehicle safety, including the requirements in Clause 2. Drivers must carry all documents required by law.

GOODS TRANSPORT BY AUTOMOBILE is addressed by Article 49, which requires goods to be neatly arranged and securely fastened to ensure safety. When goods extend beyond the vehicle, drivers must also use warning signals.

ONBOARD SERVICE PERSONNEL are service staff working on vehicles used to transport passengers. They share responsibility for guiding passengers and requiring and checking that people aboard comply with the applicable rules. Under Article 45, Clause 2 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, personnel on passenger-transport automobiles are also responsible for checking that luggage and goods are arranged and secured safely.

SERVICE STAFF are personnel serving on passenger-transport cars. They must follow applicable road traffic rules and share responsibility for instructing passengers on road safety and emergency evacuation procedures.

Article 49 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 sets road traffic order and safety requirements for automobiles transporting goods. It requires loose cargo, construction materials, and waste to be secured or covered to prevent spills and reduce noise and dust, with the load kept at least 10 centimeters below the top edge of the vehicle body. When cargo extends beyond the front or rear of a vehicle, drivers must use red warning signals during the day and lights or other signals at night or in darkness.

OVERSIZED AND OVERWEIGHT CARGO TRANSPORT is the movement by vehicle of cargo that exceeds standard size or weight limits, particularly on public roads. The vehicles used must be suitable for the cargo, and the transport must comply with applicable road traffic order and safety requirements. In Vietnam, this activity is addressed under Article 53 of Law 36/2024/QH15.
