Article 56 of Law 36/2024/QH15 sets out the conditions required of people operating vehicles in road traffic. Clause 2 specifically establishes requirements for operators of specialized motorcycles participating in road traffic.

**EMERGENCY DUTIES** are urgent assignments performed in emergency circumstances. Depending on the applicable legal provisions, they may justify allowing oversized or overweight vehicles to travel on roads. Duties carried out during a legally defined state of emergency may also qualify priority vehicles to use flashing blue lights, while urgent police duties may qualify police vehicles to use priority-vehicle signal equipment.

Foreign visitors are foreign nationals traveling to Vietnam for tourism who may bring foreign-registered motor vehicles into the country under the applicable regulatory procedure. Their trips must be organized through a Vietnamese international travel service enterprise and are subject to the required approval process. The regulations also address visitors’ departure timing and the permitted duration of their stay.

CẢNH SÁT GIAO THÔNG (the Traffic Police) is responsible for patrol and control duties concerning road traffic order and safety, including organizing traffic control and directing traffic. In carrying out these duties, the force may use systems, vehicles, equipment, data, weapons, and support tools as authorized by law. It also handles legal violations involving oversized or overweight vehicles and tracked vehicles operating on roads, and manages, operates, and uses the nationwide road traffic order and safety database. People and organizations mobilized by the Traffic Police must comply with its decisions and requests. In urgent situations, the on-scene commander may request assistance from foreign organizations or individuals.

BỘ CÔNG AN (BCA) is Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security. The “BCA” designation appears in references to Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA and Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA; the minister is identified as the issuer of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. The Traffic Police Department operates under the Ministry and is associated with the dossier-submission channel. The Ministry is also responsible for receiving reports of difficulties or obstacles arising during implementation of the circulars and providing timely guidance. Relevant authorities are to notify its traffic police agency of authorized movements by oversized, overweight, or tracked vehicles.

DRIVER’S LICENSE REVOCATION is the legally specified action under Clause 5, Article 62 of Law 36/2024/QH15. A driver’s license is revoked if it was issued contrary to regulations or if its holder used deception to obtain, exchange, or have it reissued.

DRIVING TEST EXAMINERS are people who conduct car-driving tests and may supervise a vehicle’s steering while learners or candidates participate in road traffic. They must carry the documents specified in Article 56(1). The Minister of Transport prescribes their qualifications and standards, organizes their training, and provides for the issuance of examiner cards.

Article 56 of Vietnam’s Law 36/2024/QH15 establishes the conditions people must meet to operate vehicles in road traffic, including requirements related to age, health, and possession of a valid driving licence.

Article 52 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 sets out road traffic order and safety requirements for oversized vehicles, overweight vehicles, and tracked (crawler) vehicles operating on roads. It includes a definition of an overweight vehicle and addresses the conditions and safeguards applicable when these vehicles are permitted to travel.

The article requires protection of road infrastructure, including measures to protect the road surface when tracked vehicles use roads. Organizations and individuals operating the vehicles must bear the full costs of any required surveying, design, and reinforcement of road infrastructure. Clause 4 addresses infrastructure protection and compensation for damage caused by such vehicles.

FOREIGNERS are foreign nationals who bring and operate foreign motor vehicles on Vietnam’s roads for tourism under an approved arrangement, as described in Article 55 of Law 36/2024/QH15. A Vietnamese international travel-service business may organize their entry and travel. They must follow applicable entry and exit procedures, adhere to the registered program and itinerary, and declare temporary residence as required by law. The relevant decree addresses their departure timing and permitted period of stay; violations of Vietnamese law may result in suspension of the arrangement.

Article 57 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 governs driving licences in Vietnam. It sets out the licence categories and the vehicles their holders may operate, including categories C, C1E, and D. The article also addresses licences for people with disabilities, prescribed licence forms, issuance procedures and use, and the use of licences by military and police personnel performing defence or security duties. It establishes rules on licence validity, including specified circumstances in which a licence is invalid, and Clause 8 covers requirements for international driving permits.

The **LICENSING AUTHORITY** is the competent public authority responsible for receiving, reviewing, and deciding applications for various permits and licenses. Its responsibilities include issuing, replacing, renewing, or reissuing permits for signal devices on priority vehicles and operating permits for smart or intelligent traffic vehicles. It may also revoke permits where applicable.

In processing applications, the authority checks submitted documents and, for intelligent-vehicle permits, may verify vehicle registration details against the application. It notifies applicants when submissions are incomplete, inaccurate, insufficient, or otherwise ineligible, and may request supplemental documents or issue a written refusal. Qualifying applications submitted in person are accepted. Replacement or reissued smart-traffic-vehicle operating permits are issued within two working days of receiving the application.

The LICENSING AUTHORITY also licenses certain foreign vehicles to participate in traffic in Vietnam, including foreign-registered right-hand-drive cars and motor vehicles brought into Vietnam by foreign visitors for tourism. In addition, it issues transport business licenses to transport business units.
Article 62 of Law 36/2024/QH15 concerns the issuance, exchange, reissuance, and revocation of driving licenses.

The Vienna Convention is an international agreement referenced as the basis for recognizing international driving permits issued by its member countries and for identifying which countries’ authorities are authorized to issue those permits.

CƠ SỞ ĐÀO TẠO LÁI XE Ô TÔ are automobile driver-training establishments that must meet conditions prescribed by the Government. They must maintain curricula and lesson plans and deliver training in the required format and according to the prescribed content and program for each driving-licence class. Establishments that meet the relevant qualifications may also provide road-traffic-law training, conduct tests, and issue certificates to those who pass.

The Vietnamese Ministry of Health is responsible for establishing health standards and examination requirements for drivers and operators of specialized motorcycles and other specialized motor vehicles. It regulates periodic health examinations for professional car drivers and determines requirements for assessing alcohol concentration and endogenous alcohol in blood. The Ministry also builds and manages health databases for drivers and operators of specialized vehicles. In addition, its regulations govern ambulance standards and use, as referenced in Article 20 of the decree.

Foreign nationals are people from outside Vietnam who may enter the country with foreign-registered motor vehicles for tourism or travel, including right-hand-drive vehicles, when the trip is arranged by a Vietnamese international travel service business and authorized under the applicable approval process. They may drive those vehicles in Vietnamese traffic only within the approved scope, routes, and travel periods, and must travel in a convoy where required.

Their entry, exit, transit, residence, and driving are subject to applicable documentation, visa, and entry requirements. A Vietnamese organization may need to invite and guarantee them, except where they are visa-exempt. Their permitted driving period is limited by the validity of their visa or visa-exemption period. If an unforeseen incident that cannot be resolved immediately prevents their departure, they may remain for up to 10 additional days under the stated conditions.

Foreign nationals must provide accurate and lawful information and documents and comply with Vietnamese law and the management requirements described in Article 36. Their activities, legal violations, and traffic accidents are subject to the specified management and reporting responsibilities. An approved trip may be suspended if they violate Vietnamese law and have not completed the competent authority’s requirements for resolving the violation. A route or schedule change, or an incident, may also affect or delay their departure.

Competent State Authorities are government bodies with legal authority over the relevant matter. Their responsibilities may include conducting driving tests and handling legal violations or traffic accidents involving foreign visitors or foreign motor vehicles. They may require outstanding violations or incidents to be resolved, and unresolved matters may be grounds for refusing approval. In Vietnam, an authority that previously issued an approval may also suspend the related activity until the violation has been settled.

**DRIVING LICENSE ISSUANCE** is the process by which the responsible driver training, examination, testing, and licensing authority grants a driving license to eligible learners. The license category granted is determined under the category rules specified in Clause 3 of Article 89. Driving license issuance is also one of the matters addressed in Article 62 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15.

Motorcycle Driving Tests are examinations for motorcycle drivers. They may be conducted at driving test centers or at driving practice yards that meet the required facility and technical standards. The law also sets conditions that motorcycle practice grounds must satisfy.
DRIVER'S LICENSE REISSUANCE is the act of issuing a driver’s license again. Deception used to obtain a reissued license is grounds for revocation.

DRIVER’S LICENSE ISSUANCE is the administrative process of granting a driving license. The process may include a theoretical examination using questions to assess an applicant’s knowledge of road traffic law. The term appears alongside the related administrative actions of exchanging, reissuing, and revoking licenses.

**RESTORATION OF 12 DRIVING-LICENSE POINTS** refers to restoring a driver’s license to its full 12 points. The descriptions identify two routes: restoration when the license has not lost all its points and no further points have been deducted for 12 months after the most recent deduction, and restoration after the driver passes the road-traffic rules and safety legal-knowledge examination. The applicable route depends on the relevant provision.

DRIVER'S LICENSE ISSUANCE is the act of issuing a driver’s license. It is listed in a provision’s heading alongside license exchange, reissuance, and revocation. A license may be subject to revocation if it was issued contrary to regulations or obtained through deception.

Article 62 of Vietnam’s Law No. 36/2024/QH15 governs the issuance, exchange, reissuance, and revocation of driving licences. Clause 2 sets out circumstances in which a person may exchange a licence or obtain a replacement, including when they hold a valid foreign driving licence. The article also provides restrictions affecting people with unresolved administrative violations related to road traffic.

CHÍNH PHỦ (the Government of Vietnam) sets the conditions that automotive driver-training establishments must meet and establishes the regulations under which vehicle inspection establishments are organized and operate. It also issues detailed rules for implementing Article 51 on ensuring road traffic order and safety when road vehicles transport dangerous goods. CHÍNH PHỦ is identified as the issuing authority of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP, Decree No. 47/2022/NĐ-CP, and Decree No. 41/2024/NĐ-CP.

The **Ministry of National Defence of Vietnam** is a government ministry with responsibilities spanning military transport, road traffic, and border management. It is designated to receive copies of approval documents so it can coordinate the management of relevant activities; its functional units may also receive those copies. The Ministry coordinates the organization and management of foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam, and works with the Ministry of Finance on procedures for temporarily importing and re-exporting those vehicles. The Ministry of Public Security is required to notify it of specified incidents.

Within its defence remit, the Ministry regulates driving licences for military personnel performing national-defence duties. Its Minister sets requirements for establishments and organizations that train drivers for military forces performing national-defence and security duties, and regulates the issuance, exchange, reissuance, and revocation of licences for those forces. Together with the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry also regulates licences for military and police forces performing national-defence and security duties.

The Ministry manages specialized databases within its area of responsibility, including information on vehicle registration and inspection, driver training and licensing, road traffic accidents, and administrative violations involving road traffic order and safety. Its Minister also sets rules for road inspections concerning internal military regulations, legal compliance by the military control force, and military vehicles. The Ministry is among the authorities empowered to issue, reissue, and revoke permits for signal devices on priority vehicles used by military forces on emergency missions; the Ministry of Public Security’s stated responsibilities for such devices and permits exclude matters within the Ministry of National Defence’s management area.

At border gates under its management, the Ministry organizes exit and entry inspections and controls, conducts border procedures, and issues or modifies visas and temporary-residence certificates. It coordinates with specialized state agencies to supervise vehicles completing temporary-import and re-export procedures. The Ministry includes the **Vehicle-Machinery Department**, which is referenced in connection with permits for intelligent transport vehicles used for defence purposes.

Article 60 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, titled “Driver Training,” addresses the training required to obtain a driving licence or upgrade to another licence category. It provides that applicants must complete theoretical and practical training under the curriculum for the relevant licence class, including upgrade training where applicable. The article also identifies matters concerning driver training to be regulated by the Minister of Construction.

SPECIALIZED MOTORCYCLE OPERATORS are people who operate specialized motorcycles. They are the intended participants in the road traffic law training, testing, and certification described in Article 63, and are also the trainees and certification candidates covered by the relevant provision. Their health information may be included in the driver and specialized motorcycle operator health database.
A DRIVER’S LICENSE EXCHANGE is the act of exchanging a driver’s license, as identified in the relevant provision. A license exchange obtained through deception is grounds for revocation.

The **MEDICAL EXAMINATION AND TREATMENT FACILITY** is a healthcare institution that must be notified promptly in connection with a road traffic accident, including when someone discovers an accident or is present at its scene. Its assessment of a licence holder’s medical fitness may also be relevant to whether that person’s driving licence is revoked.

SPECIALIZED MOTOR VEHICLE OPERATOR TRAINING ESTABLISHMENTS are qualified institutions that train operators of specialized motor vehicles. They provide road-traffic-law knowledge training and examinations, may register applicants for this training, and issue the relevant certificates. The Ministry of Transport sets the standards these establishments must meet.

The Minister of National Defence is the government official responsible for issuing regulations on driving licences for military forces performing national defence duties under Article 62 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The Minister is also authorized to regulate road-based inspections concerning compliance with internal military regulations, the legal compliance of the military control force, and military vehicles.

Road Traffic Patrol and Control Activities are measures intended to maintain order and safety in road traffic. They include detecting, preventing, and handling violations. Addressed in Article 65 of Law 36/2024/QH15, these activities are carried out by designated forces, which must comply with specified principles. The descriptions do not identify the responsible forces or detail those principles.

Legal violations are acts that breach applicable laws. In the road-traffic context, they include violations of road traffic order and safety, as well as other legal violations observed by road vehicle operators during patrol and control activities. They also include violations committed in Vietnam by foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles. Provincial and municipal authorities are required to report such violations to the designated ministries and relevant foreign representative bodies.

ROAD-TRAFFIC PATROL AND CONTROL is the activity conducted by the Traffic Police to maintain and enforce road-traffic order and safety. During these activities, Traffic Police perform their prescribed duties in accordance with Article 65 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15.

The **Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs** is a Vietnamese government ministry assigned responsibilities under Article 8 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP concerning road-traffic education and safety at vocational education institutions. It leads and coordinates the organization of road-traffic-law education, directs institutions to include students’ compliance with traffic laws among the criteria for assessing conduct, and oversees the teaching of relevant legal knowledge and compliance with road-traffic order and safety laws.

The Ministry also leads and directs preparations for safe motorbike-riding instruction for students. In coordination with the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Education and Training, it develops a curriculum and practical guidance materials on safe motorbike-riding skills. In addition, the Minister of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs is responsible for establishing the conditions and procedures for issuing, exchanging, reissuing, and revoking specialized vehicle-operation certificates for tractor operators who hold specified driving licences.

ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY PATROL AND CONTROL ACTIVITIES are activities under Article 65 of Vietnam’s Law No. 36/2024/QH15. They involve deploying personnel and vehicles to patrol and control road traffic, including inspecting and controlling people and vehicles participating in traffic, with the aim of maintaining road traffic order and safety. Article 65 introduces the forms these activities may take, but the descriptions provided do not specify those forms.

Article 65 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 governs patrol and control activities related to road traffic order and safety. It defines these activities as including the detection, prevention, and handling of legal violations. Clause 6 requires the forces responsible for patrol and control to comply with the law and with orders and plans issued by competent authorities.

Article 67 of Law 36/2024/QH15 sets out measures for traffic control and detecting legal violations. Its clauses 1–4 identify the systems, vehicles, equipment, and data that may be used for these purposes, including surveillance systems and traffic cameras; technical equipment for inspecting and controlling motor-vehicle loads; vehicle-monitoring data; images of drivers or passenger compartments; and data from vehicle-weight control facilities.

**OTHER LEGAL VIOLATIONS** are violations of laws other than those concerning road-traffic order and safety. The force is required to combat and prevent these violations, vehicle operators are required to help detect, prevent, and address them, and the Traffic Police may address them as authorized by law.

ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY PATROL AND CONTROL is the regulated activity addressed in Article 65, clause 6 of Law 36/2024/QH15. It is carried out by designated forces and, when necessary, by other mobilized forces and units in coordination with the Traffic Police. Forces performing these duties must respect and protect the lawful rights and interests of agencies, organizations, and individuals.

PATROL AND CONTROL FORCES are responsible for patrolling and controlling road traffic order and safety. They are authorized to issue vehicle stop orders and make inspection or control requests while carrying out these duties. They must comply with applicable laws and with patrol and control orders and plans issued by competent authorities, follow the principles governing their work, and accept legal responsibility for their decisions and actions.

An **URGENT SITUATION** is an emergency circumstance in which the traffic police commander at the scene may mobilize civilian people, vehicles, and equipment. All mobilized resources must be returned immediately when the emergency circumstance ends.

The PATROL AND CONTROL FORCE consists of the personnel responsible for carrying out patrol and control duties, including road traffic order and safety patrols. In performing these duties, the force is required to follow the principles stated in the text.

**ROAD TRAFFIC PATROL AND CONTROL** is the activity carried out by the Traffic Police to maintain order and safety on roads, as addressed principally in Article 65 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. It includes organizing forces to patrol and control directly on road routes, monitoring traffic conditions, road users and vehicles, and security and order along those routes. Traffic Police may use the systems, vehicles, equipment and data specified by law while carrying out their duties and exercising their statutory powers.

The activity also includes coordinating efforts to detect and prevent violations of laws protecting road works and road-safety corridors, following the procedures established for patrol and control, and assisting road users and vehicles when needed. Road vehicle operators may report legal violations that occur during these activities in accordance with the law on denunciations. Article 68 also identifies patrol and control as a duty during which emergency mobilization may occur.
ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT RISK is the risk of a traffic accident arising when a vehicle stops or is parked on a road in violation of applicable rules.

The ROAD MANAGEMENT AGENCY is a public government authority responsible for managing roads and carrying out responsibilities within its functions, duties, and legal powers. It must respond when it discovers or receives information about an unexpected situation covered by Article 76, Clause 1, including situations that disrupt road order or safety. The agency also receives reports, inspects and addresses factors that threaten traffic safety, and informs relevant parties of inspection results.

The ROAD MANAGEMENT AGENCY coordinates with traffic police to detect and prevent violations involving road works and road safety corridors. It also leads efforts to identify the causes of traffic congestion, coordinates with relevant parties, and takes measures within its authority—or recommends action to competent authorities—to prevent, resolve, and remedy congestion.

NATIONAL SECURITY PROTECTION refers to the activity of safeguarding national security. It is cited as a purpose for stopping road traffic vehicles for inspection and control, and as a basis for urgent mobilization under Article 68.

“Movement of a Violating Vehicle” refers to removing or relocating a vehicle that has been stopped or parked in violation of road rules when it obstructs or congests traffic, or poses a risk of causing a road traffic accident.

Article 66 of Law 36/2024/QH15 sets out the grounds on which traffic police may stop road vehicles for inspection and control. These include cases where a competent authority’s patrol and control order or plan requires a vehicle to be stopped to detect a legal violation.

**STOPPING ROAD TRAFFIC VEHICLES FOR INSPECTION AND CONTROL** is a law-enforcement action addressed in Article 66 of Law 36/2024/QH15. It involves stopping a vehicle participating in road traffic so that authorities can inspect and control it. The action may be based on reports, denunciations, feedback, petitions, or proposals concerning crimes or other legal violations.

The **JOURNEY MONITORING AND DRIVER IMAGE DATA MANAGEMENT SYSTEM** is the system identified in Article 71 for managing data collected by journey-monitoring devices and devices that record images of drivers.
MILITARY VEHICLE INSPECTION is a duty involving the inspection of military vehicles, including vehicles operating on roads.

**REMOVAL OF A VIOLATING VEHICLE** is the act of moving a vehicle from a position where it has violated stopping or parking rules. Removal may occur when the driver or owner is absent or fails to comply with traffic police instructions. The police may arrange for another organization or individual to carry out the removal.

Article 71 of Law 36/2024/QH15 governs systems for monitoring road security, public order, and traffic safety. It also addresses the management of data—including journey-monitoring and image-recording data—from vehicle and driver monitoring equipment, and technical equipment used to inspect motor-vehicle loads and weight.

RESCUE AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE includes activities carried out to address emergencies and protect people. It may be a purpose for stopping road traffic vehicles for inspection and control. In response to a road traffic accident, it includes attending the scene, providing first aid, transporting victims, and delivering emergency care and treatment.

The MOTOR VEHICLE WEIGHT INSPECTION TECHNICAL EQUIPMENT SYSTEM is a system of specialized technical equipment used to inspect the weight of motor vehicles. It is provided to the Traffic Police to detect and handle violations of road vehicle-weight regulations and is identified in the heading of Article 71.
Article 72 is a provision of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 concerning the rights and responsibilities of people operating vehicles in road traffic.
A ROAD TRAFFIC OBSTRUCTION is an impediment to the movement of road traffic that may be caused by a vehicle stopped or parked illegally or in violation of applicable rules.

The **Traffic Command Center** is a center for carrying out road-traffic command and control activities. Under Article 75 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, the system comprises national-level and provincial- or centrally governed municipal-level centers. Each center includes technical infrastructure, technology equipment systems, and a database.

Road-security, order, and traffic-safety monitoring systems are required to connect to a Traffic Command Center. Under Clause 4 of Article 75, the centers are permitted to connect to and share data with ministries, sectors, and specified systems and databases.

INSPECTION AND CONTROL refers to checks and control activities carried out by persons performing official duties on road traffic participants and vehicles. These activities are conducted after a vehicle has been stopped, and include the examinations performed, their content and results. Road traffic participants are required to comply with these activities.

The **ROAD TRAFFIC SECURITY, ORDER, AND SAFETY MONITORING SYSTEM**, identified in Article 71 of Law 36/2024/QH15, is installed on road traffic routes in accordance with national technical regulations. It collects vehicle journey signals and other data, audio and images, traffic conditions, and related information to monitor road traffic security, public order, and safety and to detect violations.

The traffic command center may connect to the system and share data with it. Data collected must be managed in accordance with the law and protected against improper use. It may be used to address legal violations and support state management.

“FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH INSPECTION AND CONTROL REQUESTS” refers to conduct addressed by Article 73 in which road traffic participants fail to comply with requests made during an inspection or control.

**RELATED AGENCIES** are agencies other than the road management authority that are involved in traffic congestion management or connected to the relevant data systems. Agencies concerned with congestion coordinate with the traffic police and road management agencies to implement preventive, resolution, and remedial measures. Other related agencies may connect to and share information through the data-management system described in Article 71, including the system for managing journey-monitoring and driver-image data. The descriptions do not identify these agencies individually.
The PROVINCIAL TRAFFIC COMMAND CENTER is a provincial-level component of the traffic command center system. It is included in the system and listed as one of its components in Article 75.
ROAD TRAFFIC PARTICIPANTS are people taking part in road traffic. They are required to comply with inspection and control requests, including requests made by persons performing official duties.

Article 72 of Law 36/2024/QH15 sets out the rights and responsibilities of people operating vehicles in road traffic. It recognizes their right to explain, complain, or sue in relation to relevant administrative decisions or acts, and requires them to obey orders to stop and requests for inspection or control.

**PERSONS PERFORMING OFFICIAL DUTIES** are officials carrying out public duties who are authorized to inspect and control, make requests to road users, and pursue operators of road vehicles who flee. When road users fail to comply with their requests or obstruct their work, these officials may take legally prescribed preventive measures and are protected against obstruction or resistance.

UNEXPECTED ROAD TRAFFIC DISRUPTION is an unexpected situation on a road that disrupts traffic order or threatens traffic safety. Article 76 of Law 36/2024/QH15 addresses the handling of such situations, including those specified in Clause 1.
The NATIONAL TRAFFIC COMMAND CENTER is the national-level component of the traffic command center system.
**OBSTRUCTION OR RESISTANCE AGAINST OFFICIALS** is a violation addressed in Article 73. It involves obstructing or resisting a person while that person is performing official duties.

TEMPORARY TRAFFIC DIVERSION is the temporary allocation or redirection of traffic flows as part of road traffic control. Under Article 77, Clause 3, the Traffic Police Authority is responsible for notifying the relevant parties about the diversion and carrying it out.

ROAD MANAGERS AND USERS are people who manage or use roads. Within the scope of their duties and authority, they share responsibility for receiving reports of road traffic safety hazards, inspecting and addressing those hazards, and notifying the relevant parties of the results.

Article 79 of Law 36/2024/QH15 concerns recommendations on road traffic order and safety in relation to road works. It requires the traffic police authority to address identified risks within its management scope or recommend that the relevant road managers take timely action.

**MINISTRIES AND SECTORS** refers to the Vietnamese government ministries and sectoral bodies responsible, in accordance with law, for building national and specialized databases and connecting and sharing relevant information with the road traffic order and safety database. They agree on the detailed data fields for this information exchange. Under Article 75, Clause 4, of Law 36/2024/QH15, traffic command centers may connect to and share data with these ministries and sectors, subject to the law’s provisions.

RELATED PERSON is an individual identified in the traffic-accident records as connected with the accident. The person is subject to the responsibilities set out in Article 80, including preserving the accident scene and any relevant evidence.

RELATED PERSONS are people connected with a road traffic accident whose responsibilities are addressed in Article 80. The provision’s heading identifies these people as having responsibilities in relation to the accident.

**RELEVANT AGENCIES** are the government bodies concerned with the decree and responsible for its implementation. They include agencies tasked with managing foreign nationals who drive or operate foreign motor vehicles in traffic in Vietnam. They also include agencies that address traffic congestion and coordinate with the road management agency to identify its causes, as well as the agencies assigned relevant responsibilities under Article 36.

The ROAD ADMINISTRATION AGENCY is responsible, within its assigned functions and duties, for responding to unexpected or sudden road-traffic situations that disrupt road order or traffic safety. When it detects such a situation or receives information about it, the agency must take appropriate measures, promptly organize forces to attend the scene, and help restore traffic order and safety. Where damage to road infrastructure is disrupting order or safety, the agency must arrange for it to be remedied promptly.

A **PERSON PRESENT AT THE ACCIDENT SCENE** is a person who is at the location of a road traffic accident and is covered by the responsibilities set out in Article 80. These responsibilities include providing relevant information about the accident when requested by a competent authority.

A ROAD VEHICLE OPERATOR is a person operating a vehicle involved in a road traffic accident that they cause. Under Article 80, the operator has responsibilities at the scene, including helping transport an injured person for emergency care when no other vehicle is available and preserving the positions of the vehicle and victim, along with traces related to the accident.

The **Traffic Police Agency** is responsible for maintaining road traffic order and safety. It plans and directs traffic, handles violations of road traffic order and safety laws, and coordinates measures to prevent, resolve, and remedy traffic congestion.

When roadways or sidewalks are temporarily used for other purposes, the agency performs the responsibilities set out in Article 77. If the activity does not meet required standards, it must temporarily suspend it and recommend that the competent authority adjust the usage plan. Under Article 79 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, it also responds to information about risks to road traffic infrastructure or road works and problems with traffic organization, and is notified of the results of corrective action addressing road safety hazards.

Under Article 84 of the same law, the Traffic Police Agency leads and coordinates the collection of road traffic accident statistics. The competent agency receives relevant information and investigation results to compile those statistics and build a road traffic accident database. Its guidance also informs the timing and conduct of safe motorcycle-riding skills instruction and assessment.
UNEXPECTED ROAD-TRAFFIC DISRUPTION is an unexpected situation on a road that disrupts traffic order and safety. As described in Article 76, it requires action by the relevant authorities.

Relevant organizations are those concerned by the circular and responsible for implementing it. They may report any difficulties or obstacles encountered during implementation. Organizations affected by traffic congestion also coordinate with the road management agency to identify its causes.
INJURED PEOPLE are individuals hurt in a road traffic accident. They may be transported for emergency care, and their statements may be recorded as part of the accident investigation.

**DRIVER CAUSING THE ACCIDENT** is the person operating a road vehicle who causes a road traffic accident. The role is identified in the relevant provision as carrying responsibilities related to the accident. The driver must remain at the scene until the police arrive, except in specified circumstances, and must promptly report the accident to the nearest police agency or People’s Committee.

The deceased person is an individual who died as a result of a road traffic accident. Their identity is unknown, and their whereabouts are not established. The accident scene should remain unchanged, and the body should be covered.

A **PERSON RELATED TO THE ACCIDENT** is someone involved in or otherwise connected with a road traffic accident and subject to responsibilities under Article 80. The provision addresses this person alongside the vehicle operator and others present at the scene. Their responsibilities include stopping, warning others of danger, preserving the scene, assisting injured people, and notifying the nearest relevant authority or facility. They must provide identifying and accident-related information to the competent authority and remain at the scene until the police arrive, except where a specified exception applies; in such cases, they must report promptly as required.

An **ACCIDENT VICTIM** is a person identified in traffic-accident records as having been harmed or injured in a road traffic accident. Depending on the circumstances and the conditions stated in the relevant text, the person may be transported for emergency care.

People Present at the Accident Scene are those who are at the location of a road traffic accident. Under Article 80, they have responsibilities that include promptly reporting the accident to the nearest relevant authority or facility and helping protect the injured person’s property.

A **ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT REPORT** is a report or notification that a road traffic accident has occurred. It may be received by the responsible police agency, which must respond and take appropriate action; by an insurance enterprise, triggering its duty to send a person or authorized representative to the scene; or, under Article 81 of Law 36/2024/QH15, by the nearest People’s Committee as a report or tip-off.

A **criminal offense** may be indicated by the circumstances of a road traffic accident. The indication does not by itself establish that an offense occurred; when signs of a criminal offense are present, the accident is investigated and handled under criminal law and criminal procedure law.

Road traffic accident victims are people injured in road traffic accidents who may require assistance, first aid, transport, emergency care, and medical treatment. Those who visit medical examination or treatment facilities for care are included in the statistics reported to the traffic police.

Article 59 of Law 36/2024/QH15 sets out age and health requirements for people operating vehicles in road traffic. It establishes minimum-age requirements for eligibility for specified driving licence classes and for a certificate to operate specialized motorcycles, and includes maximum-age requirements for drivers of certain passenger vehicles. Its requirements are also referenced in connection with registration for driving tests.
Rescue and Relief refers to the response activities covered by Article 82 when a road traffic accident occurs, including rescue and relief duties performed by police vehicles.

**RELATED AGENCIES AND ORGANIZATIONS** refers to the agencies and organizations concerned with implementing the circular, as well as those involved in responding to road traffic accidents. In accident rescue and relief operations, these organizations coordinate with the police agency.

Diplomatic Missions are foreign diplomatic representative bodies in Vietnam. Their personnel and vehicles may be involved in road traffic accidents in the country. Foreign diplomatic missions may also be notified about legal violations or traffic accidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles.

The effective date of Law 36/2024/QH15 is January 1, 2025, except as otherwise provided in Clause 2 of Article 88. This date also marks the cutoff for transitional rules concerning driving licences issued before the law takes effect.

**Investigation and Resolution of Road Traffic Accidents** is part of the state management of road traffic order and safety and is addressed in Article 83 of Vietnam’s Law No. 36/2024/QH15. The process must be carried out promptly, accurately, objectively, and in accordance with the law, without being misused or abused to infringe the State’s interests or the lawful rights and interests of organizations or individuals.

The applicable procedure depends on whether the accident shows signs of a criminal offense. If it does, the case is handled under criminal law and criminal procedure law. Where criminal signs have not been determined, the investigation and resolution proceed under the applicable non-criminal rules, which may include recording statements from drivers, injured people, witnesses, and others involved, as well as detention of vehicles and related items as provided by law.

Resolution 73/2022/QH15 is a resolution of Vietnam’s National Assembly establishing a pilot auction of automobile license plates. It ceased to be effective when Law 36/2024/QH15 took effect, except as provided in Clause 7 of Article 89 of that law, which governs the continued handling of certain auctions that began before the law took effect.
STATE MANAGEMENT OF ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY is the state-management activity addressed by Article 86 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

**ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION AND RESOLUTION** is the process by which an investigative agency examines and resolves a road traffic accident. Under Article 83 of Law 36/2024/QH15, including Clause 2, the process establishes the events, damage, causes, fault, and directly related conditions. It includes examining injuries and checking the vehicles, drivers, passengers, cargo, and relevant documents, as well as determining whether the accident shows signs of a criminal offense and checking involved drivers for alcohol, drugs, or other prohibited stimulants. The applicable procedures depend on whether there are signs of a criminal offense. The Minister of Public Security prescribes the procedures that Traffic Police must follow.
Article 87 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 sets out responsibilities for the state management of road traffic order and safety, including responsibilities assigned to the Ministry of Construction.

QUỸ GIẢM THIỂU THIỆT HẠI TAI NẠN GIAO THÔNG ĐƯỜNG BỘ (the Road Traffic Accident Damage Mitigation Fund) is established to reduce the harm caused by road traffic accidents. Article 85 sets out the Fund’s operating principles. It may support activities specified in Clause 3 of that article only when the state budget does not fund them or provides insufficient funding.

The ROAD TRAFFIC LAW KNOWLEDGE CHECK assesses legal knowledge of the laws concerning road traffic order and safety. It is referenced in the scope provisions of the relevant circular, and the competent authority assigns personnel to conduct the check.

Article 86 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 concerns the contents of state management of road traffic order and safety. It covers the issuance and implementation of relevant legal normative documents; inspection and examination; resolution of complaints and denunciations; and the building, training, and development of forces directly responsible for ensuring road traffic order and safety.

Article 89 of Law 36/2024/QH15 sets out transitional provisions related to the law’s commencement. It addresses the status and permitted use of certain driving licences issued before the law takes effect: Clause 2 specifies their continued validity and use, while Clause 3 provides rules for exchanging or reissuing certain previously issued licences. Article 89 also covers driving learners who have not yet taken their tests or received a licence when the law takes effect.

The **ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT DAMAGE MITIGATION FUND**, established under Article 85 of Vietnam’s Law No. 36/2024/QH15, is a central-level state financial fund outside the state budget. It is intended to mobilize social resources to mitigate harm caused by road traffic accidents.

The Fund’s financial sources include support, aid, and voluntary contributions from domestic and foreign organizations and individuals, as well as other sources provided for by law. Under Article 85(3), it may finance support for accident victims and their families, and assistance and emergency care for people injured in road traffic accidents.

The Fund operates on a non-profit basis. It must be managed and used for its proper purposes, lawfully, promptly, effectively, openly, and transparently. The Government is responsible for regulating its establishment, management, and use.

Article 89 of Law 36/2024/QH15 sets out transitional provisions for matters arising before the law took effect. It addresses both driving licences issued before that date and car licence-plate auctions conducted before it. For the auctions, it distinguishes between cases in which confirmation of the winning bid had already been issued and cases in which it had not.

The MILITARY FORCE uses legally prescribed priority signals on its vehicles when carrying out urgent missions or other emergency duties. These signals include flashing blue and red lights, a priority siren, and a military flag.
July 1, 2026 is the effective date of Clause 3 of Article 10 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. It is also the effective date of Law No. 118/2025/QH15, except for provisions covered by Article 11, Clause 2.

TEST PARTICIPANTS are people who take the road traffic law knowledge test using connected computers at the testing location. They log in to the test software, complete the test according to the examiner’s instructions, and follow the rules of the testing location.
Vietnam’s National Assembly is the country’s legislature and the body that issued Resolution No. 73/2022/QH15. It may decide whether to extend the period for applying the relevant article.

ROAD TRAFFIC LAW KNOWLEDGE TESTS assess knowledge of the laws governing road traffic order and safety. The competent authority must organize them at least twice per week and provide the facilities and equipment needed to conduct them.

SIMULATED TRAFFIC SITUATIONS are computer-based traffic scenarios used in a simulated legal-knowledge test. They are presented on a computer and serve as the practical simulations through which the test is conducted.

VEHICLE STOPPING is the act or event of bringing a vehicle to a stationary position. Temporary stopping refers to remaining stationary long enough for passengers to board or alight, goods to be loaded or unloaded, a technical inspection to be conducted, or another activity to take place. Generally, the driver must keep the engine running and remain at the driving position, subject to stated exceptions and safety requirements. A vehicle must come to a stop before its door is opened under Article 19. The cited provision prohibits stopping at road intersections and within five meters of their edges.

The **LEGAL-KNOWLEDGE TEST ON ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY** is a test concerning legal knowledge of road traffic order and safety. The circular sets out requirements for organizing the test and for participants, including attending at the notified time and place and providing or accessing information needed to verify their identity.

The **ROAD TRAFFIC LAW KNOWLEDGE TEST** is an examination of knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. Under Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, Article 7 addresses registration for and organization of the test; the registration dossier includes a request using Form No. 01 in the circular’s appendix. People whose driving-licence points have all been deducted may take the test.

Participants attend at the time and place notified by the competent authority and present an accepted identity document so their details can be checked against their application. Electronic identification information may be used for verification when available. The test is conducted on computers using designated, approved software, with secure data handling and logging. The testing room must have a secure camera-surveillance system that records and stores images. Participants follow the examiner’s instructions and the testing-location rules. Foreign participants and ethnic-minority participants who cannot read or write Vietnamese use an interpreter hired by the competent testing authority. The test’s organization is funded from specified public revenues.

The **LEGAL KNOWLEDGE TEST ON ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY** is a theoretical examination assessing candidates’ knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. Under Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, candidates take the test on a computer using dedicated multiple-choice examination software. Article 5 sets out the conditions for organizing the examination. Applicants register by submitting the required documents and may select a test date and competent testing authority; they are then notified of the expected time and place. The available information does not specify the actual test time or location.

The Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam, abbreviated BCA, is the issuing authority identified in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. The circular sets out provisions on the road-traffic legal-knowledge examination, including its registration and organization, responsibilities assigned to local-level police directors, and funding for the tests under Article 9. It also addresses driver testing and licensing, an area for which the Minister of Public Security issues regulations.

Under Article 10, the Ministry is responsible for building and managing specialized databases. These include databases on vehicle registration, traffic violations, road accidents, vehicle journeys and driver images, drivers’ operating time, vehicle inspections, driver testing and licensing, and certificates of legal-knowledge training. Some of these databases concern the People’s Public Security.

The **SIMULATION-BASED LEGAL KNOWLEDGE TEST** assesses participants’ knowledge of traffic law through computer simulations in which they respond to traffic situations. The test lasts no more than 10 minutes and consists of 10 questions, each scored from 0 to 5 points. A score of at least 35 out of 50 is required to pass.

The **COMPETENT TESTING AUTHORITY** is the authorized body responsible for organizing and conducting examinations on knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. It must have the facilities and equipment required for the examinations available for its use.

The authority announces examination schedules and locations, publicly posting the relevant information on an electronic information portal within its management scope. It receives or processes applications, including requests to retake the examination. After receiving a complete and valid application, it notifies registered candidates of the examination time and location at least two working days in advance, and promptly informs them of any changes.

On the examination day, the authority notifies candidates of the required time and location, checks their documents, and compares their identity information with their applications. When language assistance is needed, it may hire an interpreter for a participant, including a foreign participant who cannot read or write Vietnamese.
The Ministry of Public Security (BCA) is Vietnam’s public security ministry. The BCA designation appears in the cited circular numbers, including Circular No. 65/2024/TT-BCA.

**CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA** is a circular issued by Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security establishing requirements and procedures for testing drivers’ legal knowledge of road traffic order and safety, particularly for drivers whose driving-license points have been fully deducted and who must pass a test to restore points.

Article 5 sets requirements for the conditions, facilities, and equipment needed to organize the tests. Article 6 specifies the test requirements, including the content and method of assessment, duration, question structure, results, and passing requirements. Clause 3 addresses the theoretical test’s timing, questions, and pass criteria; point (a) of clause 1 was amended and supplemented by Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA. Provisions of Article 6 are also referenced by Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA, whose transitional rule keeps the specified testing provisions in effect through June 30, 2027.

Article 7 governs registration for and organization of the road-traffic-law knowledge examination, including retesting. Article 8 sets out the responsibilities of competent authorities conducting examinations, including publicly posting study materials on the electronic information portal under their management.

Article 11 addresses implementation responsibilities. It assigns the Traffic Police Department’s director responsibility for researching, developing, administering, maintaining, and upgrading software used for the tests, and for reporting that work to Ministry leadership. It also assigns responsibilities to directors of provincial and centrally governed municipal police. The circular provides for reporting difficulties and requesting guidance during implementation.
BÀI KIỂM TRA is the examination addressed in Article 6. The article sets out its content, method, timing, and structure, as well as the criteria for achieving a satisfactory result.

The **SIMULATED LEGAL-KNOWLEDGE TEST** is a computer-based examination that assesses knowledge of road-traffic rules, order, and safety through simulated traffic situations. It is required alongside the theoretical test for the restoration of driving-license points.

The **THEORETICAL LEGAL KNOWLEDGE TEST** assesses knowledge of road traffic regulations and safety using questions developed and issued by the Traffic Police Department. It is used in motor vehicle driver licensing and may also be required when a person whose motorcycle licence points have all been deducted seeks to have those points restored. For holders of category A or B1 licences, the test lasts 19 minutes and contains 25 multiple-choice questions, including one critical question. A score of at least 23 is required, and an incorrect answer to the critical question results in failure.

The **LEGAL KNOWLEDGE EXAMINATION ON ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY** assesses knowledge of laws and regulations concerning road traffic order and safety. It is organized on a monthly schedule, and prospective participants may submit registration applications and select an available examination date.

The ROAD-TRAFFIC LEGAL-KNOWLEDGE EXAMINATION assesses knowledge of the laws governing road-traffic order and safety. It may be retaken after an unsuccessful result. Article 7 addresses the examination’s registration and organization; under clause 1, the registration dossier must include a valid driver’s health certificate issued by a competent medical facility.

THÔNG TƯ 65/2024/TT-BCA is a Vietnamese circular dated 12 November 2024 that regulates examinations of legal knowledge on road traffic order and safety for drivers seeking to restore points on their driving licences. Article 6, clause 3, specifies the duration, structure, and passing criteria for the theory test taken by people holding a class B driving licence.

The **LEGAL-KNOWLEDGE THEORY TEST** is an examination for holders of automobile driving licences, including class B licences, whose licence points have been fully deducted. Drivers must pass it to have their points restored and before taking the simulated legal-knowledge test. As specified in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, the test lasts 20 minutes and consists of 30 multiple-choice questions, each worth one point, including one disqualifying question. A score of at least 27 is required, and answering the disqualifying question incorrectly results in failure.

The ELECTRONIC IDENTIFICATION AND AUTHENTICATION SYSTEM is an electronic system used to access and verify a test participant’s identity information. It is accessed through the national identification application and may provide candidate identity details for comparison with the information in the participant’s examination application.

An **INTERPRETER** is a person hired by the competent testing authority or the test taker to provide language assistance during an examination. The interpreter may assist foreign or ethnic-minority participants who cannot read or write Vietnamese by translating examination questions accurately and completely and explaining and guiding the test taker through the testing procedure. The interpreter signs or fingerprints the examination record along with the examinee.

EXAMINATION REGISTRATION is the process of applying to take the road traffic law knowledge examination by submitting the required registration dossier, including an application and health certificate. When registering online, applicants also select a testing authority and choose an examination date.

A **COMPETENT MEDICAL FACILITY** is a medical facility authorized to issue a valid health certificate, in paper or electronic form, for a driver or a person registering for an examination. No specific facility is named.

An EXAMINEE is a person taking an examination on knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. The examinee may be a foreign national or a member of an ethnic minority and may have an interpreter.

“PROVINCES AND CENTRALLY GOVERNED MUNICIPALITIES” refers to the provincial-level administrative jurisdictions mentioned in the text. Police directors in these jurisdictions are responsible for reporting test results within the scope of their management.

The **ROAD TRAFFIC LAW KNOWLEDGE EXAMINATION** tests participants’ knowledge of the laws governing road traffic order and safety. Its registration and organization are addressed in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, including provisions referenced in Articles 7 and 8. Participants may register to take the examination and, if they do not pass, may register for a retest.

The responsible authority publicly announces the examination schedule, including the expected time and location for the following month. The time or location may be changed, with prior registrants notified of the change. At the conclusion of the examination, participants sign or fingerprint the examination record; an interpreter does so as well when applicable.

The **COMPETENT EXAMINATION AUTHORITY** is the authorized body responsible for administering or overseeing the examination on laws concerning road traffic order and safety. Applicants select the authority when registering and may submit their registration documents or dossiers to it, including through an online application. For in-person submissions, the authority assigns a staff member to review the dossier and issue an appointment specifying the examination time and location.

The authority publicly announces examination schedules, including the expected time and location of examinations for the following month, and must notify registered examinees if the examination time or location changes. A person who fails may request a retest from the authority that administered the earlier examination or choose another competent authority.

The authority retains a copy of the examination record. It must preserve examination-room surveillance-camera images for at least two years and examination registration records and minutes, in both paper and electronic form, for at least five years.

The Directors of Provincial and Centrally Governed Municipal Police are the officials who head their respective provincial or centrally governed municipal police agencies. They are responsible for organizing mobile checks of road-traffic legal knowledge when the conditions specified in Article 5 are met, and for periodically or exceptionally reporting the results of those checks within their areas of management.

Registered Examinees are people who have registered to take the examination and provided an email address or phone number, or other contact information, in their application. They are entitled to receive notices about the examination’s time and location through the contact details or other means provided in their application.

The **ELECTRONIC INFORMATION PORTAL** is an online portal managed within the competent authority’s scope. The authority uses it to publicly announce proposed examination dates and examination schedules, including the test’s date, time, and location. The portal also provides public access to study materials on road traffic order and safety laws.

PROVINCIAL AND CENTRALLY GOVERNED MUNICIPAL POLICE are police agencies serving provinces and centrally governed municipalities. Their directors are responsible for implementing the relevant requirements, including arranging mobile checks of legal knowledge concerning road traffic order and safety when the required conditions are met.

The **ROAD TRAFFIC LEGAL KNOWLEDGE TEST** assesses knowledge of road traffic rules and safety. Its time and location are publicly announced by the competent testing authority. Article 7 governs the test’s registration and organization, as well as the conduct expected of participants.

TEST REGISTRATION is the process of applying to take a legal-knowledge test on road traffic order and safety. It is conducted under Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA and requires submission of an application for registration.

The **Provinces and Centrally Governed Cities of Vietnam** are the country’s provincial-level administrative areas and territorial jurisdictions. They include provinces and cities directly under the central government. Their People’s Committees are assigned responsibilities under Article 15.

MINISTRY-LEVEL AGENCIES are agencies within the ministry to which the units referred to in Article 14 belong. In this context, they are agencies within the Ministry of Public Security whose subordinate units are responsible for implementing Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA.

The ROAD TRAFFIC LEGAL KNOWLEDGE EXAMINATION is an examination that assesses knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. It is organized by a competent authority, with arrangements covering registration for and administration of the examination.

The **THEORETICAL DRIVING TEST** is the examination used to assess applicants for the relevant driver’s-license class. Its duration, questions, and required passing score serve as the basis or benchmark for the corresponding legal-knowledge and point-restoration tests.
The PEOPLE'S PUBLIC SECURITY FORCE is Vietnam’s public security force. Applications through the force are listed as one channel for submitting examination applications and registration.

The **LEGAL KNOWLEDGE TEST** is an examination of candidates’ knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. It is generally conducted as a multiple-choice test on a computer using examination software, subject to the exception specified in Clause 8 of Article 7, as amended by Article 2 of the circular. The applicable circular and Article 6 address the test’s content, method, duration and timing, questions, and results. Candidates who pass may have points restored to their driving licence; those who fail may register to take the test again after seven working days have elapsed from the end of their previous examination.
APPENDIX I is attached to Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP (Decree 151/2024/ND-CP) and sets out the technical requirements for signal devices, including sirens, used by priority vehicles.

The Provincial and Municipal Police are police forces operating in provinces and centrally governed cities. Their management portals publish examination schedules and locations for commune-level police to use when arranging appointments. The directors of these forces are responsible for implementing Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA.

**Provinces and Centrally Governed Cities** are Vietnam’s provincial-level administrative jurisdictions. Their responsibilities include having provincial police directors implement the relevant circular and having People’s Committees and their chairpersons implement the decree. People’s Committees also direct local management and inspection, and notify the specified authorities of relevant violations, accidents, and incidents. The jurisdictions’ Departments of Construction receive journey-monitoring data, and the jurisdiction in which an intelligent transport vehicle operates determines which local traffic police authority may issue its permit.

The **POSTAL SERVICE** is a permitted mail-delivery channel through which applicants may send prescribed written notices, applications, dossiers, requests, and supporting or follow-up documents to the competent authority. Submissions may relate to intelligent transport vehicle operating permits, approvals, road traffic law examination registration, permit reissuance, or other required procedures.

Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP requires the installation of driver-image recording devices in vehicles used for commercial passenger transport that have at least eight passenger seats, as well as in tractor-trucks, ambulances, and road-rescue vehicles.

The **INSTALLATION OF JOURNEY-MONITORING DEVICES** requirement under Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP applies to specified commercial-transport and internal-transport vehicles. It includes cars used for commercial transport.

Primary school students are the intended recipients of education on road traffic order and safety laws. This instruction includes practical guidance on safely getting on and off bicycles, mopeds, and motorcycles. Students are also expected to comply with road traffic laws, and their compliance may be considered when assessing their conduct.
APPENDIX II is an appendix to Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. It contains forms relating to applications for permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles, including Form No. 02a.

VIETNAMESE INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL SERVICE ENTERPRISES are Vietnamese businesses licensed to provide international travel services. Under Article 33, they may apply for approval to organize tourism trips in which foreign visitors bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam. In specified cases, the required application dossier must be submitted through the enterprise to the Traffic Police Department.

Under Article 35, these enterprises are responsible for the accuracy and legality of documents and information submitted concerning foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles. They must notify the competent authority if previously approved details change. If an incident delays the visitors’ departure, the enterprises must contact the relevant authority and local police.

ORGANIZATIONS BRINGING RIGHT-HAND-DRIVE CARS are organizations that bring cars with right-hand steering into Vietnam for use on public roads or in traffic for purposes other than tourism. Their activities are subject to the applicable rules and requirements, including the approval provisions described in Article 33 and Appendix IV.

Individuals Bringing Right-Hand-Drive Cars are people who bring right-hand-drive cars into traffic in Vietnam for road use, including for purposes other than tourism. Their use of these vehicles is subject to the applicable requirements and approval provisions set out in the decree, including Article 33 and Appendix IV. Where specified, they may also be required to submit a notice if their travel or departure arrangements change.

Lower-secondary students are the intended recipients of legal education on road traffic order and safety. The instruction covers relevant laws and includes recognizing and obeying road traffic signals. Students’ compliance with these laws is also a criterion in their conduct assessment.

Vocational education establishments are educational institutions whose managing agencies are directed to prepare facilities and motorbikes for safe-riding instruction. Their students are covered by the decree’s provisions on education in road traffic order and safety law.

High schools are educational institutions covered by Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. They are responsible for educating students about road-traffic order and safety laws and for including compliance with those laws among the criteria for evaluating and classifying student conduct. Under Article 6, they also guide students in safe motorbike-riding skills, organize students and their families to sign commitments to follow road-traffic laws and safety requirements, and work with student parent representative boards to support compliance. High schools must remind students to honor their commitments and communicate with families about students’ compliance.

DECREE NO. 151/2024/ND-CP is a Vietnamese government decree concerning road traffic order and safety. Article 1 defines its scope, covering when people and vehicles must assist drivers, warn other road users, and take safety measures for oversized, overweight, crawler-track, and exceptionally large or heavy cargo vehicles operating on roads. It also covers journey-monitoring and driver-image recording devices for specified commercial vehicles, permits for intelligent-transport vehicles, and operating conditions for rudimentary vehicles.

The decree addresses several related procedures and responsibilities. Article 12 concerns the collection of information for the road traffic order and safety database. Article 21 sets out procedures for issuing or reissuing permits to use signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles, while Article 22, Clause 2 provides that such permits for vehicles assigned emergency duties expire immediately when the emergency ends. The decree is also cited as the legal basis for procedures to withdraw operating permits for intelligent-transport vehicles.

Other provisions cover road users and vehicle management: Article 5, Clause 1 concerns safe motorbike-riding guidance for students beginning upper-secondary school or vocational education, including recognizing and responding to dangerous situations. Article 30 sets requirements for the exterior paint and identifying signs of vehicles transporting preschool children and pupils. Article 36 specifies the responsibilities of relevant agencies in managing foreign nationals who drive foreign motor vehicles in traffic in Vietnam.

SAFE MOTORBIKE RIDING SKILLS GUIDANCE is the guidance described in Article 5 for students beginning upper-secondary education and students attending vocational education institutions. It covers safe motorbike riding skills, including how to mount and dismount safely, and addresses traffic culture, motor vehicle operators’ responsibilities, and how to assist people injured in traffic accidents.

Upper secondary schools are educational institutions that students begin attending upon entering upper secondary education. Students at this stage are among those intended to receive safe motorbike-riding guidance, and these schools may also provide safe-riding instruction and assessment.

Upper secondary education institutions are educational institutions that provide instruction to students beginning upper secondary education. Their intended recipients are students at this stage of their education.

**SAFE MOTORBIKE-RIDING SKILLS GUIDANCE** is instruction for students beginning upper secondary school or vocational education. It covers starting a motorbike, adjusting speed appropriately, stopping safely, and recognizing and handling dangerous situations while riding. The guidance is described in Article 5 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, with responsibilities for providing it set out in Article 6.
Students beginning upper secondary school or vocational education are the intended recipients of instruction in safe motorbike and moped riding skills.

Students’ families are responsible for helping ensure their children follow road-traffic safety laws. They are expected to coordinate with relevant authorities to educate students about traffic regulations and provide safe moped-riding instruction. Family members should not allow students to operate vehicles unless they meet all applicable legal requirements. They should also regularly remind their children to honor their signed commitments and communicate with the school about the students’ compliance with traffic-safety laws.

**NGHỊ ĐỊNH 151/2024/NĐ-CP** is a Vietnamese government decree governing a range of matters related to road traffic order and safety. It provides for education about road traffic laws and safety under Article 4, including safety topics for children in educational institutions.

Articles 11 and 12 address the road traffic order and safety database. Article 11 specifies information recorded in the database, including information on the registration and management of motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles, as well as motor-vehicle registration fee details. Article 12 sets out sources and methods for collecting that information, including provisions in Clause 5.

The decree also regulates signal devices on priority vehicles. Article 19 establishes technical requirements for signal-emitting devices, including the use of flashing blue lights for specified duties. Article 20 sets out the documentation required to apply for a new or replacement permit to use such devices, while Article 22 governs those permits and provides for their revocation in specified circumstances, including when a vehicle is converted to another use or liquidated.

Article 27 concerns journey-monitoring devices installed in transport vehicles and the collection, use, and sharing of data from them. Article 33 sets out dossier and submission procedures for matters involving foreign vehicles entering Vietnam and right-hand-drive cars participating in Vietnamese traffic. It also addresses approval of international travel-service businesses organizing specified activities involving foreign vehicles or road use in Vietnam, and reporting changes to previously approved information.

Under Article 38(2), the decree repeals specified phrases and provisions, including parts of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP.

Upper-secondary students receive instruction on laws governing road traffic order and safety, and their compliance with these laws is considered in conduct assessments. Students beginning upper-secondary studies are also among those intended to receive guidance in safe moped-riding skills.

Upper secondary education is the education level that students are beginning when they receive safe motorbike-riding guidance under the decree. Incoming students at this level are among those covered by the guidance.

**DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP** is a Vietnamese government decree cited as the legal basis for a broad set of provisions on road traffic order and safety. Its provisions cover education, traffic databases, priority-vehicle signaling equipment, intelligent transport vehicles, journey-monitoring data, and foreign vehicles operating in Vietnam.

Articles 4–8 address road-safety education in educational institutions. They cover legal-knowledge instruction for students at different levels, safe moped-riding guidance for students beginning upper-secondary or vocational education, and the responsibilities of schools, families, and the Ministry of Education and Training.

Articles 9–16 govern the road traffic order and safety database and specialized databases. They set principles for building and managing the databases; describe responsibilities, funding, access, sharing, and use; and provide for collecting and updating information. Article 11 covers records such as vehicle registration and inspection, drivers and licences, training and certificates, driver operating time and health, compulsory civil-liability insurance, administrative violations, foreign vehicles, and vehicles involved in violations. Article 12 specifies collection methods and sources.

Articles 17–23 regulate signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles, including which vehicles may use them, requirements for their signals and technical specifications, permits and application procedures, permit forms and terms, and the authorities responsible for issuing, reissuing, or revoking permits. Use is restricted to authorized vehicles and official duties.

Articles 25 and 25a concern operating permits for intelligent or smart traffic vehicles, including application documents and procedures for issuing, changing, renewing, or reissuing permits. Articles 27–29 address the use, sharing, transmission, management, and storage of data from journey-monitoring and driver-image recording devices. Article 28 requires driver-image recording equipment for specified passenger, tractor, ambulance, and road-rescue vehicles. Article 31 covers assistance, warnings, and safety measures for oversized or overweight vehicles and certain heavy or unusually long loads.

Articles 32–36 regulate foreign motor vehicles and foreign nationals driving in Vietnam. They set vehicle and driver requirements, including inspection documentation, describe approval procedures for foreign vehicles entering Vietnam for tourism and for certain right-hand-drive vehicles, and assign relevant agencies responsibilities for managing these activities. Article 37 provides transitional arrangements for previously approved programs.

The decree also contains provisions on its scope and appendices, entry into force, repeal of specified legal provisions, and implementation responsibilities.

Specialized databases are subject-specific databases built and maintained by ministries and sectors. In accordance with law, their relevant information may be connected to and shared with the road traffic order and safety database.

The TRANSPORT BUSINESS UNIT is an entity engaged in providing transport services. Its information is included in a database, where its record may contain its name, enterprise identification number, transport business license number, address, licensing authority, transport operator, and type of transport business. The unit is also identified as a data field in records used to manage drivers’ vehicle operating time.

DRIVER’S LICENSE POINT RESTORATION is the process of restoring points to a driver’s license after all points have been deducted. It requires passing a road-traffic legal-knowledge test, and the time at which restoration occurs is recorded.

The **DATABASE ON ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY** is an information system for collecting and maintaining information concerning road traffic order and safety. Under Article 12 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, information is collected for inclusion in the database, including specified information from the database on compulsory civil liability insurance for motor vehicle owners.

The database includes information on driver training, testing and licensing, as well as certificates for training in road traffic law.
