This includes training information and road-traffic-law certificates for operators of specialized motorcycles. Article 13 of the decree addresses updating the database: records are added or adjusted using information from sources prescribed by law.

The Ministry of Finance is a Vietnamese government ministry involved in coordinating the management of foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam. Under the relevant decree, it works with the Ministries of Foreign Affairs, Transport, Construction, and Public Security on the activities and procedures covered, including the temporary import and re-export of foreign motor vehicles participating in traffic in Vietnam.

The Ministry of Finance and its relevant functional units receive copies of approval documents so they can coordinate management of the approved activities. It is also responsible for building and managing databases concerning exported and imported vehicles, vehicle sale invoices and related documents, vehicle registration fees, and customs information.

**CƠ SỞ DỮ LIỆU VỀ TRẬT TỰ, AN TOÀN GIAO THÔNG ĐƯỜNG BỘ** is a database concerning road traffic order and safety. Article 12 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP addresses how information is collected for the database and describes information it contains, including details about vehicle owners and compulsory civil liability insurance.

ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATION HANDLING is the process of handling administrative violations of road traffic order and safety. It includes determining applicable penalties, fines, supplementary sanctions, remedial measures, and the time allowed for compliance. Information about the processing and its results is recorded in the database and may be used to update it.

A **DRIVER TRAINING COURSE** is a course recorded by its identifier and name. Its record may include the training period, including opening and closing dates, the practical training distance, the completion result, and the time the course was completed.

Traffic accidents are road incidents in which people may be injured, and guidance on them includes assistance to those injured. In Vietnam, accidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles must be reported by provincial and municipal authorities to the designated ministries and foreign representative bodies. Costs arising from these accidents are handled by the parties responsible under Article 35. Unresolved matters connected with accidents involving foreign nationals or foreign motor vehicles may affect the approval or continuation of the relevant activity.

INFORMATION COLLECTION FOR THE ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE is the Article 12 process of gathering information from the databases and data categories specified in the referenced provisions, including the National Database on Finance.

MOTOR VEHICLE REGISTRATION AND MANAGEMENT is the administrative process for registering and managing motor vehicles, including specialized motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles, but excluding military vehicles. The process includes recording vehicle and owner information in the road traffic order and safety database, which is managed by the Ministry of Public Security.

The PROCURACY FORCE is a Vietnamese law-enforcement body whose vehicles may operate as priority vehicles when carrying out urgent duties, including arrests, searches, and other investigative activities. Under Article 18 of the decree, vehicles used for these emergency duties are covered by the rules governing priority-vehicle signals and use flashing blue and red lights together with a priority siren.

Article 11 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP sets out, in clauses 1 through 5, information requirements referenced in Article 12. The information specified in those clauses is collected for the road traffic order and safety database.
SEARCH is an operation carried out as part of listed military duties. It may also be performed by procuracy-force vehicles while they are on emergency duty.

**DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP** is a Vietnamese government decree dated November 15, 2024, providing detailed regulations and implementation measures for the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. It covers education, traffic-safety data, vehicle equipment and operation, and the participation of foreign vehicles and drivers in traffic in Vietnam.

Articles 4–8 address road-safety legal education across preschool, primary, lower-secondary, upper-secondary, and vocational education. They also provide for safe motorbike-riding instruction for students and assign related responsibilities to education authorities and institutions.

Articles 9–15 establish principles for building, managing, using, connecting, and sharing the road traffic order and safety database and related specialized databases. The database may include information on vehicle registration, ownership, inspection, origin and sales; driver training, licensing, and health examinations; insurance; accidents and traffic-safety recommendations; administrative violations; transport businesses and vehicle badges; and vehicle journeys and driver images. These provisions also address collecting, updating, accessing, and exchanging information, including data from foreign-vehicle and customs databases.

Articles 17–24 regulate signal-emitting equipment on priority vehicles. They cover technical requirements, installation, eligible vehicles and duties, applications and procedures for issuing or replacing permits, reissuance, validity, revocation, and management of the equipment. The decree includes relevant application forms and technical requirements in appendices. It specifies, for example, signals for ambulances responding to emergencies.

The decree also regulates licensing and operation of intelligent or smart transport vehicles, including application documents, licensing authorities, permit replacement or reissuance, and grounds for revocation; the relevant provisions are cited as Articles 25 and 25a in the descriptions. Other provisions address journey-monitoring equipment for specified transport and emergency vehicles, operating conditions for rudimentary vehicles, commercial vehicles transporting students, and safety measures for oversized, overweight, tracked, or exceptionally large or heavy vehicles.

Articles 32–36 govern foreign motor vehicles and foreign drivers in Vietnam. They address vehicle and driver eligibility, registration and licensing, customs and temporary import and re-export procedures, permitted routes and periods of circulation, required documents and insurance, and compliance with Vietnamese traffic laws. They also establish approval procedures and responsibilities for international travel businesses arranging foreign-vehicle tourism and for entities using right-hand-drive vehicles in Vietnam for non-tourism purposes, as well as responsibilities of relevant agencies. The decree’s final provisions include repeal of specified earlier regulations upon its entry into force.

USE OF PRIORITY-VEHICLE SIGNAL EQUIPMENT refers to the installation and use of signal-emitting equipment on vehicles assigned to qualifying priority duties. It includes operating such equipment while those vehicles are carrying out their priority functions.

FIRE PREVENTION, FIREFIGHTING AND RESCUE POLICE is the police force responsible for fire prevention, firefighting, and rescue. Its fire trucks are equipped with priority-vehicle signal devices, including a red flashing light and a priority siren, as specified in the decree.

APPLICANT AGENCIES AND ORGANIZATIONS are entities seeking permission to use signal devices on priority vehicles. They submit the required written application and supporting dossier for a new or replacement permit, or request reissuance of an existing permit. Applicants must provide documents demonstrating their functions and eligibility unless the relevant information is available through a connected, shared database.

The RECEIVING AUTHORITY is the competent authority that receives and reviews applications and supporting documents. It notifies applicants if submissions are incomplete or they are ineligible, and explains why an applicant does not qualify. It accepts qualifying, complete applications and issues or reissues the permit; approval decisions are issued within two working days after receipt of a complete submission.
ARREST is an operation to take a person into custody. It may be carried out by procuracy-force vehicles on emergency duty and is also included among listed military duties.

The NATIONAL DATABASE ON FINANCE is a national database identified as a source from which specified information is collected, including information recorded in the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database.

Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government decree addressing road traffic order and safety, related databases, and signaling devices on priority vehicles. Article 11, clause 15, concerns information about foreign motor vehicles driven by foreigners participating in road traffic in Vietnam. Article 12 provides for collecting information for the Road Traffic Order and Road Safety Database, while Article 15 governs management of that database and assigns coordination responsibilities to government bodies.

The decree also sets out rules for signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles. Article 21 addresses procedures for issuing and reissuing permits to use the devices. Under Article 24, agencies and organizations licensed to use them are responsible for their management, installation, and use; the competent authority issues and may revoke permits. Licensed entities must report annually on their management and use of the devices to the authority that issued the permit, before December 15, using Form No. 02d in Appendix II.

Article 38, clause 2, repeals specified provisions, including provisions of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP. Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP is also cited as the legal basis for provisions on collecting database information and is relevant to administrative procedures referenced in a transitional provision of Decree No. 236/2026/NĐ-CP.
COUNTERTERRORISM refers to participation in efforts to prevent or combat terrorism, including police duties focused on countering terrorist threats.

AGENCIES AND ORGANIZATIONS USING PRIORITY VEHICLES are entities that operate priority vehicles and apply for permits authorizing the use of the vehicles’ signal-emitting devices. They submit the required application documents and may receive an initial or reissued permit.

The STEERING COMMITTEE is served by vehicles assigned to perform duties during emergency situations, including emergencies defined by law. These vehicles may be authorized to use priority signal devices.

An **EMERGENCY SITUATION** is a legally defined and declared emergency under the relevant decree. During it, vehicles assigned to serve the Steering Committee or mobilized functional forces may perform their duties, including qualifying missions using a priority-vehicle signal device under Article 17(3)(a). Applicants may communicate with the competent authority in advance about a permit, but must submit the required application documents immediately afterward. Under Article 22(2) of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP, the permit for the vehicle’s signal device expires immediately when the emergency condition referred to in Article 18(8) ends.

“OTHER INVESTIGATIVE ACTIVITIES” refers to investigative activities or operations carried out by police that are not specifically listed as traffic-accident investigations and are distinct from arrests or searches.

Licensed Agencies and Organizations are entities authorized by license or permit to use signaling devices on priority vehicles. They must report annually to the competent authority that issued the license on how the devices are managed and used. If a permit is revoked, they must return it.

The **Licensing of Intelligent Transport Vehicles** is the administrative process governed by Article 25 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. It concerns the granting of permits or other authorization required to operate intelligent transport vehicles.

VIỆT NAM is the country referenced in the formal name of the Vietnam Road Administration. It is also the country where the regulated vehicle activities take place and whose government authorities and international travel-service businesses are addressed by the decree. The decree’s provisions concerning foreign vehicles and right-hand-drive cars apply to traffic and territory in Việt Nam.

The **COMPETENT ISSUING AUTHORITY** is the authority that previously issued a permit for signaling devices on a priority vehicle or an intelligent transport vehicle operating license. It is responsible for receiving the relevant permit or license when it is subject to revocation and for carrying out the revocation.

Foreign Drivers are foreign nationals who operate foreign motor vehicles or other vehicles participating in traffic in Vietnam. They must hold an appropriate, valid driving licence and comply with the applicable conditions set out in Article 32. Their driving activities are subject to management and inspection, including the reporting of legal violations and traffic accidents.

The **PERMIT ISSUANCE AND REISSUANCE PROCEDURE**, described in Article 21, governs applications to issue or reissue permits for using signal devices on priority vehicles. Once a complete and valid application is received, it is reviewed within two working days. When an application is handled directly, the permit information must be entered into a database for management.

OPERATING PERMIT ISSUANCE is the licensing process through which an operating permit for an intelligent transport vehicle is issued on the prescribed form once the application meets the requirements. The permit is issued within five working days after the application is received.
Functional Forces are the competent forces that may be mobilized to perform duties and tasks when an emergency situation or state of emergency is declared.

FOREIGN VEHICLE DRIVERS are foreign nationals who drive foreign motor vehicles in road traffic in Vietnam under the conditions specified in the relevant provision. The provision requires information about these drivers to be recorded.
**DRIVER ASSISTANCE AND ROAD-USER WARNINGS** covers providing assistance to drivers and issuing warnings to people and vehicles participating in road traffic, as described in Article 31.

“Participation in Traffic in Vietnam” refers to driving or operating vehicles on Vietnam’s roads. It includes foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles, whose participation is subject to written approval. Foreign vehicles may use Vietnam’s roads for no longer than the applicable visa or visa-exemption period, except where an additional-stay circumstance applies. Violations, accidents, and other related incidents may occur during such participation.

**EXIT FROM VIETNAM** refers to the departure of foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles from Vietnam. Required customs procedures must be completed as part of the exit process. If an unforeseen incident prevents departure, a foreign national may be permitted to remain in Vietnam for up to 10 additional days, subject to the prescribed procedures.

The **Law on Entry, Exit, Transit, and Residence of Foreigners in Vietnam** is the Vietnamese legal framework governing foreign nationals’ entry into, exit from, transit through, and residence in Vietnam. It is cited as the basis for requirements established by the decree and for determining the maximum permitted stay of foreigners in the country.

Intergovernmental international organizations are organizations formed by governments. Under the relevant decree, their representative offices in Vietnam may issue an official dispatch or diplomatic note requesting authorization for foreign vehicles to participate in Vietnamese traffic for non-tourism purposes.

International border gates are designated international crossing points. Foreign vehicles may be temporarily imported and re-exported through them when the competent authorities have approved the crossing. For travelers holding electronic visas, entry into Vietnam must take place through the international border gates designated by the Government of Vietnam.

Foreign travelers are individuals from outside Vietnam who visit the country for tourism and may bring foreign motor vehicles under arrangements organized by Vietnamese international travel service businesses and covered by the relevant decree. Their information and planned departure timing may be subject to notification if they change.

ENTRY INTO VIETNAM refers to the process by which foreign nationals enter the country. Their entry is governed by applicable immigration rules, which determine the relevant visa period and the period during which they may participate in traffic. Required customs procedures must also be completed as part of the entry process.

Vietnamese international travel service businesses are businesses licensed to provide international travel services in Vietnam. Under the relevant decree, they may organize tourism trips in which foreign visitors bring foreign-registered motor vehicles into Vietnam, subject to approval by the competent authority. To obtain approval, the businesses must submit an application dossier to the Traffic Police Department or other competent authority specified by the procedure.

Article 35 sets out their responsibilities for organizing these trips and managing the foreign motor vehicles and visitors participating in traffic, including arranging traffic guidance where required. The businesses must report the results of the activity to the authority that issued the permit. The Ministry of Public Security is responsible for inspecting and handling violations related to these businesses’ organization of foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam.

Foreign diplomatic missions in Vietnam are designated recipients of notifications from the Ministry of Public Security concerning specified legal violations, traffic accidents, and vehicle-related incidents involving foreign drivers or vehicles. They may also submit diplomatic notes requesting permission for a right-hand-drive car to participate in Vietnamese traffic for a non-tourism purpose, with the reason for the request stated.

The PEOPLE'S COMMITTEES OF PROVINCES AND CENTRALLY RUN CITIES are local government bodies in the relevant provinces and centrally run cities. They are notified of approvals to coordinate management, and their chairpersons are responsible for implementing the decree.

Foreign Vehicle Tourism in Vietnam is a tourism activity in which foreign visitors bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism. The activity is arranged by an approved Vietnamese international travel service enterprise, as described in Article 33.

Foreign tourists are visitors from outside Vietnam who travel within the country. They may bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism when their travel is organized by a Vietnamese international travel service business. Road-travel programs and routes are to be developed for these visitors.
“ORGANIZATIONS BRINGING RIGHT-HAND-DRIVE CARS INTO TRAFFIC” refers to organizations that bring right-hand-drive cars onto roads in Vietnam for purposes other than tourism.

Article 33 of Vietnam’s Decree 151/2024/ND-CP sets out approval and application procedures for certain foreign vehicles entering or travelling on roads in Vietnam. It covers foreign vehicles used for non-tourism purposes, including right-hand-drive cars, and explains how changes to approved routes or departure times are handled.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is a Vietnamese government ministry responsible for coordinating the organization and management of activities involving foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam, as provided under Article 36 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. It coordinates with the Ministry of Transport, other relevant agencies, and foreign representative agencies.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its relevant functional units receive copies of approval documents so they can coordinate the management of approved activities. The Ministry of Public Security must also notify it of specified legal violations, traffic accidents, or other incidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam.

FOREIGN MOTOR VEHICLES PARTICIPATING IN TRAFFIC IN VIETNAM refers to the use of foreign motor vehicles on Vietnamese roads by foreign nationals. The decree provides for organizing and guiding this activity, monitoring it, and sharing relevant information.

“RELEVANT PROVINCES AND CENTRALLY GOVERNED CITIES” refers to the Vietnamese provinces and centrally governed cities whose People’s Committees may receive approval documents and whose authorities may coordinate the management of approved vehicle movements.

Foreign consular agencies in Vietnam may use diplomatic notes to explain the reasons and purposes for which vehicles participate in Vietnamese traffic. They may also submit diplomatic notes requesting permission for a right-hand-drive car to be used in Vietnam for a non-tourism purpose, stating the reason for the request. The Ministry of Public Security must notify these agencies of the specified incidents.
Individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam are people who bring those vehicles into Vietnamese traffic for purposes other than tourism. They are identified in the heading of Article 35.

Foreign National Drivers are foreign nationals who drive foreign motor vehicles on roads in Vietnam. They must comply with Vietnamese road traffic laws and carry the required documents. When they participate in traffic in Vietnam, violations they commit may fall within the responsibilities assigned to the Ministry of Public Security.

ENTRY AND EXIT OF FOREIGN MOTOR VEHICLES refers to the regulated process of bringing foreign motor vehicles into traffic in Vietnamese territory and taking them out of the country. These movements must be organized and conducted in accordance with applicable regulations.

The **Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism** is a Vietnamese government ministry with responsibilities under Article 36 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP for coordinating the organization and management of activities involving foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam. It guides relevant organizations and individuals on bringing foreign motor vehicles into traffic in Vietnam in accordance with the decree, and works with relevant units, localities, and enterprises to research and develop road-travel programs and routes for foreign tourists. It also coordinates with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant transport authorities on these management activities.

For coordination and oversight, the Ministry’s relevant functional units receive copies of approval documents concerning approved vehicle activities. The Ministry is also to be notified by the Ministry of Public Security about specified legal violations, traffic accidents, or other incidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam.

FOREIGN MOTOR VEHICLE TRAFFIC IN VIETNAM refers to the participation of foreign motor vehicles in traffic within Vietnam, including bringing the vehicles into the country and taking them out afterward. This activity may require arranging the vehicles and traffic guides and displaying an identifying logo or flag. Participants must comply with applicable laws on security and public order.
Individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars into traffic in Vietnam are those who use or introduce such vehicles on Vietnamese roads for purposes other than tourism.

Foreign Nationals Driving Foreign Motor Vehicles are people from outside Vietnam who bring or operate foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam and participate in traffic there. Their activities, including the management of their vehicles and any legal violations, traffic accidents, or vehicle-related incidents, are addressed by Article 36 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP.

**FOREIGN MOTOR VEHICLE INCIDENTS** are incidents caused by, associated with, or involving foreign motor vehicles while they participate in traffic in Vietnam. Provincial and municipal authorities are required to report these incidents, and the Ministry of Public Security must report them to the designated agencies and representatives.

Representative Offices of Intergovernmental International Organizations in Vietnam are offices located in Vietnam that may be involved in specified administrative and traffic-related procedures. The Ministry of Public Security must notify them about specified violations, accidents, or other incidents. Their official dispatches may also state the reasons and purpose for a vehicle to participate in traffic in Vietnam.
Article 12 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP concerns the collection of information for the database on road traffic order and safety.

Organizations bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam are organizations that import or otherwise bring such vehicles into traffic in Vietnam for purposes other than tourism. The category is identified in the heading of Article 35.

APPLICATION RECEIPT AND REVIEW is the administrative step in which the licensing authority receives and checks a permit application and its accompanying documents for the use of signaling equipment on a priority vehicle.

FOREIGN REPRESENTATIVE AGENCIES IN VIETNAM are foreign agencies represented in Vietnam that coordinate with the relevant Vietnamese ministries to organize and manage activities involving foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles brought into the country, including activities covered by Article 36.

**Management and Inspection of Foreign Drivers and Vehicles** is the administrative activity through which local competent authorities manage and inspect foreign drivers and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam. The activity is carried out by local functional agencies under the direction of the relevant provincial and municipal People’s Committees.

The **Permit Reissuance Procedure** is the administrative process for applying for and receiving a reissued permit to use a signal-emitting device on a priority vehicle. It is the procedure identified as the subject of the text.

Vietnam’s National Identity Application is an online channel through which applicants can submit licensing dossiers and documents, complete application forms electronically, and provide materials for permit-reissuance procedures.

**LEGAL VIOLATIONS BY FOREIGN DRIVERS** refers to violations of Vietnamese law committed by foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam. The relevant authorities must inform the designated government agencies and representative bodies: the Ministry of Public Security is required to report such violations, and the relevant People’s Committee must notify the specified ministries and representative bodies. The descriptions do not identify those recipients.

The **COMPETENT PERMIT-ISSUING AUTHORITY** is responsible for issuing documents and processing applications for permission to use signal devices on priority vehicles. It is also the authority that issued the smart traffic vehicle operating permit and receives requests to amend or reissue that permit.

Traffic accidents involving foreign drivers are accidents in Vietnam involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles. In such cases, the Ministry of Public Security must report the accidents to the listed agencies and representatives, while the relevant People’s Committee must notify the designated ministries and representative bodies. These are separate reporting and notification responsibilities.

APPLICANT AGENCY OR ORGANIZATION is an agency or organization seeking a permit to use a signal-emitting device on a priority vehicle. It may maintain an account on the National Public Service Portal or National Identification Application, through which it may receive notices about applications that are deficient or do not meet licensing requirements. In an emergency, it may contact the competent authority in advance, but it must submit the required application afterward.
CỔNG DỊCH VỤ CÔNG QUỐC GIA (Vietnam’s National Public Service Portal) is an online channel through which applicants can submit a dossier.

Vietnamese international travel-service businesses are businesses licensed to provide international travel services in Vietnam. Under Article 33, they may organize tourist trips in which foreigners bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam, subject to approval. To obtain approval, the businesses must submit the prescribed dossier to the Traffic Police Department.

The **NEW PERMIT ISSUANCE PROCEDURE**, set out in Article 21, Clause 1 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, is the administrative process for obtaining a new permit to use a signal-emitting device on a priority vehicle. It involves submitting an application to the licensing authority, which receives and reviews it and handles complete, eligible applications as well as deficient submissions. The authority must issue the permit within one working day after receiving a complete application.

Article 37, “Transitional Provisions,” of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP allows programs approved before the Decree took effect to continue under the terms of their approval. It also provides that certain existing permits remain valid until their stated expiry, while holders in other specified groups must apply for a new permit under Chapter IV.

LAW 118/2025/QH15 is a Vietnamese law whose Article 7 amends and supplements provisions of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. Under Article 11, the law generally takes effect on July 1, 2026, subject to the exception in Clause 2: point a, Clause 20, Article 7 takes effect earlier, on January 1, 2026.

**APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL** is the administrative filing through which a Vietnamese international travel service enterprise submits a dossier to obtain approval to organize tours for foreign visitors bringing foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism.

Foreign Diplomatic Missions in Vietnam are diplomatic missions representing foreign countries in Vietnam. Their official dispatches or diplomatic notes may state the reasons and purposes for vehicles to participate in traffic in Vietnam.

CÔNG AN CÁC ĐƠN VỊ, ĐỊA PHƯƠNG (police units and local police authorities) are responsible for reporting difficulties and obstacles encountered while implementing the Circular to the Ministry of Public Security through the Traffic Police Department, so that the Ministry can provide guidance.

DECREE 184/2025/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government decree. Article 27 amends and supplements provisions of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. Article 28 addresses the decree’s entry into force and specifies when Article 2 ceases to have effect.

An **AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE** is a person authorized by law to act on behalf of a vehicle owner in matters concerning the vehicle’s operating permit. This may include requesting a change to or reissue of the permit, or surrendering it when it is subject to revocation.

**NGHỊ ĐỊNH 236/2026/NĐ-CP** is a Vietnamese government decree that amends provisions on road traffic administration. Article 1 amends Clause 1 of Article 9 concerning the nationwide road traffic order and safety database. Article 10 amends Clauses 1 and 2 of Article 23, specifying which traffic police authorities may issue, reissue, and revoke permits for priority-vehicle warning-signal equipment.

DECREE 236/2026/ND-CP (also identified as 236/2026/NĐ-CP) is a Vietnamese government decree. Its text refers to Article 4, while Article 16 addresses the supplementation, repeal, or replacement of specified phrases, points, clauses, articles, and attached appendices.

DECREE 184/2025/ND-CP is a Vietnamese government decree. Article 28 addresses the decree’s entry into force and implementation, stating that it enters into force on July 1, 2025, and establishing rules for when Article 2 and its corresponding provisions cease to have effect.

Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA sets out test-related provisions, including the test content, methods, timing, structure, and requirements for passing. It is referenced by the circular’s transitional rule.

Decree 238/2026/ND-CP (Nghị định 238/2026/NĐ-CP) is a Vietnamese government decree that amends and supplements provisions of existing regulations. Article 8 amends specified points and clauses of Article 21; Article 13 amends Article 42, concerning the authority of chairpersons of People’s Committees to impose administrative penalties and remedial measures; and Article 16 amends Clause 2 of Article 46. Article 9 is also referenced in the decree.

The decree addresses rules concerning the transport of construction materials, earth, rocks, waste, bulk goods, and other loads, including cases where loads are not properly covered or materials or water spill onto the road. Article 20 concerns the decree’s entry into force and assigns responsibility for guiding, organizing, and enforcing its implementation.
Article 6 of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA is a provision cited in the transitional rules of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA, including in Clause 3 of Article 6 of that circular.

Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA is a Vietnamese Ministry of Public Security circular that amends and supplements point a, clause 1, Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. Its Article 6 contains testing provisions referenced by Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA, whose transitional rules keep those provisions in effect through June 30, 2027. Article 14 sets out implementation provisions, assigns the Director of the Traffic Police Department responsibility for overseeing implementation, and identifies the parties responsible for carrying it out.

DECREE NO. 236/2026/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government decree that amends and supplements rules concerning road traffic order and safety. Article 5 amends Clause 1 of Article 14 on connections to and sharing of information involving the road traffic order and safety database. Article 14 adds Article 33a, which sets out procedures for approving international travel-service businesses and other organizations or individuals to bring foreign motor vehicles, including right-hand-drive cars, into Vietnam, as well as procedures for amending information in an existing approval. Article 17 establishes transitional rules for administrative-procedure applications received or postmarked before the decree takes effect.

DECREE 238/2026/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government decree amending and supplementing regulations on administrative penalties for road-traffic violations and related matters. Its provisions include amendments to several points of Clause 3, Article 3, and Article 3 also amends point b, clause 8, Article 13 concerning vehicle license plates that are missing, improperly positioned or formatted, unclear, altered, obscured, or made difficult to identify by materials or devices. Article 18 adds rules governing administrative penalties related to image-recording equipment on certain road-transport vehicles. Article 19 addresses the supplementation, replacement, and repeal of specified phrases, points, clauses, and articles. Article 21 establishes transitional rules for handling administrative violations involving road-traffic order and safety.

Article 6 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA is titled “Effectiveness and transitional provisions.” Clause 3 specifies which testing rules remain applicable during the transition and for how long. These rules concern legal-knowledge tests for restoring driver’s-license points; Article 1 of the Circular amends the provision setting out those tests’ content, method, duration, and passing requirements.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP includes driver training establishments among the organizations covered by its provisions, as stated in Article 2, Clause 2. Article 39 establishes fines for driver training establishments that commit specified violations, including providing training outside the prescribed curriculum.

CIRCULAR 105/2026/TT-BCA is a Vietnamese Ministry of Public Security circular that amends and supplements rules for legal-knowledge tests on road traffic order and safety, including tests taken to restore points on a driver’s license. Its provisions address test content and methods, timing, questions, duration, passing results, and the restoration of license points.

Article 5 provides an appendix of forms for use in these tests. Article 6 sets out the circular’s entry into force and transitional provisions: tests held after it takes effect must follow its requirements, while Clause 3 continues specified testing rules from earlier circulars until June 30, 2027. Article 7 assigns the Director of the Traffic Police Department responsibility for directing, inspecting, and urging implementation.

THÔNG TƯ 105/2026/TT-BCA is a Vietnamese circular. Article 4 replaces certain wording and repeals appendices and forms in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. Article 7 sets out responsibilities for implementing the circular and procedures for reporting any difficulties or obstacles.
The COMPETENT AUTHORITIES OF VIETNAM are the Vietnamese authorities responsible for granting permission for operations within VIETNAM and issuing permits for vehicle travel within its territory.
Article 3 is a provision of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It forms part of the decree.

DECREE 168/2024/ND-CP addresses remedial measures for violations in Article 3, whose title refers to remedial measures.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out sanctions and remedial measures for administrative violations involving road traffic order and safety.

Article 3 is titled “Revocation of Licenses and Practice Certificates,” identifying revocation of licenses and practice certificates as the subject it addresses.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP addresses the revocation of licenses and practice certificates, as identified in the decree’s heading.

Decree 168/2024/ND-CP establishes penalties that may apply to administrative violations of road traffic order and safety. It also sets out remedial measures for these violations in Article 3, Clause 3.

Article 4 is a provision of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP.

Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP establishes rules on administrative violations involving road traffic order and safety in the road transport sector. It also sets out the remedial measures applicable to those violations.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP is Vietnamese legislation governing road traffic violations and penalties in VIETNAM. Its penalties are stated in Vietnamese đồng. The decree’s Clause 8 excludes international driving permits or licenses issued by Vietnam from the specified license-related violation. A cited provision also requires vehicles to be re-exported from Vietnam.

Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out administrative penalties and remedial measures for administrative violations. Article 4 addresses the limitation periods for sanctioning such violations, including both completed and ongoing violations.
Drivers are expressly required to undergo periodic health examinations. These examinations are identified as a remedial measure.
Administrative sanctioning is the process of applying penalties for an administrative violation. It refers to the measures imposed in response to such a violation.
Organizations may be identified as having committed an administrative violation based on collected technical results. They may also commit the administrative violations described in Article 31.
Individuals may be identified as having committed an **ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATION** based on collected technical results. They may also commit the administrative violations described in Article 31.
Article 5 is a provision within Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.

Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government decree that amends and supplements regulations on road traffic, permits and transport-related procedures. Its provisions address priority-vehicle signal devices, intelligent traffic vehicles, and foreign motor vehicles operating in Vietnam.

Articles 6 and 8 amend rules for installing and managing signal devices on priority vehicles and for issuing or reissuing permits to use them. Article 17 sets transitional rules for administrative-procedure files received or postmarked before the decree takes effect, and for existing permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles. The decree’s text also includes the heading for Article 7 and refers to Article 9, although the available descriptions do not specify their subject matter.

Article 12 adds Article 25a, setting out procedures to issue, exchange, reissue and revoke operating permits for intelligent traffic vehicles. Article 13 amends Article 33, including requirements for approving foreign motor vehicles entering Vietnam for tourism and right-hand-drive cars participating in traffic. Article 15 amends and supplements certain clauses of Article 35.

Article 18 addresses the decree’s entry into force and related implementation matters. It provides for procedures to approve international travel service businesses that organize foreign visitors bringing foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism, as well as procedures for bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam for non-tourism purposes. It also concerns databases on foreign motor vehicles driven by foreign nationals in Vietnam and on transport businesses and transport-business vehicle insignia. The relevant provisions take effect on 1 July 2027.
Article 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP addresses administrative violations, covering applicable administrative penalties and the remedial measures for those violations.
The 1968 Convention on Road Traffic is a United Nations convention associated with the United Nations.
Article 6 is a provision of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It specifies penalties for certain road traffic violations.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP addresses penalties for drivers of vehicles registered to operate in an INTERNATIONAL BORDER-GATE ECONOMIC ZONE. It also provides that, as a remedial measure for an administrative violation, a vehicle may be required to return to an INTERNATIONAL BORDER-GATE ECONOMIC ZONE.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP prescribes monetary fines for drivers who commit the road traffic violations covered by the decree. The applicable MONETARY FINE depends on the specified violation.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP refers to the LAW ON HANDLING ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATIONS as the legal basis for several enforcement procedures. Article 48 cites Article 125 of the Law as the basis for temporarily seizing or detaining vehicles—and, where applicable, related documents—before a penalty decision is issued. The decree also provides that the procedure for returning altered licenses and certificates is to follow Article 85 of the Law, and refers to Clause 1 of Article 6 as the basis for determining the limitation period for sanctioning an administrative violation.
Article 6 addresses the deduction of driving-license points as a penalty measure for specified road traffic violations.

Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is a Vietnamese government legal instrument governing road traffic penalties in Vietnam. It distinguishes permits issued by Vietnam from international permits issued by other participating countries.

Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is a provision of the decree that establishes penalties for specified road traffic violations and contains related licence-point provisions. Article 48 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP refers to specified clauses and points of Article 6.
The decree concerning the 1968 Convention on Road Traffic distinguishes international driving permits issued by Vietnam from permits issued by countries participating in the convention.

Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out the driving-license point deductions that apply to specified road-traffic violations. Its title identifies the article’s subject as driving-license point deductions for those violations.

DECREE 168/2024/ND-CP sets out rules for determining the limitation period and status of an ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATION. It also prescribes corrective measures to address the consequences of an administrative violation.
Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP sets out penalties for traffic violations and deductions from driving-licence points. It is part of the decree and is referenced by Articles 41 and 48.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP provides for driving-license point deductions as a penalty for specified road-traffic violations. Its provisions address deductions for covered violations in Articles 6 and 7, while Article 20 also concerns point deductions for violations within its scope. Article 32 addresses sanctions and point deductions for specified road-traffic violations; Clause 21 provides for a four-point deduction in the circumstances it specifies.
A driver commits the violation of turning around in a road tunnel by turning a vehicle around inside the tunnel.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 6, Clause 3, establishes a fine of 800,000 to 1,000,000 VND for the described lighting violation.
The driver commits a violation by reversing a vehicle inside a road tunnel.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP prescribes a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng for the listed traffic violations. This fine range is set out in Article 7, Clause 3.
Article 6 is a provision of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. It is also referenced in Article 41, Clause 2 of the decree.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP establishes a fine of 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND in Clause 5 of Article 6.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP treats specified acts of illegal stopping or parking as road traffic violations subject to penalties. Article 8, clause 2 sets out a fine for this violation; the available information does not specify the fine amount or the particular acts covered.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP, in Article 6, provides penalties, including a fine, for vehicle operators who cause a ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT and fail to fulfill the duties required of them afterward.

The records identify the **VEHICLE OPERATOR** as the person who operated a vehicle involved in the **ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT**. The operator is described as causing the accident and is subject to the duties set out in the text that follows.
Article 6, Clause 5 is a provision of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.
Article 6, Clause 4 treats making a U-turn where prohibited by a traffic sign as a punishable traffic violation and provides for a fine, subject to the clause’s stated exceptions.

Decree 168/2024/ND-CP establishes driving-license point deduction as a penalty measure for specified traffic violations. Its provisions address point deductions in Articles 6, 7, 13, 14, 17, 20, and 27. The available descriptions do not specify the number of points deducted under each article; in particular, they note that the excerpts for Articles 7 and 27 give no specific deduction amount.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP provides for deduction of points from drivers’ licenses as a sanction for specified road-traffic violations. Articles 6 and 7 address point deductions for the violations they cover. The decree also includes point deductions among the penalties addressed in Article 30, while Article 32 concerns penalties, including deductions, for vehicle-owner violations. Overall, the decree establishes driver’s-license point deduction as a sanction applicable to covered violations.
The provision concerns a DRIVER whose specified traffic-rule violation causes a TRAFFIC ACCIDENT. It also sets out the driver’s duties following the accident.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP establishes penalties and consequences for specified ROAD TRAFFIC RULE VIOLATION, including violations committed by drivers of cars and similar vehicles.
Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP specifies a fine of 30,000,000 to 40,000,000 VND for drivers who commit the violations listed in the article.
ROAD TRAFFIC RULE VIOLATIONS result in DRIVING-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION from the driver’s license.

Article 7 of **DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP** prescribes a fine of **4,000,000 to 6,000,000 VND** for the specified traffic violation or violations. The descriptions do not identify which violations are covered.
A driver or operator involved in a road traffic accident must promptly report it to the nearest police authority.
Article 6 addresses penalties for specified road traffic rule violations, including violations committed by drivers of specified vehicles.
DECREE 168/2024/ND-CP, in Article 6, prescribes penalties, including fines, for specified driving violations when those violations cause a ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT.

Article 7 sets out the penalties and driving-license point deductions for violations committed by drivers of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP classifies REFUSAL TO COMPLY WITH AN ALCOHOL TEST as a traffic violation. A driver who refuses an alcohol-concentration test requested by an on-duty official is subject to a fine of 30,000,000 to 40,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP specifies a fine for reversing on an expressway. The rule does not apply to priority vehicles reversing while performing emergency duties.

Under **DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP**, penalties for **DRIVING 10–20 KM/H OVER THE SPEED LIMIT** are addressed in provisions that depend on the vehicle type: Article 6, Clause 5 applies to drivers of cars and similar vehicles, while Article 7 addresses drivers of motorcycles and similar vehicles. DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP establishes penalties for vehicle operators who commit specified road-traffic violations. For penalty purposes, a vehicle operator who is the spouse of the registered vehicle holder is treated as a vehicle owner.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP specifies a fine for DRIVING AGAINST TRAFFIC ON AN EXPRESSWAY, except when a priority vehicle is performing emergency duties.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP specifies a fine for MAKING A U-TURN ON AN EXPRESSWAY. The prohibition and fine do not apply to priority vehicles making a U-turn while performing emergency duties.

Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP addresses the deduction of driving-license points as a penalty for specified road-traffic violations.

DECREE 168/2024/ND-CP establishes penalties for road traffic violations, including the specified ROAD TRAFFIC VIOLATION. Under Article 6, clause 3, it sets a fine for that violation. The available information does not state the fine amount.

Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP addresses driving-license point deductions for specified violations. Driving-license point deduction is a sanction under the article, but the provided descriptions do not specify how many points are deducted for any particular violation.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP establishes a FINE OF 400,000–600,000 VND for certain violations. Article 7, clause 2 specifies this fine for the violations listed there, while Article 9, clause 4 sets the same fine for the violation described in that provision.
Article 7, the “Penalty Provisions” section of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, sets out penalties for the traffic violations described in the decree.
FAILURE TO YIELD WHILE TURNING occurs when a MOTORCYCLE OR MOPED DRIVER turns without yielding as required. The rule applies to drivers of motorcycles, mopeds, or similar vehicles.

DECREE 168/2024/ND-CP provides for DRIVER’S LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION as a penalty for specified road traffic violations. DECREE 168/2024/ND-CP, under Article 34, Clause 3, prescribes a fine of 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 VND for the specified violation or violations. The descriptions provided do not identify the underlying conduct.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP provides a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 VND for violations covered by Article 12, Clause 5; Article 14, Clause 1; Article 36, Clause 2; and Article 7. The specific violations are not identified in the provided descriptions.
Article 7 provides for **DRIVER'S LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION** as a penalty for **ROAD TRAFFIC RULE VIOLATIONS BY MOTORCYCLE AND MOPED DRIVERS**.
**Failure to Obey Traffic Directions** is a violation in which a person does not comply with the commands, directions, orders, or instructions given by a **Traffic Controller**.

ARTICLE 7 PENALTY PROVISIONS address driving-license point deductions for the described drivers who commit covered violations. The DRIVING-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION is the penalty provided under Article 7 for those violations.
DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP establishes a FINE OF 8,000,000 TO 10,000,000 VND for the specified traffic violation.

The **ON-DUTY OFFICIAL** is the official who requests that the driver take an alcohol test. **REFUSAL TO COMPLY WITH AN ALCOHOL TEST** is the violation in which the driver fails to comply with that request.
Article 7 addresses the deduction of driving-license points for the specified traffic violations it covers.

DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP establishes sanctions for specified ROAD TRAFFIC VIOLATION offenses. Article 30 identifies people lacking civil act capacity as one of the groups participating in road traffic.
Article 35 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15. It is referenced by Article 88.
Under Law 36/2024/QH15, Article 30 identifies children among the groups participating in road traffic, and clause 2 specifically regulates their participation.

People with disabilities are identified as a group participating in road traffic, and their participation is regulated by the provision.

The VEHICLE LICENSE PLATE AUCTION WINNER is the person who won the VEHICLE LICENSE PLATE AUCTION for a vehicle license plate.

LAW NO. 36/2024/QH15 assigns regulatory responsibilities concerning vehicle inspections to the Minister of Transport. Under Article 42(5), the Minister is directed to provide detailed regulations for Article 34.
Article 35 refers to Clause 1 of Article 35 as the source of the conditions that vehicles must meet. Clause 1 sets out the applicable vehicle conditions.

Drivers and vehicles covered by the law must comply with applicable Vietnamese road-traffic and safety requirements.

Article 57, Clause 6 addresses the validity within Vietnam’s territory of qualifying driving licences. The law also provides for issuing international driving permits to eligible residents who hold valid driving licences.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 sets restrictions on motorcycle and moped drivers in Article 33. Article 56(1) establishes a general driving-licence requirement but excludes the motorcycle drivers specified in Article 56(4). Article 33 concerns PASSENGER safety and conduct. Clause 4 specifies prohibited conduct, including carrying passengers in designated unsafe positions.

The WINNER OF A VEHICLE LICENSE PLATE AUCTION is the person identified as having won the VEHICLE LICENSE PLATE AUCTION. The winner is subject to the auction’s payment deadline and any related obligations.
Article 39 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15 and forms part of that law.

LAW NO. 36/2024/QH15 assigns provincial-level People’s Committees two related local regulatory responsibilities. Representative Agencies of International Organizations are agencies that act on behalf of and represent International Organizations.

In a vehicle license plate auction, participants who meet the stated registration and bidding conditions compete to acquire a license plate. The winning bidder is the participant selected under those conditions who wins the auction and pays the winning bid amount.
Article 34 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15 and forms part of that law.
Article 39 of Law 36/2024/QH15 addresses the procedures for issuing and revoking vehicle registration certificates and license plates.
Article 42 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15 and forms part of that law.

Article 42 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15.
Article 45 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15.

Article 43 of LAW 36/2024/QH15 specifies the responsibilities of vehicle inspection establishments.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 addresses the revocation of vehicle registration certificates and license plates in Article 39. Clause 6 of that article specifies circumstances in which those certificates and plates are revoked.
Article 45 is a provision of Law No. 36/2024/QH15.

Under **Law 36/2024/QH15**, the **Government of Vietnam** is responsible for providing detailed regulations for Article 77 and prescribing the implementation roadmap for requirements on recording within motor-vehicle passenger compartments. In addition, Article 61 refers to conditions for driver examination centers as prescribed by the Government.

The Minister of National Defense is the head and ministerial office of the Ministry of National Defense, and acts on the Ministry’s behalf in prescribing procedures specified in the relevant provision. The MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT’s Minister is authorized and tasked with prescribing the procedure for the TEMPORARY SUSPENSION OF OPERATIONS of inspection establishments.
Article 46 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15 and forms part of that law.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 addresses TECHNICAL SAFETY AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION CERTIFICATION in Article 41. Article 41, paragraph 2 (clause 2), specifies that the certification covers technical safety and environmental protection quality, as well as motor vehicle energy consumption.

The Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of National Defense share several vehicle-related regulatory responsibilities.
