Each ministry’s minister prescribes inspection and certification procedures for vehicles under that ministry’s management. Both ministries issue driving licenses subject to the same exchange and reissuance rules, and they jointly prescribe the training program and standards described in the relevant provisions.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 sets requirements for VEHICLE REGISTRATION. Registration of a vehicle involved in a violation cannot be completed while the related administrative matter remains unresolved. A winning bidder for an auctioned vehicle registration plate must register a vehicle to attach the plate within the prescribed deadline.
Article 47 is a provision and section of Law 36/2024/QH15.

Under LAW 36/2024/QH15, provincial-level People’s Committees have authority over certain transport operating conditions in their localities. Article 44 provides that they set the permitted operating hours for specified vehicles, while Article 48 assigns them responsibility for regulating the times and geographic scope of specified passenger and goods transport activities.
Article 49 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15 and forms part of that law.
Article 50 is a provision within Law 36/2024/QH15 and forms part of that law.
Article 48 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15.

Under LAW 36/2024/QH15, drivers of passenger transport cars are responsible for complying with the road traffic rules set out in Chapter II, as provided in Clause 2 of Article 45. Article 46 also requires educational institutions to instruct drivers in safe transportation procedures.
Article 52 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15.
Article 55 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15.
The Traffic Police Agency of the Ministry of Public Security belongs to and is associated with the Ministry of Public Security.
Law 36/2024/QH15 was passed by the National Assembly of Vietnam. Its “QH15” designation identifies it as a law adopted by Vietnam’s 15th National Assembly.
A specialized motorcycle operator participates in road traffic while operating a specialized motorcycle.
Article 57 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15 and forms part of that law.

Under **Law 36/2024/QH15**, the **Traffic Police (CẢNH SÁT GIAO THÔNG)** are assigned responsibilities and powers in several areas. Article 52 assigns them to patrol, control and direct traffic, and handle violations involving specified vehicles on roads. Article 68 sets out duties and powers related to their decisions and requests, including the ability to request assistance in urgent situations.

The Government of Vietnam is the national government of Vietnam and is responsible for regulating matters within the country. Under the stated electronic-visa requirement, it determines which international border gates may be used for entry into Vietnam.

Under **LAW 36/2024/QH15**, the **COMPETENT AUTHORITY** is responsible for licensing the operation of vehicles that meet the conditions set out in Article 35. Article 56 also provides that a valid driving licence must be issued by the COMPETENT AUTHORITY.

LAW NO. 36/2024/QH15 assigns the Traffic Police a range of road-safety, enforcement, and institutional responsibilities. Under Article 53, the Traffic Police are responsible for patrolling, inspecting, and handling violations involving specified cargo vehicles. Article 65 sets out their powers when conducting road-traffic patrols and controls, while Clause 4 of that article specifies their duties during those activities. Article 70 identifies equipment the Traffic Police may use and establishes the legal rules governing its use.

The law also requires people temporarily using roadways or sidewalks to comply with Traffic Police requirements (Article 77). Under Article 79, the Traffic Police have responsibilities and powers to address risks to road infrastructure, unsafe road works, and traffic arrangements. Finally, Article 87 assigns responsibility for developing the Traffic Police into a regular, elite, and modern force.

Foreign nationals who enter, exit, transit through, or reside in Vietnam may participate in road traffic there, including by operating foreign-registered motor vehicles. Those driving foreign motor vehicles must comply with the applicable traffic requirements while in Vietnam. Foreign nationals may also bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism, subject to the approval process described in the relevant amendment. Vietnamese rules determine how long foreign nationals may participate in traffic and permit a limited additional period in specified circumstances.
LAW NO. 36/2024/QH15 is Vietnamese legislation that sets out road traffic requirements applicable in Vietnam, including requirements for certain foreign vehicles.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 references the VIENNA CONVENTION in Article 57, clause 8. It specifies that an international driving permit must be issued by the competent authority of a country that is a party to the VIENNA CONVENTION, and sets requirements for permits issued by those countries.

Article 56 of LAW 36/2024/QH15 specifies the documents drivers must carry when driving a vehicle mortgaged to a CREDIT INSTITUTION. These documents include a valid receipt issued by the CREDIT INSTITUTION.

Article 57 of LAW 36/2024/QH15 assigns the MINISTRY OF NATIONAL DEFENSE’s Minister responsibility for prescribing regulations on driver’s licenses used by military forces while performing national defense duties.

The Ministry of National Defense is a Vietnamese government ministry. It coordinates procedures for foreign motor vehicles participating in traffic in Vietnam and is a partner in managing activities involving foreign nationals and vehicles brought into the country.

Under **LAW 36/2024/QH15**, a **DRIVER** participating in road traffic must meet the age, health, and driving-licence requirements established in Article 56(1). A driver transporting goods by automobile must also comply with the safety rules set out in Article 49.
Article 56 of LAW 36/2024/QH15 addresses the documents drivers must carry when a vehicle is mortgaged to a FOREIGN BANK BRANCH. These include a valid receipt issued by the branch.

Article 57 assigns authority over driver’s-license rules for police forces performing national security duties to the Minister of Public Security, rather than the Minister of Transport. The Ministry of Transport’s database responsibilities also exclude specified data concerning the police forces, their vehicles, and their personnel.

The MINISTRY OF NATIONAL DEFENSE, through its Minister, prescribes the rules governing the format, issuance procedures, and use of driving licenses for MILITARY FORCES performing national defense duties.
Article 59 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15.

The Ministry of Public Security, through its Minister, regulates driving licences for police forces performing national defence and security duties. This includes prescribing the format, issuance procedures, and use of those licences, as well as setting rules for driver-training establishments and organizations that serve those police forces.
Article 60 is a provision of, and forms part of, Law 36/2024/QH15.

Article 57 assigns responsibility for setting driver’s-license rules for MILITARY FORCES performing national defense duties to the Minister of National Defense, rather than the Minister of Transport. The MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT’s database responsibilities also exclude specified information concerning the military forces, their vehicles, and their personnel.

The Ministry of Public Security is a government ministry of Vietnam. It is involved in managing activities concerning foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles brought into or driven in Vietnam. The Ministry handles procedures for foreign motor vehicles participating in road traffic and maintains a database about those vehicles. It also manages the application used to report convoy activities while vehicles are in traffic in Vietnam.

Through its Traffic Police Department, the Ministry participates in the approval framework for activities in Vietnam. It also performs entry and exit controls at Vietnam’s border gates and administers visas and temporary residence certification for foreign nationals entering the country.
ARTICLE 60 sets out requirements for DRIVER TRAINING, including related training requirements.
Article 67 is a provision of Vietnam’s Law 36/2024/QH15. It is cited by Article 65 in connection with the systems, vehicles, equipment, and data used for control.

Under **LAW 36/2024/QH15**, the **Minister of Public Security** is assigned a range of regulatory and implementation responsibilities. These include regulating driving licences and international driving permits (Article 57); specifying details required under clause 3 (Article 58); prescribing driver age requirements and driver training for police forces performing security duties (Articles 59 and 60); and regulating driving licences for those forces (Article 62). The law also authorizes the Minister to specify provisions and prescribe procedures (Article 65), issue technical regulations and prescribe rules concerning the systems described in the law (Article 71), and carry out additional responsibilities assigned under Article 75.

Under LAW 36/2024/QH15, the Minister of National Defense is responsible for regulating driving licenses for military forces performing national defense duties. The law also authorizes the Minister to prescribe age requirements for drivers in those forces and to establish their driver-training requirements.
The Minister of Public Security is authorized to prescribe driver training, minimum age requirements, and driving tests for Police Forces performing national security or security duties.

The Ministry of Public Security coordinates with the Ministry of Transport on the relevant management activities and is responsible for notifying the Ministry of Transport about specified violations, accidents, or incidents. The Ministry of Transport generally regulates driver training, while the Ministry of Public Security sets the rules for driver training for police forces performing defence and security duties.

The Ministry of National Defence regulates driving licences for military forces performing national-defence duties and establishes rules for driver-training establishments and organizations serving military forces engaged in national-defence and security duties. The Ministry, through its minister, also regulates these licences. It may issue, reissue, or revoke permits for signal devices on priority vehicles used by military forces performing emergency missions.
The Minister of National Defense is authorized to prescribe driver training, age requirements, and driving tests for the Military Forces when they perform national defense duties.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 sets out requirements and obligations for road vehicle operators. Article 59 addresses the age and health conditions of people operating vehicles in road traffic, while Article 72, Clause 2 specifies operators’ duties. The law also provides for enforcement measures and consequences when operators fail to obey a stop signal or order and flee.

Article 62 of LAW 36/2024/QH15 assigns the Minister of National Defence responsibility, jointly with the Minister of Public Security, for regulating driving licences for military and police forces performing national-defence and security duties. This includes the Minister of National Defence’s regulatory role concerning military personnel carrying out national-defence duties.
Article 66 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 addresses ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY PATROL AND CONTROL. Article 65, Clause 3 specifies which forces may conduct or participate in these patrol and control activities, while Article 65, Clause 6 sets out the principles that apply when they are carried out.
Article 65 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15 and forms part of that law.

Within the People’s Public Security, other forces and mobilized units coordinate with the Traffic Police in conducting patrol and control operations. The Traffic Police also perform other duties prescribed by the Law on People’s Public Security.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 sets out the role of the Traffic Police in road traffic safety and enforcement. Article 65 addresses the Traffic Police’s patrol and control activities, including the procedures they follow and the powers and duties they exercise during operations. Article 69 authorizes the Traffic Police to arrange for the removal of vehicles stopped or parked in violation of road rules. Under Article 79, the Traffic Police also have responsibilities when risks to road infrastructure or safety are reported or discovered.
The Traffic Police are responsible for investigating and resolving road traffic accidents in accordance with the law. They also receive statistics concerning people injured in these accidents.

ROAD TRAFFIC PATROL AND CONTROL is an activity carried out by the TRAFFIC POLICE under the procedures provided in Article 65. During patrol and control, the Traffic Police observe road traffic conditions, road users, vehicles, and security and order along road routes. They conduct inspections and exercise their powers to maintain traffic order and safety, while guiding and encouraging road users to comply with traffic laws.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 addresses road traffic patrol and control in Article 65. The article sets out the patrol and control activities carried out to maintain road traffic order and safety, the powers available during those activities, and—under clause 4—the duties undertaken as part of them.
The Traffic Police Force manages and operates a system that is connected to related agencies and shares information and data with them.
The NATIONAL TRAFFIC COMMAND CENTER is included in the TRAFFIC COMMAND CENTER system. In other words, the TRAFFIC COMMAND CENTER system includes the NATIONAL TRAFFIC COMMAND CENTER.
ILLEGAL STOPPING OR PARKING occurs when a vehicle stops or parks in violation of traffic rules. It may create a ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT RISK by obstructing or disrupting road traffic.
The Traffic Police carry out ROAD-TRAFFIC PATROL AND CONTROL activities to maintain road-traffic order and safety.
The Provincial Traffic Command Center is part of the Traffic Command Center system, which includes provincial traffic command centers.

The Traffic Police carry out or arrange the removal of a violating vehicle. If the vehicle’s driver or owner obstructs or resists its removal, the Traffic Police take appropriate measures to address the obstruction or resistance.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 establishes provisions concerning the TRAFFIC COMMAND CENTER. Article 71 requires relevant road-traffic monitoring systems to connect to the traffic command center. Article 75 defines the traffic command center system and its national, provincial, and centrally governed city components. Article 75, Clause 4, specifies the center’s authority to connect to and share data with designated entities, systems, and databases.
Article 79 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 assigns the POLICE AGENCY responsibilities under Article 76 for responding to specified road-traffic situations, including qualifying unexpected situations that it discovers or is informed about. Under Article 82, insurance enterprises coordinate with the POLICE AGENCY to arrange rescue vehicles when necessary.

The road management agency leads efforts to identify the causes of traffic congestion and coordinates measures to prevent, resolve, and remedy it. It takes action within the scope of its authority to address congestion and improve traffic flow.

Article 76(3) assigns the POLICE AGENCY and the ROAD ADMINISTRATION AGENCY responsibility for responding to qualifying unexpected road-traffic situations, with each agency acting according to its respective functions and duties. Both agencies share responsibility for responding to the same type of situation.

Article 75(4), also referred to as Clause 4, provides that the Traffic Command Center may connect to and share data with ministries and sectors. This permission applies to traffic command centers generally.

The police agency must promptly notify the competent authority when an incident exceeds its capacity, authority, functions, or duties. When necessary, it must also report the accident so the competent authority can mobilize additional personnel and vehicles.
The **POLICE AGENCY** must act within its functions and duties when it detects or discovers a qualifying **UNEXPECTED ROAD-TRAFFIC DISRUPTION**, or receives information about one.
The PERSON RELATED TO THE ACCIDENT is explicitly identified as being connected to the ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT and has responsibilities arising from it.

The **PERSON PRESENT AT THE ACCIDENT SCENE** is the person identified by their presence at the scene of the **ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT**. Under Article 80, the person has responsibilities relating to the accident and must provide relevant information about it when requested.

The Road Management Agency must notify the Traffic Police Agency of the results of corrective actions taken to address road safety hazards. The two agencies must also coordinate on measures to address traffic congestion.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 assigns the ROAD ADMINISTRATION AGENCY responsibilities under Article 76 for responding to specified road traffic situations. Under Article 76(3), these responsibilities include promptly remedying certain damage to road infrastructure.

The PERSON RELATED TO THE ACCIDENT is responsible for assisting the INJURED PERSON. An exception to the requirement to remain at the scene allows the PERSON RELATED TO THE ACCIDENT to leave in order to take the INJURED PERSON for emergency medical care.
The records contain information about the RELATED PERSON, who is connected with the ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT. They also assign responsibilities to the RELATED PERSON in connection with the accident.
The DRIVER CAUSING THE ACCIDENT is identified as the person who caused the ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT and has responsibilities related to it.

The PERSON RELATED TO THE ACCIDENT is instructed to report the accident to the nearest POLICE AGENCY. They are generally required to remain at the scene until police personnel arrive. In specified exceptions, they must instead promptly report the accident to a POLICE AGENCY.
When specified circumstances apply, the person related to the accident must promptly report it to the nearest People’s Committee.

Article 80 addresses the responsibilities of RELATED PERSONS in connection with a ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT. It identifies these persons as being related to the accident and establishes that they have responsibilities concerning it.

The ACCIDENT SCENE is the location where the incident occurred. POLICE ARRIVAL AT THE ACCIDENT SCENE is the event of police personnel arriving at that location, which ends the general requirement to remain there.

The ROAD VEHICLE OPERATOR is the person who causes or is involved in the ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT. The provision focuses on an operator who causes the accident and recognizes that the operator has responsibilities arising from it, including responsibilities at the accident scene.
The **ACCIDENT SCENE** is the location where the **ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT** occurs. The scene should be preserved, particularly when the accident has resulted in a fatality.
People Present at the Accident Scene are those at the location where the Road Traffic Accident occurs. They are addressed by Article 80 and have responsibilities at the accident scene.

The entities **INVESTIGATION AND RESOLUTION OF ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENTS** and **ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENTS** concern the process of investigating and resolving road traffic accidents. Article 83 addresses this subject.
A road traffic accident investigation and resolution is the process of examining and resolving a road traffic accident. It determines the accident’s circumstances, consequences, causes, and fault.
The DECEASED PERSON died as a result of the ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT. The accident scene should be preserved, and the deceased person’s body should be covered.
The records include information about the accident victim, who was injured in the road traffic accident and may be taken for emergency care.

The **Investigation and Resolution of Road Traffic Accidents** process concerns investigating and resolving **Road Traffic Accidents**, including accidents involving personnel or vehicles of diplomatic, consular, or international-organization representative agencies.

Information relating to the ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT must be provided to the COMPETENT AUTHORITY. The COMPETENT AUTHORITY may request information about the accident from people present at the scene and may mobilize forces and vehicles to resolve it.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 addresses the response to a ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT. Article 82 concerns rescue and recovery following an accident. Article 83 sets out rules for investigating and resolving accidents; under Clause 2, this includes checking injuries, vehicles, drivers, passengers, cargo, and related documents.

A ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT that shows signs of a CRIMINAL OFFENSE is investigated and resolved under criminal law and criminal procedure law. The presence of those signs determines whether these laws and procedures apply.

When a road traffic accident occurs, the driver has responsibilities related to the incident. A provision also addresses testing the driver of a vehicle involved in road traffic in connection with a report of the accident.

When a road traffic accident is discovered, the police agency must be notified promptly. After receiving a report, the agency dispatches personnel to the scene to take prescribed measures and help address the incident. At the scene, the police agency leads and coordinates rescue and relief operations and, when necessary, arranges for rescue vehicles.
Diplomatic missions in Vietnam are the subject of a provision concerning accidents involving their personnel and vehicles within the country.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 addresses road traffic accidents in Articles 83 and 84. Article 83 sets out the investigation and resolution of road traffic accidents, with clause 2 specifying related procedures. Article 84 concerns statistics on road traffic accidents.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 addresses the investigation and resolution of road traffic accidents. Article 83 establishes the relevant procedures, with Clause 2 specifying the process for investigating and resolving such accidents.
Article 86 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15.
CONSULAR AGENCIES are located in VIETNAM. The provision concerns accidents in Vietnam involving the agencies’ personnel and vehicles.
Article 89 of Law 36/2024/QH15 contains the law’s transitional provisions.
Article 89 is a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15. It sets out transitional provisions, including those specified in Clause 3.
Article 86 sets out provisions concerning the state management of road traffic order and safety.
LAW 36/2024/QH15 takes effect on January 1, 2025, except as provided in Clause 2 of Article 88. Its transitional provision applies to licences issued before the law takes effect.
The Traffic Police Agency leads and coordinates statistical work concerning road traffic accidents. It compiles accident statistics and maintains a database about road traffic accidents.
Article 71 is a provision within Law 36/2024/QH15.

The Road Traffic Accident Damage Mitigation Fund is established to mitigate harm and damage caused by Road Traffic Accidents. It mobilizes social resources for this purpose and may support both accident victims and people who assist those injured.

Article 89 of **Law 36/2024/QH15** provides that certain auction cases already underway must continue to be handled under **Resolution 73/2022/QH15**. The resolution otherwise ceases to be effective when the law takes effect, subject to the exception set out in Clause 7 of Article 89.

The Ministry of Public Security must notify the Ministry of National Defence about the specified incidents. The two ministries jointly regulate driving licences for military and police personnel performing national-defence and security duties.
The Ministry of Public Security is responsible for building and developing the Traffic Police force into a regular, elite, and modern force.

CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA is a circular issued by Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security. The “TT-BCA” designation in its identifier associates it with the Ministry, with “BCA” referring to the Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 assigns the Ministry of Education and Training responsibilities in two areas. Under Article 6, the Ministry leads the development and integration of road traffic law knowledge into educational curricula. Under Article 62, the Minister of Education and Training regulates procedures for specialized vehicle-operation certificates for specified tractor operators.

The traffic police are a unit of the police force. Their vehicles perform duties under the police force and are identified alongside police-force vehicles, including in the context of escort vehicles.

Article 85 of LAW 36/2024/QH15 addresses the ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT DAMAGE MITIGATION FUND. It sets out the Fund’s description and purpose, identifies activities for which it may be used, and specifies its operating principles in Clause 4. The Government is responsible for regulating the Fund’s establishment, management, and use.

The COMPETENT TESTING AUTHORITY is responsible for organizing and conducting the ROAD TRAFFIC LAW KNOWLEDGE TEST. It must also ensure that the facilities and equipment required for the test are available.

The **Ministry of Public Security**, through its minister, shares responsibility with the Minister of National Defense for regulating driving licences for military forces performing national-defence duties. The Minister of Public Security also has a joint role in regulating licences for military and police forces carrying out national-defence and security duties. This permit authority does not apply to military vehicles on emergency missions.

LAW 36/2024/QH15 assigns the Minister of Construction a range of regulatory responsibilities concerning road transport and vehicles. These include issuing national technical regulations on road signals (Article 11); regulating vehicle standards, certification procedures, and vehicle inspectors (Article 41); and issuing regulations on the specified road and vehicle matters under Article 52. The Minister is also responsible for rules governing oversized or overweight cargo and its transport by road (Article 53), as well as other regulatory responsibilities set out in Article 60.

Under Article 63, the Minister of Construction is responsible for specifying requirements for training, testing, and certification, and standards for training establishments. The law also gives the Ministry of Construction state-management responsibilities and authority to issue national technical regulations for child safety equipment (Article 87). In addition, goods transported by automobile must be secured in accordance with requirements prescribed by the Minister of Construction.

CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA is a regulation issued by the Ministry of Public Security. The “BCA” designation in its identifier refers to the Ministry of Public Security and identifies it as the issuing ministry. The circular concerns regulations on legal knowledge tests and the restoration of driver’s license points. It also directs the director of the Traffic Police Department to report the assigned work to the Ministry of Public Security’s leadership.
The ROAD TRAFFIC LAW KNOWLEDGE TEST is completed by TEST PARTICIPANTS using connected computers. Participants log in to the test software and complete the test.

The Traffic Police Department is a department of, and operates under, the Ministry of Public Security. It serves as a designated channel for applications and reports submitted to the ministry and is identified in connection with licensing authority, including the issuance, reissuance, and revocation of the specified permits. The department’s director reports to the Ministry of Public Security’s leadership on the department’s work concerning traffic-law knowledge-testing software. The ministry’s wide-area network (WAN) connects test computers to a server located at the Traffic Police Department.

CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA assigns the COMPETENT EXAMINATION AUTHORITY responsibilities under Articles 7 and 8. The authority receives examination applications, arranges retests, and announces examination schedules and locations.

The COMPETENT EXAMINATION AUTHORITY organizes and conducts the ROAD TRAFFIC LAW KNOWLEDGE EXAMINATION. It announces the examination schedule and location, retains related surveillance images, registration records, and examination minutes, and may handle requests for retesting.
The COMPETENT TESTING AUTHORITY may hire an INTERPRETER to assist a participant during the test or examination.
The COMPETENT AUTHORITY is responsible for publishing announcements of examination and test dates on the ELECTRONIC INFORMATION PORTAL within its management scope.

The Road Traffic Law Knowledge Examination is addressed by Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, which contains provisions governing the examination. The circular was issued under the designation of the Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam, and “BCA” in its identifier is the ministry’s abbreviation.

CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA sets out procedures for registering for and organizing the ROAD TRAFFIC LAW KNOWLEDGE TEST. Article 7 covers these procedures and requires the testing room to have secure camera surveillance, with image data stored.
Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA is a circular issued by the Ministry of Public Security (BCA); the “BCA” designation in its number identifies the ministry as the issuing authority.
CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA assigns relevant individuals responsibility for its implementation. Those individuals may also report any difficulties or obstacles they encounter while carrying it out.

Article 11 of CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA assigns responsibilities to the director of the TRAFFIC POLICE DEPARTMENT. Under clause 1, the director is responsible for matters relating to the traffic-law knowledge-testing software and for directing, inspecting, and urging the implementation of the circular.

CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA assigns the organizations concerned responsibility for implementing its provisions. Relevant organizations may also report any difficulties or obstacles they encounter during implementation.
Article 8 of **CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA** sets out the responsibilities of the **COMPETENT AUTHORITY** conducting the examination, including announcing the proposed examination dates.

The Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam is the issuer of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, which sets out requirements for registering for and organizing the Road Traffic Law Knowledge Test. Article 7 of the circular addresses the test’s registration and organization.

The Ministry of Public Security issues regulations governing theoretical driving tests and driver-licensing procedures. These regulations cover the requirements and processes associated with taking the Theoretical Driving Test and obtaining a driver’s license.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP provides detailed regulations and measures for implementing the LAW ON ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY. Article 14 of the decree directs that database connections and information sharing be carried out in accordance with the law. Article 26 sets conditions for rudimentary and other non-motorized vehicles, referring to Article 34 of the law for the applicable requirements. The decree also refers to Article 27, Clause 1, of the law to identify which vehicles may be equipped with priority-vehicle signal devices.
The children addressed by the education provisions attend preschool educational institutions, which provide them with the specified road-traffic education.
Educational institutions teach primary school students road traffic legal knowledge, providing them with the specified road traffic legal education.
DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP addresses SAFE MOTORBIKE-RIDING SKILLS GUIDANCE in Article 5, which sets out the guidance’s contents.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP, in Article 7, identifies preschool educational institutions as settings covered by its provisions on legal instruction and compliance with road traffic laws. It provides for educating children in these institutions about road traffic law, order, and safety.
Commune-Level Police must forward valid examination applications to the Traffic Police Division within one working day of receiving them.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP includes vocational education institutions among the educational settings covered by its provisions. It addresses road traffic order and safety legal education for students at these institutions. Article 6, Clause 4 sets out responsibilities for vocational education institutions, while Article 8 concerns how they organize legal education and manage compliance with legal requirements.

Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP sets out road traffic legal education content to be delivered in educational institutions. Under Article 4, Clause 4, it specifies content for students in upper-secondary and vocational education settings.
SAFE MOTORBIKE RIDING SKILLS GUIDANCE is intended for students beginning upper-secondary education or attending vocational education institutions.
Article 5 is a provision and part of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP.

Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, issued by the Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam, sets out requirements for the Legal Knowledge Test on road traffic order and safety. It addresses the test’s content, method, duration, questions, and results.
REGISTERED EXAMINEES are the people who have registered to take the ROAD TRAFFIC LAW KNOWLEDGE EXAMINATION. They are the individuals who sit for the examination.
The guidance applies to students who are beginning their studies at upper secondary schools.
Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP sets out responsibilities for high schools in Article 6, Clause 4 and specifies legal education content on road traffic order and safety for high school students.
SAFE MOTORBIKE-RIDING SKILLS GUIDANCE is intended for students, particularly those beginning upper secondary or vocational education. It teaches students the skills needed to ride motorbikes safely.

STUDENTS’ FAMILIES are responsible for helping provide STUDENTS with road-traffic education and safe-riding instruction. They should also remind STUDENTS to honor their signed commitments and stay informed about whether they comply with traffic laws.
SAFE MOTORBIKE RIDING SKILLS GUIDANCE is intended for students beginning their studies at vocational education institutions. These students are among the guidance’s recipients.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP identifies the MINISTRY OF LABOUR, INVALIDS AND SOCIAL AFFAIRS as a partner in developing safe motorbike-riding instruction for students under Article 6. Article 8 sets out the ministry’s responsibilities. The available descriptions do not specify the details of those responsibilities.
SAFE MOTORBIKE-RIDING SKILLS GUIDANCE is intended for students beginning vocational education. VOCATIONAL EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS are responsible for providing or supporting this guidance.

Article 8 of DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP sets out the responsibilities of the MINISTRY OF LABOUR, INVALIDS AND SOCIAL AFFAIRS for organizing road traffic law education and overseeing legal compliance at vocational education institutions.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP assigns the Ministry of Education and Training responsibilities for preparing and coordinating instruction, and for leading and directing that work. Under Article 7, the Ministry is also responsible for promoting education on road traffic laws in educational institutions and overseeing their compliance with laws on road traffic order and safety.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP names the MINISTRY OF EDUCATION AND TRAINING as a partner in developing safe motorbike-riding instruction for students under Article 6. Article 7 assigns the Ministry responsibilities related to road traffic law instruction and the management of compliance with those requirements.
High schools are assigned responsibility for providing or supporting safe motorbike-riding skills guidance.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP, through Article 8, addresses teaching and compliance-management activities at vocational education institutions. It assigns these institutions responsibility for organizing students and their families to sign commitments to comply with road-traffic rules.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP assigns the Ministry of Public Security a range of responsibilities related to road traffic management. Under Article 36, the Ministry coordinates relevant management activities and procedures; Article 36, Clause 1 also assigns it responsibility for inspecting and handling the specified violations.

Article 6 gives the Ministry the lead role in developing safe motorbike-riding instruction for students. Under Article 7, it coordinates with the Ministry of Education and Training on the responsibilities set out there.

The decree also assigns the Ministry responsibility for building and managing specified specialized databases. Information for the road traffic database is collected through a connection with the Ministry’s database, and funding for the database is allocated to the Ministry. The decree further identifies the Ministry’s public service portal as a channel for submitting the required notice and the Traffic Police Department under the Ministry as the authority that receives applications.

High schools assess students’ conduct partly by their compliance with road traffic orders and safety laws. They also remind students to honor their signed commitments and monitor whether they follow traffic laws.

The Ministry of Public Security builds and manages the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database. The database collects relevant information through a connection to the Ministry of Public Security’s database.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP establishes provisions concerning the ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE. Article 9 sets out principles for building, managing, using, connecting to, and sharing the database. Article 11 specifies the information recorded in it, including vehicle inspection information and information about foreign vehicles and their drivers; its clauses identify further categories of information held in the database. Article 12 governs how that information is collected, including the collection process and the sources from which information is obtained. Article 14 addresses connecting to the database, sharing, accessing and extracting its information, and using the database.

Article 10 assigns complementary database-related responsibilities to the Ministry of Public Security and to other ministries and sectors. The Ministry of Public Security builds and manages the road traffic order and safety database, while the ministries and sectors must connect their databases to it and share relevant information.

Decree 151/2024/ND-CP assigns the Ministry of Transport responsibility under Article 10 for constructing and managing the specified specialized databases. It also requires approval documents to be sent to the ministry’s relevant functional units for coordination and management. The decree provides that the classification of intelligent transport vehicles, along with their safety and environmental quality certification, must comply with regulations issued by the Minister of Transport.
Article 11 is a provision of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government legal instrument establishing nationwide rules, including requirements for vehicle journey-monitoring equipment. Article 10 requires the databases covered by the decree to be developed in accordance with Vietnam’s e-government architecture framework.

Articles 32–34 address foreign motor vehicles and drivers participating in road traffic in Vietnam. The decree sets conditions and procedures for bringing certain foreign vehicles into Vietnam for tourism or other purposes, including temporary import and re-export through approved international border gates, and for obtaining or changing related approvals. It also covers responsibilities associated with vehicles entering or leaving Vietnam.

The decree regulates the use and circulation of foreign vehicles and right-hand-drive cars in Vietnam, including applicable approvals, procedures, and violations. It sets requirements for foreign nationals driving foreign vehicles, including compliance with Vietnamese traffic laws, valid driving licences, and insurance documentation. It also addresses related travel services and the management of foreign drivers and vehicles in Vietnamese traffic.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP governs the ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE. Article 9 establishes principles for the database’s development, creation, management, use, connection, sharing, and storage. Article 11 specifies the information held in the database, including health information, insurance information under Clause 8, and information on the handling of administrative violations under Clause 9; Clause 6 sets out additional categories of information. Article 12 governs how information is collected for the database, including the collection provisions in Clause 3 and the sources identified in the decree. Article 16 addresses funding for the database’s construction, operation, use, maintenance, and upgrading.

Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP governs aspects of the Database on Road Traffic Order and Safety. Article 11 specifies the information included in the database, including information on driver training and relevant certificates. Article 12, Clauses 4 and 5 address how information for the database is collected. Article 13 concerns updating the information held in the database.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP assigns the MINISTRY OF HEALTH responsibility under Article 10 for building and managing the specified health database. Under Article 20, ambulance permits are conditional on compliance with standards and use requirements regulated by the Minister of Health.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP assigns the MINISTRY OF FINANCE responsibility under Article 10, Clause 3 for building and managing specified specialized databases related to vehicles. Article 36 identifies the Ministry as a coordinating agency for relevant procedures and management activities. The decree also requires approval documents to be sent to the Ministry’s relevant functional units for coordination and management.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP provides that vehicles used by MILITARY FORCES on emergency missions are excluded from the permit authority specified in Article 23. It also excludes military-related data from Ministry of Transport databases concerning vehicle inspection, driver training and licensing, and vehicle operators.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP assigns the Ministry of National Defense several coordination and information-management roles. Under Article 36, the Ministry is a coordinating agency for specified procedures and management activities. The decree also makes it responsible for building and managing designated specialized databases, and provides that information for the road traffic database is collected through a connection with the Ministry’s database. Approval documents must be sent to the Ministry’s relevant functional units for coordination and management.
The ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE contains information about transport business units. The TRANSPORT BUSINESS UNIT is one of the information fields specified for records in the database.

The **ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE** stores information about the handling of administrative violations related to road traffic order and safety. It supports **ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATION HANDLING** by maintaining records of how these violations are processed.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP assigns the MINISTRY OF PUBLIC SECURITY a range of responsibilities involving databases, road traffic, and immigration. Under Article 10, the Ministry is responsible for building and managing specified specialized databases. Article 12 identifies a Ministry-built and -managed database as a source of collected information, while Article 15 provides that the database on road traffic order and safety is managed centrally and uniformly by the Ministry.

The decree also refers to the Ministry’s database of foreign motor vehicles driven by foreigners in Vietnam. Relevant vehicle and road-traffic information may be collected through connections to Ministry of Public Security databases. The Ministry is additionally named as a coordination partner in organizing and managing specified activities.

Under Article 36, the Ministry is responsible for border entry and exit controls, visa issuance, and certification of temporary residence, as well as related notification responsibilities.
Article 12 is a provision of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP and forms part of that decree.
The ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE contains information about DRIVER TRAINING, including available training courses and records of training completion.
The ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE records information about each DRIVER TRAINING COURSE, including its identifier, name, date, training distance, results, and completion information.
Article 11 addresses and describes the information held in the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database.

Nghị định 151/2024/NĐ-CP quy định về **Cơ sở dữ liệu về trật tự, an toàn giao thông đường bộ**. Khoản 8 Điều 11 xác định các thông tin được đưa vào cơ sở dữ liệu; Điều 12 quy định việc thu thập thông tin phục vụ cơ sở dữ liệu này.
Article 9 establishes the principles governing the construction, management, exploitation, use, connection, and sharing of the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database.
Article 17 is a provision of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP.
Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is a decree of the Government of Vietnam. Article 14 refers to Government regulations on the management, connection, and sharing of digital data.
Article 19 is a provision within Decree 151/2024/ND-CP.

DECREE NO. 151/2024/NĐ-CP assigns the MINISTRY OF PUBLIC SECURITY roles in two areas. Under Article 15, it identifies the Ministry as the body with which other government agencies coordinate on the database. Under Article 24, it gives the Ministry responsibilities concerning signal-emitting devices and permits for priority vehicles.

The ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE contains information about vehicle journeys and vehicle operating times, along with drivers’ names, driving licence numbers, and images of drivers. It relates this information to the DRIVER entity.
Vehicles serving the STEERING COMMITTEE may be used to carry out missions and other duties during an EMERGENCY SITUATION, including one that is legally defined as such.
Article 21 is a provision within Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP.
When an **EMERGENCY SITUATION** is declared, **FUNCTIONAL FORCES** may be mobilized to carry out their assigned duties.
APPLICANT AGENCIES AND ORGANIZATIONS may submit their applications or dossiers, along with supporting documents and written requests, through the POSTAL SERVICE.

Decree 151/2024/ND-CP sets out provisions for collecting information in the Database on Road Traffic Order and Safety. Article 12 specifically governs and specifies the collection of information for that database.

Under **Decree 151/2024/ND-CP**, the **competent authority** issues the permits required to use signal devices on priority vehicles under Article 17, Clause 3. Article 23 assigns the authority responsibility for permits and for tracking their issuance and revocation. The decree’s transitional provision also addresses programs approved by the competent authority before the decree took effect.
Article 21 of **DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP** establishes the procedure for issuing and reissuing permits and specifies the applicable deadline.
The PROCURACY FORCE’s vehicles are described as being used for EMERGENCY DUTY. The applicable rule covers these vehicles when they are used for emergency duties.

BỘ GIAO THÔNG VẬN TẢI (the Ministry of Transport) is identified in Nghị định 151/2024/NĐ-CP as the agency responsible for building and managing the vehicle-inspection database. Article 27 also addresses the sharing of vehicle-monitoring data with the Ministry.
Agencies and Organizations submit a single application dossier, consisting of one set of application documents, to the Competent Authority.
Article 25 is a provision within Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP.
The TRAFFIC POLICE DEPARTMENT’s stated permit authority does not cover MILITARY FORCES vehicles engaged in emergency or urgent missions.
The decree provides for the ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE and SPECIALIZED DATABASES to be connected and to share information in accordance with the law.
APPLICANT AGENCIES AND ORGANIZATIONS may submit their applications, supporting documents, and dossier directly to the COMPETENT AUTHORITY specified in Article 23.
The POSTAL SERVICE is a permitted channel for sending the application dossier and required documents to the COMPETENT LICENSING AUTHORITY.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP sets out rules for signal devices on priority vehicles performing duties during a legally defined EMERGENCY SITUATION. The permit for the relevant signaling equipment expires immediately when the emergency situation ends.
Article 32 is a provision of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP.
Article 32 is a provision of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP.
The LICENSING AUTHORITY is responsible for issuing the OPERATING PERMIT within the stated timeframe, provided the application is valid.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP assigns the MINISTRY OF NATIONAL DEFENSE responsibilities related to priority-vehicle signal equipment and the associated permits within its remit. The decree also assigns the Ministry’s Department of Military Vehicles and Transport the role of issuing permits for intelligent transport vehicles used for national defense purposes. In addition, the Ministry is identified as a coordination partner in organizing and managing the activities specified in the decree.
Participation in Traffic in Vietnam refers to foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles taking part in traffic within Vietnam. The activity takes place in Vietnam.

Under DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP, the COMPETENT LICENSING AUTHORITY is the authority responsible for receiving applicants’ dossiers under the prescribed application procedure. It is also the authority that previously granted approval: when violations occur, it may suspend the covered activities. The authority must be informed of a qualifying incident and must receive a written report once the incident has been resolved.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP sets out the responsibilities of the LICENSING AUTHORITY and the process for deciding permit applications. Under Article 21, the LICENSING AUTHORITY receives and reviews applications and notifies applicants when submissions are deficient or the applicants are ineligible.

Vietnamese international travel service businesses may organize foreigners to bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism and participate in traffic. They are responsible for ensuring that the foreigners follow the approved program and registered route, and for coordinating the required temporary-residence declarations in accordance with the law.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP sets conditions for FOREIGN NATIONALS operating foreign-registered motor vehicles in Vietnam for tourism. It also governs the approvals required for their entry with those vehicles and arrangements concerning delays to their departure from Vietnam.

The decree governs foreigners entering, staying in, and departing from Vietnam, including cases in which their departure is delayed or they exceed the maximum permitted stay. It also allows foreigners to bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism when the trip is organized by a Vietnamese international travel service business. Their vehicle activities, travel routes, and temporary-residence declarations are subject to applicable Vietnamese law.
Foreign drivers, including foreign nationals, participate in traffic in Vietnam by driving foreign motor vehicles.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP assigns the TRAFFIC POLICE DEPARTMENT responsibility for receiving and reviewing applications related to vehicle operations covered by the decree. Under Article 25, the department may issue operating permits for intelligent transport vehicles, except vehicles serving national defense purposes. Article 33 provides that applications for approval of the specified non-tourism vehicle activity must be submitted to the department. The department reviews applications and issues an approval or refusal.
Vietnamese international travel service businesses submit an application dossier to the Traffic Police Department seeking approval to organize the entry of foreign vehicles into Vietnam.

Decree 151/2024/ND-CP of Vietnam establishes procedures and conditions for foreign visitors and foreign motor vehicles entering, traveling in, staying in, or participating in traffic in Vietnam. It addresses approvals for specified vehicle-related activities, changes to information associated with those activities, and the possible suspension of activities while violations of Vietnamese law are resolved. It also sets transitional rules for programs involving foreign vehicles entering or being driven in Vietnam.

Article 32 concerns foreign vehicles and drivers participating in traffic in Vietnam. Article 33 governs approvals and information changes for specified vehicle-related activities. Article 34, Clause 3, sets requirements for foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam, including the requirement to comply with Vietnamese road traffic laws. Article 36 concerns the management of foreign nationals operating foreign motor vehicles in traffic in Vietnam.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP sets out requirements involving VIETNAMESE INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL SERVICE ENTERPRISES. Article 33, Clause 4 specifies the notice procedure for enterprises organizing trips for foreign visitors and vehicles. In specified cases, applicants must also submit applications for approval through a Vietnamese international travel service enterprise.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP sets out requirements and procedures for VIETNAMESE INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL SERVICE BUSINESSES that organize tourist trips to Vietnam for foreign nationals bringing foreign motor vehicles. Article 33 addresses the approval required for arranging these trips, while Article 35 establishes the businesses’ responsibilities in connection with the foreign vehicles and travelers.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP links its provisions to the LAW ON ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY. Article 14 of the decree provides that data connection and sharing must be carried out in accordance with that law. Article 25 refers to Article 34, Clause 4 of the law for the definitions of intelligent transport vehicles and the motor vehicles covered by the relevant provisions.

VIETNAMESE INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL SERVICE ENTERPRISES are Vietnamese businesses that provide international travel services. Under the rules governing activities in VIETNAM, they may organize the entry of foreign motor vehicles into the country for tourism and are responsible for fulfilling the obligations associated with traffic in VIETNAM.
FOREIGN VEHICLE TOURISM IN VIETNAM is a tourism activity in which foreign motor vehicles are brought into VIETNAM for tourism purposes.

The Traffic Police Department of Vietnam receives and processes applications for authorization to bring foreign vehicles into Vietnam and use them in traffic there. This includes applications involving foreign motor vehicles and, specifically, right-hand-drive cars seeking approval to participate in traffic for non-tourism purposes. The department handles the related approvals under the applicable procedure.

Vietnamese international travel service businesses organize vehicle-based tourism activities in Vietnam, including trips in which foreign nationals bring foreign motor vehicles into the country for tourism or other permitted purposes. These businesses and activities are subject to the applicable decree and must comply with Vietnam’s laws on foreigners’ entry, exit, transit, and residence, as well as other relevant laws.
Foreign tourists may travel in Vietnam with foreign motor vehicles, subject to the applicable approval procedures. Road-travel programs and routes in Vietnam are intended for foreign tourists.
The Traffic Police Department sends approval documents to the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism after an application is approved, enabling the two entities to coordinate management.

Foreign visitors may bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism, subject to the approval process and arrangements set out in the relevant regulation or decree. The provisions also address visitors’ travel and stay in Vietnam, including their departure and the maximum permitted length of stay. No specific approval requirements or time limits are stated in the descriptions.
Article 33 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP governs the approval procedures for foreign motor vehicles to enter or travel on roads in Vietnam and regulates their participation in traffic.

Individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam may seek approval to use those vehicles on Vietnamese roads for non-tourism purposes. These imports are intended for road traffic rather than tourism.

The Traffic Police Department sends approval documents to the Ministry of National Defence to coordinate management. When an application is approved, the department forwards the approval to the ministry for this purpose.

Vietnamese international travel service businesses may organize tourism trips for foreign nationals who bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam. They must also complete the required invitation and guarantee procedures for foreign nationals operating those vehicles when entering, exiting, or residing in Vietnam, except where the foreign nationals are visa-exempt.
The Traffic Police Department sends approval documents to the Ministry of Finance when an application is approved, enabling coordination in management.
The Traffic Police Department sends approval documents to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs after an application is approved, so the ministry can coordinate management.

The decree allows Vietnamese international travel service enterprises to organize trips in Vietnam for foreign visitors, including trips in which visitors enter the country with foreign motor vehicles for tourism.

Individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars must notify the competent licensing authority—the authority that previously granted approval—when specified arrangements change. They are responsible for ensuring that all information and documents submitted to the authority are accurate and lawful.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP assigns the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism a role in coordinating specified management activities under Article 36. The decree also makes the Ministry responsible for providing guidance on bringing foreign motor vehicles into traffic in Vietnam and requires approval documents to be sent to the Ministry’s relevant functional units for coordination and management.
The COMPETENT LICENSING AUTHORITY sends approval documents to the relevant functional units of the MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS for coordination and management.

Article 36 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP assigns the Ministry of Foreign Affairs a coordination responsibility. The decree also requires approval documents to be sent to the Ministry’s relevant functional units for coordination and management.

Under Decree 151/2024/ND-CP, the Competent Licensing Authority carries out the prescribed approval procedure. Notifications and supporting documents are sent to the authority that previously granted the approval.

The competent licensing authority receives written requests from Vietnamese international travel service enterprises and decides whether to approve the arrangements described in the decree. The enterprises must submit relevant documents and information to that authority. If covered arrangements or details change, they must notify the authority that previously granted approval and provide the required document. If an incident delays departure, the enterprises must promptly inform that authority and subsequently submit a written report.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP covers the approval process for individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam for use in traffic for non-tourism purposes. Article 33 addresses the handling of violations involving those individuals and vehicles.
The Competent Licensing Authority sends approval documents to the relevant functional units of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism for coordination and management.

Organizations Bringing Right-Hand-Drive Cars bring right-hand-drive vehicles into traffic in Vietnam for non-tourism purposes. They may seek approval to use these vehicles for non-tourism traffic in Vietnam.
Article 34 is a provision of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP.
The COMPETENT LICENSING AUTHORITY sends approval documents to the relevant functional units of the MINISTRY OF FINANCE for coordination and management.

Vietnamese International Travel Service Enterprises are responsible for ensuring the accuracy and legality of documents and information about foreign nationals included in their submissions. They may also organize tourism programs or trips in which foreign nationals bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP sets out rules applicable to VIETNAMESE INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL SERVICE ENTERPRISES. Article 33 addresses approval requirements and violation provisions relating to the enterprises’ travel arrangements, including the organization of foreign visitors’ vehicle trips in Vietnam. It also establishes duties to respond to incidents that delay a vehicle’s departure. Article 35 addresses the responsibilities of these enterprises.

Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP covers the approval process for organizations bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam for use in traffic for non-tourism purposes. Article 33 addresses the handling of violations involving those organizations.
Foreign national drivers who operate foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam while participating in traffic are subject to Vietnam’s road traffic order and safety laws.
DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP, in Article 35, addresses individuals who bring right-hand-drive cars into traffic in Vietnam for non-tourism purposes.

Decree 151/2024/ND-CP addresses Vietnamese international travel service businesses in two relevant provisions: Article 33 covers approval for these businesses to organize foreign visitors bringing vehicles into Vietnam for tourism, while Article 35 sets out the businesses’ responsibilities.
Article 35 is a provision of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and forms part of that decree.

Competent State Authorities may refuse or withhold approval for Vietnamese International Travel Service Businesses that fail to meet applicable requirements, violate relevant rules, or have not addressed specified incidents or violations. An authority that previously granted approval may also suspend the organized activity if a foreign participant has an unresolved violation.

Individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam for road use, for purposes other than tourism, must comply with the applicable security and public-order laws while using those vehicles in Vietnam.

The Ministry of Finance is a Vietnamese government institution named in the relevant regulation. It is identified as a partner in managing activities involving foreign nationals and motor vehicles brought into Vietnam, and it coordinates procedures for foreign motor vehicles participating in traffic in Vietnam.

Organizations Bringing Right-Hand-Drive Cars into Vietnam bring those vehicles into Vietnam for road use and purposes other than tourism. While the vehicles are in traffic, these organizations must comply with applicable Vietnamese laws on security and public order.

Article 35 of **DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP** identifies **organizations bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam for non-tourism purposes** as subject to the responsibilities set out in that provision. Its heading likewise identifies these organizations as covered by the article.
The “Entry and Exit of Foreign Motor Vehicles” event concerns foreign motor vehicles entering Vietnam and leaving Vietnamese territory.
Article 36 of DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP sets out the responsibilities of the relevant agencies and assigns them responsibility for implementing the decree.
Under **Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP**, Article 35 identifies individuals who bring right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam for non-tourism purposes as subject to the responsibilities set out in that article.
DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP, through Article 35, addresses organizations that bring right-hand-drive cars into traffic in Vietnam for non-tourism purposes.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is required to coordinate with the Ministry of Public Security on the specified management activities. The Ministry of Public Security must notify the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the specified violations, accidents, or incidents.

The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism coordinates with the Ministry of Public Security to organize and manage the relevant activities. The Ministry of Public Security is responsible for notifying the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism about specified violations, accidents, or other incidents.
The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism coordinates with the Ministry of Finance to organize and manage the relevant specified activities.

The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Public Security each build and manage databases that serve as sources of information collected under Article 12 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. They also coordinate on procedures for the temporary import and re-export of foreign motor vehicles, with the Ministry of Finance working with the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Public Security coordinating with the Ministry of Finance.
Foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles participate in traffic in Vietnam. The provision concerns these drivers and their participation in Vietnamese traffic.

The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs are responsible for coordinating with each other in organizing and managing the specified activities. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism works with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on their organization and management, while the Ministry of Foreign Affairs coordinates with the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism on the related management activities.

The Ministry of National Defence is a government institution named in a Vietnamese regulation. In Vietnam, it carries out border-control and related administrative duties under the decree and participates in procedures for foreign motor vehicles brought into the country.

The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism is identified in a Vietnamese regulation as a government institution with responsibilities related to foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam. Its stated role includes providing guidance on foreign motor vehicles participating in traffic and matters concerning road travel in Vietnam.

The Vietnamese International Travel Service Enterprises may use the Ministry of Public Security Public Service Portal to submit their application dossiers and required notices of changes to routes, itineraries, or departure times.
Traffic accidents involving foreign drivers in Vietnam refer to road accidents in Vietnam involving foreign nationals who are driving foreign motor vehicles.
Article 37, titled “Transitional Provisions,” is part of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. It sets out the decree’s transitional provisions.

The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism coordinates with the Ministry of Transport to organize and manage relevant activities. The Ministry of Transport also coordinates with the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism on management activities.

The Ministry of Public Security is responsible for notifying the relevant Representative Offices of Intergovernmental International Organizations in Vietnam about the specified violations, accidents, or incidents. It is required to provide these offices with notice of such events.
Legal violations by foreign drivers in Vietnam concern foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles in traffic within Vietnam.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP assigns the MINISTRY OF CULTURE, SPORTS AND TOURISM responsibilities under Article 36 for coordinating the organization and management of specified activities. Article 36, Clause 2, further sets out the ministry’s responsibilities.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is required to coordinate with the Ministry of Finance on the specified management activities.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is required to coordinate with the Ministry of National Defense on the specified management activities.

The MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS is a government institution named in Vietnamese regulation. It is also identified as a partner in managing activities involving foreign nationals and vehicles brought into VIETNAM.
FOREIGN MOTOR VEHICLE INCIDENTS are incidents involving foreign motor vehicles participating in traffic in VIETNAM.

The decree assigns related responsibilities to the Ministry of Construction and the Ministry of Public Security. The Ministry of Construction is required to coordinate with the Ministry of Public Security on specified management activities, while the Ministry of Public Security must notify the Ministry of Construction about specified incidents. The decree also identifies both ministries’ databases as sources for gathering road-traffic and vehicle-related information.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is required to coordinate with foreign representative agencies in Vietnam to organize and manage the covered activities and carry out the specified management activities.

The **Licensing Authority** uses the **National Public Service Portal** to exchange applications and processing notices with applicant agencies and organizations. It may send notices about applications or deficient submissions to an agency’s or organization’s account on the portal.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP assigns the MINISTRY OF CONSTRUCTION several responsibilities relating to road-traffic data and management. Under Article 10, Clause 3, the Ministry is responsible for building and managing specified specialized databases. Article 12 identifies information from a driver-training and certificate database managed by the Ministry as a source for data collection, while the decree also provides for road-traffic database information to be collected through a connection with the Ministry’s database.

Under Article 27, journey-monitoring data is to be connected and shared with the MINISTRY OF CONSTRUCTION for public-safety, enforcement, and road-transport management purposes. Article 36 assigns the Ministry a coordination responsibility. The decree further states that vehicle classification and safety and environmental certification are governed by regulations issued by the Minister of Construction.
The ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY DATABASE contains information about TRANSPORT BUSINESS UNITS and the vehicle badges associated with them.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP identifies the MINISTRY OF FINANCE as a coordination partner in organizing and managing the activities specified in the decree. Article 12 also lists the customs information database, built and managed by the MINISTRY OF FINANCE, as a source of collected information.

The Ministry of Construction’s responsibility for the specified databases does not include data concerning the police forces. In particular, the decree’s database responsibilities for driver training and legal-knowledge certificates exclude police-force data, as do the Ministry’s responsibilities for data on police-force vehicle inspections, driver training, and certificates.
The Ministry of Construction and the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism are required to coordinate with each other in organizing and managing the specified activities.

DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP assigns the MINISTRY OF CONSTRUCTION responsibility for building and managing specified specialized databases. It also designates the Ministry as a coordination partner in organizing and managing the specified activities. Relevant vehicle and road-traffic information is to be collected through connections to the Ministry of Construction’s database.

The Ministries and Sectors connect to and share information with the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database. They agree on the detailed list of data fields, based on the information specified in Article 11 of the decree.

The National Identification Application is a channel through which applications and processing notices are exchanged with the Licensing Authority. The Licensing Authority may use the application to send notices about deficient, incomplete, or ineligible submissions to an agency or organization’s account.
Under the NEW PERMIT ISSUANCE PROCEDURE, the LICENSING AUTHORITY reviews applications and issues new permits within one working day after receiving a complete application.

The Ministry of Construction’s responsibility for the specified databases does not include information concerning the military forces. This exclusion covers military-force vehicle inspections, driver training, and related certificates, including certificates of legal knowledge.
The Licensing Authority issues permits to agencies and organizations using priority vehicles and reissues permits to those agencies and organizations.
The **LICENSING AUTHORITY** is responsible for **APPLICATION RECEIPT AND REVIEW**, including receiving and checking permit applications and their supporting documents.

The **NEW PERMIT ISSUANCE PROCEDURE** sets out how **AGENCIES AND ORGANIZATIONS USING PRIORITY VEHICLES** can obtain new permits. These agencies and organizations submit applications for permits under the procedure.

The National Public Service Portal is an online channel through which applicants may submit applications, dossiers, and follow-up documents addressed to the competent authority, including the Traffic Police Department. It is one of the permitted channels for submitting applications to the Traffic Police Department.
APPLICANT AGENCY OR ORGANIZATION may receive application-related notices in its account on the NATIONAL PUBLIC SERVICE PORTAL.

The APPLICANT AGENCY OR ORGANIZATION may receive application-related notices through the NATIONAL IDENTIFICATION APPLICATION, which can deliver those notices to the agency’s or organization’s account.

DECREE NO. 151/2024/ND-CP sets out the permitting procedure that applies when an EMERGENCY SITUATION arises. It also provides that a permit for a priority vehicle’s signal devices expires when the emergency situation for which the vehicle was assigned duties ends.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP identifies the NATIONAL PUBLIC SERVICE PORTAL as an online channel for submitting an application dossier and its required documents. It also provides that notices concerning ineligible applications may be sent to the applicant’s account on the portal.

The National Identification Application is a digital, permitted channel for submitting applications and dossiers to the Traffic Police Department, including follow-up documents addressed to the competent authority.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP assigns the Traffic Police Department, under the Ministry of Public Security, authority over permits for signal devices on the specified priority vehicles (Article 23). Under Article 33, applicants must submit or send their application dossier to the Traffic Police Department.

NGHỊ ĐỊNH 151/2024/NĐ-CP governs vehicle-related activities and administrative procedures in VIỆT NAM. It also establishes requirements for vehicles entering and participating in traffic in the country.
ỨNG DỤNG ĐỊNH DANH QUỐC GIA là một trong các kênh trực tuyến để gửi hoặc nộp hồ sơ đến CỤC CẢNH SÁT GIAO THÔNG.

DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP recognizes the National Identification Application as an online channel through which an applicant may submit an application dossier and required documents. It also provides that notices concerning an ineligible application may be sent to the applicant’s account on the National Identification Application.

DECREE 236/2026/NĐ-CP provides that the NATIONAL IDENTIFICATION APPLICATION may be used to submit applications under the permit procedures it regulates and to receive notices about the processing of those applications.

DECREE 236/2026/NĐ-CP governs the participation of foreign motor vehicles—including right-hand-drive cars—in traffic in VIETNAM. It also sets provisions concerning transport businesses in the context of traffic in VIETNAM.

DECREE 236/2026/NĐ-CP sets requirements for priority signal devices installed on vehicles used by the MILITARY FORCES while performing emergency duties. Its transitional provisions also address permits for signal devices already issued for the military forces’ priority vehicles.
Vietnamese international travel service businesses may organize foreign visitors to bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism.

CÔNG AN CÁC ĐƠN VỊ, ĐỊA PHƯƠNG (police units and local authorities) submit their reports to the Ministry of Public Security through CỤC CẢNH SÁT GIAO THÔNG (the Traffic Police Department).
